- **`observedPairs`**: `Map<emojiId, CatalogEmojiInfo>` — emoji observed inline in incoming message content (`extractEmojiObservations`). NOT sendable; not returned by `getSendableEmoji`. Exists so the normalizer can render `:name:` for emoji not yet in the catalog.

**`getSendableEmoji(guildId?)`**: returns guild emoji (for the given guild, alphabetically) followed by app emoji (alphabetically). Observed pairs are excluded.

**`resolve(token, guildId?)`**: parses the token as either a raw Unicode emoji glyph or a `:shortcode:` string. Unicode glyphs pass through directly (`kind: "unicode"`). `:shortcode:` is matched first against the target guild's emoji (priority), then against app emoji; returns `{ kind: "custom", id, name, animated }` on match, `null` on miss. Observed pairs are not resolvable (not sendable).

**`renderShortcodes(body, guildId?)`**: rewrites every `:name:` token (2–32 `[A-Za-z0-9_]` chars) that `resolve` maps to a custom emoji into Discord markup; unresolvable names (including unicode aliases like `:smile:`) pass through. Code spans/fences and tokens preceded by a word character or `<` (timestamps, existing markup) are skipped. Used on the outbound body by `send` and `editMessage`.

**`nearMatches(query, guildId?)`**: substring search over sendable emoji names; returns up to 5 `:shortcode:` strings.

**Static helpers**: `EmojiCatalog.formatForApi(id, name)` → `"name:id"` (Discord API reaction emoji format); `EmojiCatalog.normalizedKey(id)` → `"discord:<id>"` (normalized key stored in the reactions table).

**Gateway lifecycle**: the `guildEmojisUpdate` listener signature is `(guild, _oldEmojis, newEmojis)` per discord.js v14 (the guild is always the first argument). `guildCreate` loads emoji for newly joined guilds. `guildDelete` calls `clearGuildEmoji` so stale entries don't persist.

### Reaction routing

Four gateway events map to `host.onReaction` and `host.onBulkReactionClear`:

| Gateway event | Handler | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `messageReactionAdd` | `handleReactionAdd` | `host.onReaction` with `action: "add"` |
| `messageReactionRemove` | `handleReactionRemove` | `host.onReaction` with `action: "remove"` |
| `messageReactionRemoveAll` | inline | `host.onBulkReactionClear` with no `normalizedKey` |
| `messageReactionRemoveEmoji` | inline | `host.onBulkReactionClear` with `normalizedKey` |

All four are gated on `isAllowedByGuild(runtime, guildId)` before dispatch.

**`isAllowedByGuild(runtime, guildId)`**: returns `true` if `runtime.allowedGuilds` is unset (allow all), the `guildId` is in `allowedGuilds`, or `guildId` is `null` (DM — allowed when `dmEnabled`).

**Reaction primary key**: `discord:<messageId>:<normalizedKey>:<userId>`, where `normalizedKey` for custom emoji is `discord:<emojiId>` and for unicode is the emoji glyph string. This PK is deterministic: the same add and remove events for the same (message, emoji, user) tuple produce the same key, so the remove tombstones the add row in the reactions table.

**`handleReactionAdd`** constructs the PK, builds the `timelineKey` from `reaction.message.channelId` + `channelType` + optional `parentId` (for threads), and calls `host.onReaction` with `action: "add"`, `kind` (`"unicode"` or `"custom"`), `display` (glyph or `:name:`), `shortcode` (for custom), `normalizedKey`, `targetEventId`, and `reactedAtMs`.

**`handleReactionRemove`** reconstructs the same PK (using the same `buildReactionNormalizedKey` helper) and calls `host.onReaction` with `action: "remove"` and no `kind`/`display`/`targetEventId` (tombstone shape).

### DiscordChannelClient (`src/discord/channel-client.ts`)

`DiscordChannelClient` implements the `ChannelClient` interface using discord.js REST through the account's `Client.rest`.

| Method | Notes |
|---|---|
| `react(externalId, emoji)` | `EmojiCatalog.resolve()` then `PUT /channels/{id}/messages/{msgId}/reactions/{emoji}/@me`. Unicode glyphs are URL-encoded; custom emoji use `name:id` format. |
| `unreact(externalId, emoji)` | `DELETE /channels/{id}/messages/{msgId}/reactions/{emoji}/@me` |
| `listReactions(externalId, limit?)` | Fetches the message to get the reaction array; then for each emoji fetches users via `GET /reactions/{emoji}`. Returns `ReactionListing` with per-emoji `{ display, users }` entries. |
| `editMessage(externalId, body)` | `PATCH /channels/{id}/messages/{msgId}` |
| `deleteMessage(externalId)` | `DELETE /channels/{id}/messages/{msgId}` |
| `readMessages(req)` | Delegates to an internal `DiscordHistoryClient` instance |
| `readMessage(externalId)` | `GET /channels/{id}/messages/{msgId}` → `HistorySummary` |
| `memberInfo(userId)` | Guild member cache lookup; REST `GET /guilds/{id}/members/{userId}` on miss (only if `memberIntentEnabled`) |
| `members()` | REST `GET /guilds/{id}/members` with pagination (`limit=1000`, `after` cursor); only present iff `memberIntentEnabled` |
| `channelInfo()` | Cache hit → `channelInfoFromCached`; cache miss → `GET /channels/{id}`, result cached. Returns `ChannelInfo` with `id`, `displayName`, `isDirect: false` (always false for guild channels), `topic`, `threadCount` |
| `pins()` | `GET /channels/{id}/pins` |
| `pinMessage / unpinMessage` | `PUT / DELETE /channels/{id}/pins/{msgId}` |
| `emojiList(limit?)` | `EmojiCatalog.getSendableEmoji(guildId)` → up to `limit` entries as `EmojiEntry[]` |
| `createPoll(req)` | `POST /channels/{id}/messages` with `poll: { question, answers, duration, allow_multiselect }` Discord object |

`URLSearchParams` objects are used for all REST `query` parameters (discord.js v14 requires `URLSearchParams`, not a plain object).

### DiscordHistoryClient (`src/discord/history-client.ts`)

`DiscordHistoryClient` implements both `HistoryClient` and `BackfillReadClient`. It uses before-snowflake backward pagination via `GET /channels/{id}/messages`. A client built for a thread channel (`history()` passes the thread id) stamps every summary with `threadRootExternalId` = the thread id, mirroring the live normalizer, so the backfill classifiers route them to the `…:thread:<id>` key. Summaries never set `edited` — that flag marks a *replacement event* (Matrix `m.replace`), which the classifiers apply as an edit or drop when it names no target; an edited Discord message is simply returned with its current content. A 403/404 from the endpoint is thrown as `HistoryUnavailableError` (§7c release path).

**`readMessages(req)`**: accepts `req.limit` (1–100, clamped), `req.before` (explicit snowflake), and `req.cursor` (previous page cursor — also a snowflake). `before` takes priority over `cursor`. Response messages arrive newest-first; the oldest snowflake becomes `nextCursor`. Returns `HistoryPageResult` with `messages` (as `HistorySummary[]`) and `nextCursor`.

**Structural compatibility**: `DiscordHistoryClient` satisfies `BackfillReadClient` because `readMessages` shares the same signature as `BackfillReadClient.readMessages`. This lets `runInitialBackfill` in `app.ts` use the history client directly without a wrapper (non-Matrix providers use `provider.history?.(target)` as the read client; Matrix uses `makeBackfillReadClient`).

### Voice message send (`src/discord/voice-message.ts`)

When the outbound message has an attachment with `asVoice = true` and a `localPath`, `send()` enters the voice message path.

**`encodeVoiceMessage(inputPath)`** (two ffmpeg passes):
1. Pass 1 — `ffmpeg -i input -vn -c:a libopus output.ogg` (transcode to ogg/opus)
2. Pass 2 — `ffmpeg -i input -vn -ar 48000 -ac 1 -f s16le pcmfile` (extract s16le PCM for waveform)

**`computeWaveform(pcmBytes, targetSamples)`**: divides the s16le PCM into `min(targetSamples, totalSamples, 256)` chunks, computes the peak absolute amplitude of each chunk (interpreting 16-bit LE signed samples), normalizes all peaks relative to the global maximum (0 → 0, max → 255), and returns a `Buffer` of `Uint8` values. `WAVEFORM_SAMPLE_COUNT = 256` is the Discord-enforced maximum.

The provider sends the ogg file as a multipart POST using the raw REST client (discord.js attachment builder does not expose `duration_secs`/`waveform`). The payload sets `flags: MessageFlags.IsVoiceMessage` and includes `duration_secs` and `waveform` (base64-encoded waveform buffer) on the attachment object. After send, `cleanupVoiceFile` removes the temp ogg file.

### `set_profile` (`setProfile` method)

`setProfile(accountId, opts)` implements the `IChatProvider.setProfile` contract for Discord:

- **Avatar**: `PATCH /users/@me` with `avatar` as a `data:<contentType>;base64,<data>` URI. Returns the updated CDN URL.
- **Display name (per-guild nick)**: `PATCH /guilds/{guildId}/members/@me` with `{ nick }` for each allowed guild the account is in. Empty string clears the nick. Non-fatal per-guild (some guilds may block nick changes). Global username rename is deliberately excluded (globally unique, rate-limited at ~2/hr, collision risk).

### Identity and metadata upserts

**`upsertUserIdentity`** is called from two sites:

1. `handleMessageCreate` — after every inbound message, calls `callbacks.upsertUserIdentity({ provider: "discord", userId: author.id, username: author.username, displayName: <nick or globalName or username>, observedAt: message.createdTimestamp })`. The `displayName` is the most-resolved visible name: nick (from guild member cache) → `globalName` → `username`.
2. `guildMemberUpdate` listener (gated on `memberIntentEnabled`) — calls `callbacks.upsertUserIdentity` when a member's display name or username changes, using the updated `GuildMember` data.

**`setChannelMetadata`** is called from `handleMessageCreate` with `{ displayName, serverId?, serverName? }`. The `displayName` is built by `buildChannelDisplayName(message)`: `#channel-name (Guild Name)` for guild text channels, `#<channelId>` for unknown/DM channels. `serverId = message.guildId ?? undefined`; `serverName = message.guild?.name ?? undefined`. The `room_metadata` table (`server_id`, `server_name` columns — schema v6) stores the guild scope so `serverIdsFor(timelineKey)` in `app.ts` can return the Discord guild id for limits enforcement.

### Self-id disposition

Discord self-ids (the bot's own snowflake) are only known after the `ready` event fires asynchronously. To make them available to the `UserLimitEngine` and backfill coordinator at call time (not just at construction time):

- `app.ts` declares a mutable `botSelfIdsForLimits: Set<string>` (pre-seeded with Matrix `user_id` values) and `gapBackfetchSelfIds: Map<string, string>` (pre-seeded with Matrix account self-ids) **before** the providers IIFE.
- The `onSelfResolved(accountId, selfId)` callback mutates both containers: `botSelfIdsForLimits.add(selfId)` and `gapBackfetchSelfIds.set(accountId, selfId)`.
- `UserLimitEngine` is constructed with `selfUserIds: botSelfIdsForLimits`; it reads the Set by reference at each `isUserIdentity` call, so READY-time additions are visible without restart.
- `runInitialBackfill` reads `gapBackfetchSelfIds.get(accountId)` at backfill time; READY fires before the first `activating` transition, so the self-id is always available when needed.

## 6d. IRC Provider

`src/irc/` implements the IRC provider using the `irc-framework` v4 library. It splits into a pure normalizer module (`normalizer.ts`), the live provider class (`provider.ts`), a per-channel roster tracker (`roster-tracker.ts`), a nick-to-account tracker (`account-tracker.ts`), and a `ChannelClient` implementation (`channel-client.ts`).

### IRCv3 capability policy

**Required floor** (hard error when absent): the provider requires `server-time`, `message-tags`, and `echo-message` — all three must appear in the server's CAP LS response. `sasl` is additionally required whenever `sasl_user` + `sasl_password` are configured. On a missing required cap, the account emits a structured error naming the cap and the server host (`"irc account "<key>": server <host> does not advertise required capability "<cap>" — mikuswarm requires a modern IRCv3 server (Solanum, InspIRCd, UnrealIRCd, Ergo or equivalent)"`) and then `QUIT`s. The `capFailed` flag suppresses repeated error logging on auto-reconnect attempts; the account is permanently unusable until the process restarts with a cap-capable server.

If a required cap is **withdrawn mid-connection** (`CAP DEL`), the provider logs an error, clears `registered`, and calls `QUIT` with `capDelReconnect = true`. The library's `close` event then fires (because `QUIT` sets `requested_disconnect = true`, preventing the library's own auto-reconnect) and the provider's `close` handler explicitly calls `client.connect()` after a 1 s delay — implementing a clean reconnect loop that repeats cap validation on the fresh connection.

**Opportunistic caps** (auto-detected, never config knobs): `msgid`, `labeled-response`, `batch`, `account-tag`, `account-notify`, `extended-join`, `away-notify`, `chghost`, `setname`. These are requested unconditionally; the server grants only the ones it advertises. Their presence silently improves internal fidelity (better message ids, identity resolution, echo correlation, roster freshness) but never changes the tool-visible capability surface.

### Key grammar

| Context | Timeline key |
|---|---|
| Channel | `irc:<accountId>:room:<casemapped_channel_name>` |
| DM (query) | `irc:<accountId>:dm:<networkId>/<identity>` |

Channel names are casemapped for key stability using the network's `CASEMAPPING` ISUPPORT token (default `rfc1459`). DM keys use the network-scoped identity (see **Identity ladder** below) — e.g. `irc:myaccount:dm:libera.chat/alice` — so a user who DMs while unauthenticated gets a separate timeline from their authenticated sessions (the accepted consequence) and users on different networks with the same nick are always distinct.

Event id: `irc:<accountId>:<externalId>:<nanoid8>`. `externalId` is the `msgid` tag value when the server assigns one (preferred) or a synthetic id — `syn:<serverTimeMs>:<senderNick>:<counter>` — where the counter is a per-account monotonic integer. Synthetic ids serve dedup and echo-merge; no stable referenceability is required.

### Identity ladder

Per-message identity is resolved deterministically in three rungs, then **network-scoped**:

1. **Per-message `account` tag** (wins unconditionally when present and non-empty) — the sender's services account name from the `account-tag` cap. Never `"*"` on PRIVMSG (that form only appears on `ACCOUNT` messages; handled defensively).
2. **Tracked state** (`AccountTracker`) — populated by `extended-join` (account field in JOIN), `account-notify` (ACCOUNT messages), per-message `account` tag (opportunistic refresh), and WHOX WHO responses on self-join.
3. **Casemapped nick** — final fallback when no account information is available.

`SenderInfo.id` = `<networkId>/<ladderResult>` — network-scoped via `scopeIrcId(networkId, bareId)` (`src/irc/normalizer.ts`). `networkId` is the `NETWORK` ISUPPORT token lowercased when advertised, else the configured host lowercased; it is frozen on the first `server options` event (RPL_ISUPPORT / 005) so that ids are never minted before the name is final. `SenderInfo.username` is always the current nick (the display identity). The bot's own identity (`SelfIdentity.id`) follows the same scoping.

`ownsUserId` requires the `/` separator — bare nicks are rejected, making IRC ids disjoint from Matrix (`@`-prefixed) and Discord (all-digit) ids. Cross-network collision between two networks sharing a services account name is impossible: `libera.chat/alice` and `efnet/alice` are distinct ids in `user_identities` and independent budget aggregates.

### Capabilities

| Capability | Value |
|---|---|
| `maxMessageChars` | 400 (static conservative budget; actual per-send budget is computed from the bot's real hostmask — see "Send") |
| `maxAttachmentsPerMessage` | 0 |
| `formatting` | `"plain"` |
| `typing` | `true` (via `TAGMSG +typing=active/done`) |
| `reactions` | `false` |
| `edits` | `false` |
| `deletes` | `false` |
| `pins` | `false` |
| `pollCreate` | `false` |
| `pollVote` | `false` |
| `voiceMessages` | `false` |
| `threads` | `false` |
| `history` | `false` (initial-activation backfill is skipped; `chathistory` is a deferred follow-up) |
| `encrypted` | `false` |
| `linkPreviews` | `"none"` |
| `singleAttachmentPerMessage` | `false` |
| `membershipRoster` | `true` (backed by `RosterTracker`) |
| `mediaUpload` | `false` |

IRC has no attachment or media capability, but `enrichment()` still returns a
capabilities object (attachment download rejects, reply-context summary is
`null`, `memberInfo` resolves display nicks from the roster) with
`resolveLinkPreviews` omitted — registering IRC accounts with the enrichment
pool so link previews run through the framework-level `DirectLinkPreviewClient`
fallback (and body-URL stages like YouTube apply), exactly as Discord uses it
for non-embedded links.

### Inbound pipeline

Events handled: `privmsg` (PRIVMSG + CTCP ACTION via the library's `action` event), `notice`, `cap del`, `nick`, `user updated` (CHGHOST/SETNAME), `join` (+ WHOX WHO on self-join), `userlist` (RPL_ENDOFNAMES), `part`, `kick`, `topic`, `away`, `back`, `account`, `quit`, `socket close`, `close`, `socket error`.

**PRIVMSG / ACTION**: inbound messages from other users are normalized via `normalizeIrcMessage()` — a pure function with no live client references — and routed through `applyTriggerHoldOrEmit()`. `account` tag (if present) is used to refresh `AccountTracker` before normalization so the identity ladder reads the freshest state. DMs to a disabled (`dm_enabled = false`) account are dropped.

**NOTICE**: channel NOTICEs are ingested (trigger forced to `undefined`). Query NOTICEs (DMs) are dropped entirely. This is the only inbound suppression that is not a config option.

**Control code stripping**: mIRC color codes (`\x03`, `\x04` hex-color), bold/italic/underline/strikethrough/monospace/reverse/reset control characters are stripped from every inbound body at normalization time. `CTCP ACTION` bodies are rendered as `* nick action text`.

**Trigger detection**: `dm` for any query message; `mention` for a channel message that matches the bot's nick (recognized as a `nick: text` / `nick, text` / `nick text` addressing prefix at line start — the space separator overlaps with the bare-nick form — OR a bare-nick word-boundary occurrence anywhere in the message, casemapped per the network's CASEMAPPING). Notices never trigger.

**Trigger hold** (`applyTriggerHoldOrEmit`): the Matrix and Discord hold, same semantics (§6 "Trigger hold"). With `trigger_hold_ms` (optional config field) above 0, every message is emitted at once without its trigger, so it is stored as it arrives; a trigger opens a hold keyed by timeline **and sender**, every further message of that sender in that timeline joins the held trigger's `groupedEventIds` (a trigger-bearing one resets the timer, capped at `4 × trigger_hold_ms` from the hold's `holdStartedAt`; a non-triggering one rides the timer), and the flush delivers the trigger once, rooted on the hold's first message, with `holdEndedAt`. Another sender's trigger opens its own hold (before, the hold was keyed by timeline and kept only the newest trigger, so earlier held messages were never stored). IRC has no message deletions (`capabilities.deletes = false`), so nothing ever leaves a held group.

### Send and byte-accurate chunking

`send(target, message)` computes the actual PRIVMSG byte budget from the bot's known hostmask (`nick!user@host`): `budget = 498 - byteLen(hostmask) - byteLen(ircTarget)` (the 512-byte wire limit minus CRLF/prefix/command/target overhead), with a minimum of 50 bytes and a fallback to the static 400-byte budget before the hostmask is learned.

`chunkIrcMessage(text, maxBytes)` splits on embedded newlines first (matching the library's own newline handling — without this, a single `PendingEcho` for a multi-line body would never match the N separate echoes and every multi-line send would time out at 5 s then fabricate a receipt). Each line is then split into chunks ≤ `maxBytes` UTF-8 bytes using UTF-8-code-point iteration with whitespace-preferring split (preferring the last space in the latter half of the window). Empty / whitespace-only segments are skipped.

### Echo-merge

`echo-message` is a required cap. Every outbound PRIVMSG is echoed back by the server, and the provider merges the echo to learn the server-assigned `msgid` (preferred when `msgid` cap is enabled).

Two merge strategies depending on available caps:

- **`labeled-response` + `batch` present**: each chunk is sent with a `label` tag (`nanoid(12)`); the server echoes the PRIVMSG inside a `BATCH` tagged with that label. The provider looks up the label in `pendingByLabel` to resolve the corresponding echo promise.
- **`labeled-response` absent**: FIFO queue per target (`echoQueues`). IRC guarantees ordered per-target delivery, so the first pending entry for a (target, body) pair is the matching echo. After 5 s (`ECHO_TIMEOUT_MS`) without an echo, the pending promise resolves with the synthetic id and the entry is cleaned up.

The echo event is always delivered to `host.onEvent` with `isSelf: true` for timeline storage, regardless of how the external id was resolved.

### RosterTracker and AccountTracker

**`RosterTracker`** (`src/irc/roster-tracker.ts`) tracks per-channel membership. It is initialised from `userlist` (RPL_ENDOFNAMES) and kept current by `join`, `part`, `quit`, `nick`, `kick`, `away`, and `back` events. Cleared on `socket close` so stale membership from before a disconnect never bleeds into the reconnected session. Internally it stores `RosterEntry { nick, modes, away }` keyed by casemapped nick; the `members()` method on `IrcChannelClient` exposes the roster as `SenderInfo[]` (`{ id, username, isSelf }`, with the identity-ladder result as `id`).

**`AccountTracker`** (`src/irc/account-tracker.ts`) maps casemapped nicks to services account names. Updated by `extended-join` (per-JOIN account field), `account-notify` (ACCOUNT messages), per-message `account` tag (opportunistic refresh), and WHOX bulk responses on self-join. QUIT events prune the entry; PART does not (the user may still be in other served channels). Cleared on `socket close`.

### IrcChannelClient

`IrcChannelClient` (`src/irc/channel-client.ts`) implements `ChannelClient`. Unsupported operations (`react`, `unreact`, `listReactions`, `editMessage`, `deleteMessage`, `pins`, `pinMessage`, `unpinMessage`) throw immediately with `"IRC does not support <op>"` — the session tool-gate on `ProviderCapabilities` flags means these methods are never called from normal tool paths. `emojiList()` returns an empty array (IRC has no custom emoji concept). `readMessages()` returns an empty result (history cap is `false`).

Three live operations:

- **`members()`** — delegates to `membersFn` (the roster-backed closure over `RosterTracker.getMembers()` enriched with `AccountTracker`). Each entry's `id` is network-scoped: `<networkId>/<ladderResult>` (account name when known, casemapped nick otherwise). Absent for DMs.
- **`memberInfo(id)`** — delegates to `memberInfoFn`: strips the `<networkId>/` prefix from the input (returns `undefined` for mismatched network prefix), resolves the nick for the bare id (account→nick reverse lookup via `RosterTracker.findNickByAccount()` first, then treating the bare id as a nick directly), then issues WHOIS (10 s timeout; resolves `undefined` on timeout or socket drop). Returns `{ userId: <networkId>/<resolvedBareId>, displayName, isSelf, isDirect }`.
- **`channelInfo()`** — delegates to `channelInfoFn`: returns tracked topic and member count from `RosterTracker`. Label is `"<channelName> (<networkName>)"` for channels, `"<nick> (<networkName> DM)"` for DMs. `serverName` is set to `rt.networkName`.

### IrcProviderCallbacks

Two callbacks injected at construction, following the same pattern as `DiscordProviderCallbacks`:

- **`upsertUserIdentity(input)`** — called from the NICK event handler to record the old nick as an alias under the stable identity key (account name when known, else old casemapped nick). Per-message upserts are handled by the generic ingest path in `app.ts`.
- **`setChannelMetadata(timelineKey, meta)`** — called on every inbound channel PRIVMSG/ACTION/NOTICE to upsert `display_name`, `server_id`, and `server_name` into `room_metadata`. `displayName = channelName` (the `#channel` string); `serverId = rt.networkName`; `serverName = rt.networkName`. Used by `serverIdsFor(timelineKey)` to return the network identity for server-scoped per-user-limit partitioning (`{server_id}` template variable). Fire-and-forget; errors are swallowed.

### Config block reference

```
[irc]
enabled         = true
trigger_hold_ms = 0                        # optional; debounce ms (same semantics as matrix.trigger_hold_ms)

[irc.accounts.<key>]
host            = "irc.example.org"        # required; server hostname or IP
port            = 6697                     # optional; defaults to 6697 (TLS) or 6667 (plaintext)
tls             = true                     # optional; defaults to true when port is 6697 or absent
nick            = "botname"               # required; requested nick
username        = "botname"               # optional; IRC username (ident); defaults to nick
realname        = "botname"               # optional; gecos / real name; defaults to nick
sasl_user       = "..."                   # optional; SASL PLAIN username; when set with sasl_password, sasl cap is required
sasl_password   = "..."                   # optional; SASL PLAIN password (redacted in logs)
server_password = "..."                   # optional; PASS command password (redacted in logs)
channels        = ["#general", "#other"]  # optional; channels to join and rejoin on reconnect
dm_enabled      = true                    # optional; accept private messages (queries) from users; default true
agent           = "alice"                 # optional; which [agents.*] block this account belongs to (§4c)
```

The account key (the `<key>` in `[irc.accounts.<key>]`) must not contain `:` (breaks `parseTimelineKey`) and must not contain path-unsafe characters in agents mode.

### Terminology map

| IRC concept | MikuSwarm field |
|---|---|
| Nick | `SenderInfo.username` (mutable display identity) |
| Services account name | bare ladder result (rung 1/2); scoped → `<networkId>/<account>` in `SenderInfo.id` |
| Casemapped nick | bare ladder result (rung 3); scoped → `<networkId>/<casemappedNick>` in `SenderInfo.id` |
| `NETWORK` ISUPPORT token | `rt.networkName` (the `networkId` scope prefix) / `server_id` in `room_metadata` |
| Network-scoped user id | `<networkId>/<ladderResult>` (e.g. `libera.chat/alice`) — format of every `SenderInfo.id` |
| Channel (e.g. `#general`) | timeline key kind `"room"` |
| Query (DM) | timeline key kind `"dm"` |
| PRIVMSG msgid tag | `externalId` (preferred over synthetic) |
| CTCP ACTION | body prefix `* nick ` |

---

## 7. Timeline

### Core concept

The timeline is a continuously-growing, append-only record of everything that happens in a chat context. It exists independently of agent sessions. It is the single source of truth for all conversation history.

This architecture explicitly separates **observing** (timeline ingests all messages continuously) from **participating** (agent sessions are spawned episodically by triggers).

### Timeline keys

`timelineKey` is a provider-generic string used as the universal FK across ~20 tables. Its shape is a documented, parseable grammar (`src/storage/timeline-key.ts`):

```
<provider>:<accountId>:<kind>:<channelId>[:thread:<threadId>]
  provider   [a-z0-9-]+      no colon (e.g. "matrix")
  accountId  operator-chosen config key, no colon
  kind       "room" | "dm"
  channelId  provider-native id; MAY contain colons (Matrix room ids do)
  threadId   provider-native id (no colons in practice)
```

Matrix keys are exactly this shape — no existing row needs to change:

| Context | Format |
|---------|--------|
| Room | `matrix:{accountId}:room:{roomId}` |
| DM | `matrix:{accountId}:dm:{roomId}` |
| Thread | `matrix:{accountId}:room:{roomId}:thread:{threadRootId}` |

Because `channelId` may contain colons (Matrix room ids are `!local:server`), the `:thread:` suffix is detected from the **end** (last occurrence of `:thread:` in the remainder after the `kind:` segment). Kind is always the 3rd colon-delimited segment from the start.

**Shared parser** — `src/storage/timeline-key.ts` is the single grammar module and single source of truth. Public API:
- `parseTimelineKey(key)` → `ParsedTimelineKey | undefined` (returns `undefined` for malformed/absent keys)
- `buildTimelineKey(parts)` → `string` (inverse of `parseTimelineKey`; round-trips are identity)
- `channelIdFromTimelineKey(key)` → `string | undefined` (extracts the channel id; `undefined` for malformed/absent)
- `timelineKindOf(key)` → `"room" | "dm" | undefined`
- `roomIdFromTimelineKeyOpt` — deprecated alias of `channelIdFromTimelineKey`; kept for one release
- `threadKeyLikePattern(roomKey)` — SQLite `LIKE` pattern for `<roomKey>:thread:%`

All parse sites use these shared functions. No subsystem may parse the key with a local regex or `split(":")`. A present-but-malformed key logs `"timeline_key.malformed"` (structured JSON, consistent event name) rather than silently no-op-ing; absent/undefined keys keep their current behaviour (skip / return undefined).

DM detection uses `timelineKindOf(key) === "dm"`. The `isDmTimeline` router helper delegates to the same function. For inbound events produced by a normalizer, `InboundChatEvent.channelType` (`"group" | "dm" | "thread"`) is populated at ingest; routing code that has the full event prefers `channelType` and falls back to `timelineKindOf(key)` for stored keys.

### Storage

SQLite with WAL mode. Core tables:

- **`timeline_events`** — the event log. Each row stores denormalized columns (id, timeline_key, role, sender, body, timestamps) plus `event_json` (full `CanonicalChatEvent` serialized), `enrichment_status` (`inactive` | `pending` | `processing` | `complete` | `failed` | `skipped`), and `trigger_group_id` (event ID of the trigger that owns this group, or NULL). The `inactive` status marks events stored for a not-yet-triggered timeline (see section 7b — Channel Lifecycle); the enrichment and caption pools only claim `pending`/`processing` rows, so `inactive` events are stored cheaply but never processed until activation. It also has a generated column `is_undecryptable` (VIRTUAL, derived from `event_json`'s `undecryptable` field) for cheap UTD-row lookup by the re-decryption sweeper (see section 6a) and a `redecrypt_attempts` integer (default 0) that counts failed re-decryption probes — the sweeper's candidate query excludes rows at/above `MAX_REDECRYPT_ATTEMPTS` (and a `REDECRYPT_RETIRED` sentinel for permanently-unfetchable rows) so dead UTD rows leave rotation. A nullable `last_edit_timestamp` (issue #3) holds the `origin_server_ts` of the most recently applied edit (NULL = never edited); the edit-application paths use it to enforce latest-by-timestamp wins (an older incoming edit is a no-op). A deleted message carries its deletion marker in `event_json` (`deleted: { at, by? }`, §6 "Message edits"), like the `undecryptable` field; it has no column (lookups use `json_extract`). Indexed on `(timeline_key, timestamp, received_at, id)`, `(provider, external_id)`, `(enrichment_status, timestamp DESC)`, `(trigger_group_id)`, and a partial `(is_undecryptable, redecrypt_attempts, timestamp) where is_undecryptable = 1` (the attempts column is in the index so the give-up filter skips exhausted rows without touching the heap).
- **`timeline_compaction_state`** — per-timeline compaction cursors (`compact_start_event_id`, `rich_start_event_id`) plus channel-lifecycle columns: `timeline_state` (`inactive` | `activating` | `active` | `backfilling`, default `inactive`) and `backfill_fence_timestamp` (reserved for deferred operator backfill). A missing row means the timeline is implicitly `inactive`. See section 7b.
- **`pending_edits`** — edits (`m.replace`) that arrived/decrypted before their target message was stored, parked for replay by the append path (see section 6, "Edit-before-target replay"). Keyed by `(provider, target_external_id, timeline_key)` (the PK; `timeline_key`-scoped for the same multi-account reason as the edit lookup). Stores the resolved replacement `body` + `attachments_json` and the `edit_timestamp` (origin time, for latest-wins). Rows are deleted as soon as the target lands and the edit is applied.
- **`room_metadata`** — cached human room labels keyed by `timeline_key` (`display_name` + `resolved_at`). Populated by `RoomLabelCache` (see section 6, "Room-label resolution") so the observability console room list shows real room names instead of raw room ids; read by `listConsoleRooms`, which falls back to the `timeline_key` when no label has been resolved yet. `resolved_at` lets the cache expire stale labels (rooms can be renamed; 6-hour TTL). Also carries `server_id` (nullable) and `server_name` (nullable) — Discord guild scope and IRC network scope both use these columns, each populated by their provider's `setChannelMetadata` callback at ingest (Discord: guild id + guild name; IRC: network name from NETWORK ISUPPORT, else configured host); used by `serverIdsFor(timelineKey)` in `app.ts` to return the server-scope id for server-scoped budget limits.
- **`metadata`** — generic key-value store.
- **`timeline_counts`** — materialized per-timeline `event_count`, `last_event_at` (max event timestamp) and `session_count` behind the console rooms list, `WITHOUT ROWID`, PK `timeline_key`; kept exact by `tc_*` insert/delete/update triggers on `timeline_events` and `agent_sessions` (an event leaving a timeline re-derives `last_event_at` with one index seek) and rebuilt from the base tables at every open, like `pipeline_counts`. Both tables are written with plain INSERTs, so no REPLACE gap applies.
- **`pipeline_counts`** — materialized pipeline-monitor status counts, `WITHOUT ROWID`, PK `(pool, status, retrying, elig)`; trigger-maintained and rebuilt from the base tables at every open (see §11 "Count aggregate cost").
- **`reactions`** — the passive reaction store (§9f). One row per reaction event (PK = the reaction's own event id — `$eventId` for Matrix; `discord:<msgId>:<emojiKey>:<userId>` synthetic key for Discord), carrying the `timeline_key` locality hint, the target message's external id, sender, resolved `kind`/`display`/`shortcode`/`normalized_key`, timestamps, and a nullable `redacted_at` tombstone. The `timeline_key` column is returned in `DiscreteReactionRow` so the context builder can derive the provider for identity resolution (§6.5). Deliberately **not** part of the timeline — reactions are injected only at render time and must stay out of summarization, search, diary, and recap. No FK to `timeline_events`: the target is matched by the globally-unique event id (Matrix or synthetic Discord PK), not the internal row id. Partial index on `(target_event_id, reacted_at) where redacted_at is null`.
- **`refusal_events`**, **`contract_attempts`**, **`agent_session_branches`**: detected refusals, send-contract attempts and discarded redo branches (§8j "Storage"); **`behaviour_snapshots`**, **`behaviour_changes`**, **`model_behaviour_rollups`**, **`model_behaviour_task_rollups`**, **`model_behaviour_dirty_hours`**: model behaviour statistics (§8k); **`session_audits`**: the offline audit worker's rows (§9i).
- **`user_identities`** / **`user_identity_aliases`** — the user identity store (see §6b). `user_identities` is `WITHOUT ROWID`, PK `(provider, user_id)`, current `username` + `display_name`. `user_identity_aliases` holds prior usernames, bounded at `USER_IDENTITY_ALIAS_BOUND = 16` per user.

Enrichment tables (see section 7a):

- **`reply_contexts`** — resolved reply snapshots, one per event (keyed by the replying event's ID)
- **`media_assets`** — all downloaded media: attachments, reply attachments, link preview media, linked media in body text. Tracks download status, caption status, detected content (character cards), workspace-relative file paths, and `content_hash TEXT` (nullable sha256 hex — set by the enrichment write path when the content-addressed attachment store is enabled, NULL otherwise; see §7a "Content-addressed attachment store").
- **`link_previews`** — fetched link preview metadata (title, description, site name, source kind), plus the nullable `payload_json` structured payload for `source_kind = 'fx_twitter'` rows (§7a "X.com enrichment via FxTwitter") and `source_kind = 'youtube'` rows (§7e "YouTube Enrichment"). Media associated with previews lives in `media_assets` with a `link_preview_id` FK.

### Single-writer invariant

**All writes go through a single-writer microtask queue.** No component writes to SQLite directly. Write jobs are pushed onto an array and drained atomically via `queueMicrotask()`. This eliminates contention and `SQLITE_BUSY` errors entirely. Reads execute synchronously outside the queue (WAL allows concurrent readers) — which also means a slow read blocks the event loop for its full duration, so every read path is held to a bounded index walk (§11 "Count aggregate cost" and the paragraph after it). `Storage.open()` sets `journal_mode = WAL`, `foreign_keys = ON`, `busy_timeout = 5000`, `cache_size` (`[storage].cache_size_mb`, default 64 MiB) and optionally `mmap_size` (`[storage].mmap_size_mb`, default off). Composite operations use `readAndWrite()` which wraps the callback in a transaction and submits through the write queue.

### Schema versioning & migrations

The complete schema is defined as a single canonical block (`SCHEMA` in `src/storage/database.ts`) — clean, fully-idempotent `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` / `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` statements with every constraint baked in (the `enrichment_status` CHECK including `'inactive'`, the `is_undecryptable` generated column and its partial index, `redecrypt_attempts`, `last_edit_timestamp`, the `timeline_state` / `backfill_fence_timestamp` lifecycle columns, `enrichment_retries`, `trigger_group_id`, `media_assets.caption_error`, the `summaries.diary_status`/`diary_attempts` diary-queue columns, the `media_assets.caption_attempts`/`updated_at` pipeline-monitor columns, the `agent_sessions.resume_generation`/`chat_upper_bound_ts` reply-resume columns, the `usage_events` ledger with its `logical_model_id`/per-user columns and the `usage_event_partitions` overflow-membership child table, the `user_identities`/`user_identity_aliases` identity store, etc.). It is assembled from the shared sub-schema constants (`RETRIEVAL_SCHEMA`, `CHAT_SEARCH_SCHEMA`, `SUMMARY_SEARCH_SCHEMA`, `REACTIONS_SCHEMA`, `AGENT_SESSIONS_FTS_SCHEMA`, `SESSION_INTERJECTIONS_SCHEMA`, `USAGE_EVENTS_SCHEMA`, `TOOL_INVOCATIONS_SCHEMA`, `BACKFETCH_JOBS_SCHEMA`, `USER_IDENTITIES_SCHEMA`). `SCHEMA` always builds a fresh DB directly at the final shape.

Structurally the schema is still the **genesis (v1) shape**: `SCHEMA` is edited in place (it stays idempotent so re-running it on an existing DB only fills in newly-added tables/indexes via `if not exists`). `LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION = 34`. `MIGRATIONS` steps (`MIGRATIONS[v]` upgrades a v→v+1 DB) handle changes that `create … if not exists` cannot express — data-only transforms, additive DDL (`ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN`), and as of v10→v11, non-additive DDL (`ALTER TABLE … DROP COLUMN`, `CREATE TABLE`): **v1→v2** (`cleanupAssistantEchoDuplicates`) is the one-off cleanup of the historical assistant-echo duplicates — for every `matrix:{account}:{eventId}` row that duplicates an `assistant:{session}:{eventId}:{chunk}` sibling with the same `(provider, external_id, timeline_key)`, it remaps references onto the assistant row (`summary_events` lineage — dropped instead when the summary already lists the sibling —, `summaries.latest_event_id`, `summarization_jobs.input_start_id`/`input_end_id`, the `timeline_compaction_state` cursors), deletes the duplicate's enrichment artifacts (`media_assets`/`link_previews`/`reply_contexts`), and deletes the duplicate row itself (its `chat_index` projection cascade-deletes via the FK + FTS triggers). See "Assistant echo enrichment" and §7c for the fixes that stop new duplicates from forming. **v2→v3** (`repairReplyFallbackOverstrip`) is the one-off repair for reply bodies over-stripped by the native reply-fallback stripper before its shape gating existed (§6 "Rich-reply fallback stripping"): for every reply (`event_json.replyTo` set) whose stored `htmlBody` begins with a `<blockquote>` (the user's own quote, surviving because `<mx-reply>` stripping left it), it rebuilds the plain body — the blockquote text as `> `-prefixed lines, a blank line, then the surviving remainder — updating both the `body` column and `event_json.body`. Rows whose body still carries the quote (fallback-sending clients, compared on lowercase-alphanumeric-folded words so markdown/HTML rendering differences don't mislead) and quotes that nest another blockquote are left alone. `reply_contexts` rows quoting a repaired event get the repaired text when their stored body exactly equals the damaged one; `chat_index` self-heals via the startup `reconcileAll` sweep (`content_sig` changes); summaries generated from damaged renders are LLM output and are not recomputed. **v3→v4** (`addUsageEventPartitions`) adds the `usage_event_partitions` overflow-membership child table (see §8e). **v4→v5** (`addUserIdentityTables`) adds the `user_identities` and `user_identity_aliases` tables (purely additive DDL, no data backfill — see §6b). **v5→v6** (`addRoomMetadataServerColumns`) adds `server_id TEXT` and `server_name TEXT` nullable columns to `room_metadata` for Discord guild scope (see §6c). The migration uses `PRAGMA table_info(room_metadata)` to check column existence before each `ALTER TABLE` — SQLite 3.45 does not support `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, and tests simulate downgrades on a physically-v6 database, so idempotency is required. **v6→v7** (`addMemoryChunksAgentColumn`) is a full table rebuild of `memory_chunks` — adds the nullable `agent TEXT` column and changes `UNIQUE(id)` to `UNIQUE(agent, id)` for multi-agent memory scoping (see §4c "Memory scoping and search account filtering" and the schema-version note there). **v7→v8** (`addSenderBotColumns`) adds `sender_is_bot INTEGER` and `sender_is_webhook INTEGER` nullable columns to `timeline_events` for Discord bot-chain counting (spec MULTI-AGENT-SUPPORT §9 — see §4c). The migration uses `PRAGMA table_info(timeline_events)` for idempotency. Existing rows keep `null` in both columns; the chain counter treats null as human for the `sender_is_bot`/`sender_is_webhook` path (only `role = 'assistant'` or `siblingUserIds` membership elevates a null-flagged row to bot). **v8→v9** (`addSummaryMirroredFrom`) adds the `mirrored_from TEXT` nullable column to `summaries` for summary mirroring (see §9b "Summary mirroring"). **v9→v10** (`addMediaAssetsContentHash`) adds the `content_hash TEXT` nullable column to `media_assets` for content-addressed attachment dedup (see §7a "Content-addressed attachment store"). The migration uses `PRAGMA table_info(media_assets)` for idempotency. Existing rows and rows written without the attachment store keep `NULL`; the write path sets it when `[attachment_store].enabled` is true. **v10→v11** (`splitSessionPayloads`) moves `context_snapshot_json` and `transcript_json` out of `agent_sessions` into a new `agent_session_payloads` side table (`session_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES agent_sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, context_snapshot_json TEXT, transcript_json TEXT`), and creates three new indexes: `idx_agent_sessions_recent` on `coalesce(completed_at, updated_at) desc` (covering the console's recent-sessions sort), and `idx_agent_sessions_sender_recent` on `(trigger_sender_id, coalesce(completed_at, updated_at) desc) WHERE trigger_sender_display_name IS NOT NULL` (covering the `getUserLabels` fallback per-sender query). The two blob columns were SQLite overflow-page chains that forced a full page-chain traversal for any row read — `getAgentSession` now does a `LEFT JOIN agent_session_payloads` instead, and list/metadata queries are unaffected (they projected `AGENT_SESSION_META_COLUMN_NAMES`, which never included the blobs). `saveAgentSessionSnapshot` and `saveAgentSessionTranscript` each do an `UPDATE agent_sessions` for their non-blob fields plus an `INSERT … ON CONFLICT(session_id) DO UPDATE SET` that touches only its own column, so the two writers are independent and never clobber each other. The migration uses `PRAGMA table_info(agent_sessions)` to guard the copy+drop against re-runs on already-migrated schemas (fresh v11 DBs never had those columns). The timeline-query rewrite (UNION ALL range probe replacing `OR LIKE`) and `getUserLabels` batch rewrite (single window-function query replacing per-user loop) accompany this migration step but are pure query changes requiring no DDL or data backfill. **v11→v12** (`addAbsorbedParentIdColumn`) adds `absorbed_parent_id TEXT` nullable column to `summarization_jobs` for the budget-driven eager condensation absorb shape (see §9b "Budget-driven eager condensation"): a job that absorbs an existing parent P carries `absorbed_parent_id = P.id`; `insertSummaryWithLineage` uses this to atomically supersede P and the absorbed run members when the replacement summary P′ lands. The migration uses `PRAGMA table_info(summarization_jobs)` for idempotency. **v12→v13** (`widenDiaryStatusConstraint`) widens the `summaries.diary_status` CHECK constraint to include the new `'excluded'` terminal status, which the diary gate sets for channels whose resolved visibility mode is not `"shared"` (see §9h). SQLite cannot alter a CHECK constraint in place, so this is a full table rebuild of `summaries`: (1) save `summary_events` and `summary_parents` rows to temp tables and delete from children (to avoid FK cascade deletion when the parent is dropped); (2) CREATE TABLE `summaries_new` with the widened CHECK; (3) INSERT…SELECT preserving explicit rowids (the external-content `summaries_fts` addresses by rowid — mismatched rowids would corrupt the FTS index); (4) DROP the old table and RENAME; (5) recreate the `summaries_ai`/`summaries_ad` triggers and all indexes; (6) rebuild the FTS index (`INSERT INTO summaries_fts … VALUES('rebuild')`); then restore `summary_events`/`summary_parents` from the temp tables. Idempotent via the `PRAGMA table_info(summaries)` column-existence check before the rebuild. **v13→v14** (`addInputChildIdsColumn`) adds `input_child_ids TEXT` nullable column to `summarization_jobs` (see §9b "Explicit child id list and span-integrity guard"): each enqueued eager condensation job now carries the exact ordered child id list, eliminating the bug where `getSummariesBetween` at build time returned phantom interlopers and produced 2 MB+ condense requests. The migration also DELETES any non-complete row that has `absorbed_parent_id` set and `input_child_ids` null — deletion, not a terminal `failed` status, because every summarization job either completes or is removed: lingering failed level-2+ rows would block the evaluator's chunk-skip guard and show as permanently-actionable failures in the pipeline monitor. The next reconcile re-evaluates and enqueues a fresh job with an explicit child list. Uses `PRAGMA table_info(summarization_jobs)` for idempotency. **v14→v15** (`deleteCancelledPoisonedJobs`) is the data-only cleanup for databases migrated by the original v13→v14 (which marked those rows `failed` instead of deleting them): it deletes any `failed` row with `absorbed_parent_id` set and `input_child_ids` null; a no-op on databases migrated by the current v13→v14. **v15→v16** (`supersedeOrphanedAbsorbedParents`) is the data-only backfill for the worker-pool bug where both `insertSummaryWithLineage` call sites (success and truncation paths) omitted `absorbedParentId`, causing the supersession block to silently no-op: P and the absorbed run members remained `complete` even after the replacement P′ was written, producing duplicate same-level coverage that broke span-integrity checks. For every row in `summarization_jobs` with `status = 'complete'`, `absorbed_parent_id IS NOT NULL`, `input_child_ids IS NOT NULL`, and `result_summary_id IS NOT NULL` where the result summary is `complete` or `truncated`: mark the absorbed parent P as `superseded` (if still `complete`/`truncated`), then mark the run members (`input_child_ids` minus P's original children from `summary_parents`) as `superseded`. Idempotent: already-superseded rows are unaffected by the `status in ('complete', 'truncated')` filter. **v16→v17** (`addDmOptoutsTable`) adds the `dm_optouts` table (purely additive DDL; see §6b DM opt-out table). **v17→v18** (`addDmPeersTable`) adds the `dm_peers` table (purely additive DDL; see §6 DM peers table). **v18→v19** (`addWorkspaceSeedLedger`) adds the `workspace_seed_ledger` table (purely additive DDL; see §4b and §6 workspace_seed_ledger). **v19→v20** (`repairStaleEditedQuotes`) is the one-off data repair for reply quotes stored before by-id lookups became edit-aware (§6 "Message edits"): every `reply_contexts` row whose target has an applied edit (`last_edit_timestamp` set) takes the target's stored post-edit body, choosing the target as `Storage.getEditedBody` does (same provider, the quoting event's room or one of its threads, never another account's room, an exact room-key row over a thread row). Body-less stubs are left alone, matching the live refresh. **v20→v21** (`addUsageEventPartitionsTimelineKey`) adds `timeline_key` to `usage_event_partitions`, back-filled from the parent rows (see §8f). **v21→v22** (`addAgentSessionInitialPreloads`) adds the nullable `agent_sessions.initial_preloads` column (JSON `SessionRoutingState`: preloaded skills, routed model / cascade / thinking level) for decision-model routing (see §8h "Routing"); additive, no back-fill. **v22→v23** (`addUsageEventModelPrompt`) adds the nullable `usage_events.model_prompt` and `model_prompt_hash` columns (see §8 "Model prompts"); additive, no back-fill. **v23→v24** (`addSessionRecordsTables`) creates the `session_records` and `decision_evaluations` tables with their two `decision_evaluations` indexes (see §8i "Storage" and §8h "Decision visibility"); purely additive DDL, the same shape `SCHEMA` builds on a fresh DB. **v24→v25** (`addRefusalHandlingTables`) creates `refusal_events`, `contract_attempts` and `agent_session_branches` (DDL shared with `SCHEMA` as `REFUSAL_HANDLING_SCHEMA`) and adds, `PRAGMA table_info`-guarded, `agent_sessions.contract_outcome`/`contract_nudges`/`contract_version`/`refusal_pin`, `decision_evaluations.checkpoint`/`branch_no`/`tool_call_id`/`attempt_no`/`consequence` and `usage_events.system_prompt_hash` (§8j "Storage"); new columns are appended at the end of each table in `SCHEMA` so a migrated table's shape equals a fresh one. **v25→v26** (`addModelBehaviourTables`) creates the model behaviour tables, the `idx_agent_sessions_created` and partial `idx_timeline_events_session` indexes and the dirty-hour triggers on the raw tables (a trigger or index only when its table exists), then marks every hour with history dirty so the rollups fill in the background (§8k). **v26→v27** (`addSessionAuditsTable`) creates `session_audits` with its unique expression index and dirty-hour triggers (§9i). **v27→v28** adds `tool_invocations.metadata_json` (paid service provenance). **v28→v29** creates the durable Exa research tables. **v29→v30** (`addLateInputColumns`) adds the late-input columns (§8 "Late input"). **v30→v31** (`markWipedDeletions`) is the data-only step for messages wiped by the old deletion path, which stored a deletion as an empty edit: every row with an empty body, no attachments and `last_edit_timestamp` set gets the deletion marker (`deleted.at` = `last_edit_timestamp`, deleter unknown), so the recent tiers show the deletion placeholder instead of an empty message, when it is a human's (`role = 'user'` with neither `sender_is_bot` nor `sender_is_webhook`: another bot's or a webhook's edited embed-only message looks the same and was never deleted) or the agent's own (`role = 'assistant'`: its sends always have a body and `edit_message` refuses empty text, so an empty edited one was wiped by a deletion). Their content cannot be recovered; nothing else on the row changes, and a row already marked is left alone. **v31→v32** (`repairWipedDeletionMarkers`, data-only) repairs databases the first version of that step migrated: it removes the markers it put on bot and webhook rows (only a marker that step could have made: no deleter, `at` equal to `last_edit_timestamp`, on a wiped row; never one a live deletion set), then marks the wiped rows as v31 now does (the agent's own wiped messages, which it skipped). Idempotent. **v32→v33** (`markSiblingWipedDeletions`, data-only): another agent sharing the database (§4c) is another bot to this agent, so a sibling agent's wiped message stayed unmarked in this agent's timeline. The sibling's own copy of the same message (`role = 'assistant'`, the same `(provider, external_id)`) is marked when it was wiped (v32), and an agent's sends always have a body, so that marker tells a deletion apart from an edited embed-only message: a wiped bot row (`sender_is_bot`, not a webhook) with such a marked twin gets the marker (`deleted.at` = its own `last_edit_timestamp`, deleter unknown). Idempotent. Webhook rows stay unmarked in every step: a deleted proxied message (a PluralKit proxy, treated as a human elsewhere) whose body the old path wiped and an edited embed-only webhook message look the same in storage (an empty body, no attachments, an edit time), no agent copy exists to compare with, and the stored link previews do not tell them apart either (an embed-only message may have none stored, a proxied message with a link has some), so a marker would be a guess; such a row renders as an empty message. **v33→v34** (`addMemoryRetrievalTables`) creates the judged-retrieval tables (`memory_block_provenance`, `memory_block_participants`, `memory_filter_verdicts`, `memory_filter_hits`, `memory_late_vectors`, `memory_index_failures`, `memory_retrievals`; DDL shared with `SCHEMA` as `MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_SCHEMA`, src/storage/memory-retrieval-schema.ts) and `memory_sender_names` (each display name a sender id has used, kept by `timeline_events` insert/update triggers; rows older than the triggers are back-filled after startup in 500-row batches, `MemoryRetrievalStore.backfillSenderNames`, because an index on `timeline_events(provider, sender_id, timestamp)` takes seconds to build on a large timeline, 6.5 s on 2M synthetic events, on the event loop); purely additive (see §9d). A future column/table rename or data transform that `create … if not exists` cannot express follows the same pattern: bump `LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION` and append an ordered step.

Versioning still uses SQLite's `PRAGMA user_version`. Inside `open()`'s write callback, the runner first records whether the database is **fresh** (no `timeline_events` table yet) *before* any DDL runs (`SCHEMA` uses `if not exists`, so afterward a fresh and an existing DB look identical):

- A **fresh** DB runs `SCHEMA` *first* (builds every table/index at the latest shape — which contains no duplicates by construction, so the data-only step is irrelevant to it), then `runMigrations` only stamps `user_version = LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION`. Both run inside a **single `db.transaction()`** so a crash mid-build is all-or-nothing — a partial set of tables can never be left behind to be misclassified as fresh on the next open (issue #7).
- An **existing** DB runs `runMigrations` *first* (applies any pending `MIGRATIONS` steps in one transaction), then `writer.exec(SCHEMA)` reconciles it to the canonical shape, creating via `if not exists` any table/index it lacks. The order (migrations before `SCHEMA`) means any future legacy-shape ALTER lands before `SCHEMA`'s latest-shape DDL.
- In all cases, `runMigrations` reads `user_version`: a version *newer* than the build supports (`> LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION`) is a **hard error** — it refuses to open, to avoid corrupting forward-versioned data; at the latest version it is a no-op (re-opening is idempotent); below the latest version it applies each `MIGRATIONS` step from the current version up to the latest, then stamps `user_version`.

The `sqlite-vec` `memory_vec` virtual table (and its `memory_vec_*` shadow tables) are **not** part of `SCHEMA`: they are created at runtime by `VectorStore.ensure()` (`src/retrieval/vector-store.ts`) at the embedding model's dimension, so a freshly-opened DB that has not yet embedded anything will not contain them. This is orthogonal to the schema-version machinery.

### Event lifecycle

1. **Append** — upsert via `ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE`, preserving original `created_at`
2. **Dedup + ingest previews** — `appendIfMissing()` checks existence by canonical `id` first, then by `(provider, external_id, timeline_key)`, and returns `{ event, duplicate }`. The external-id check is what dedups a **bot self-message** re-encountered by backfill/backfetch: send_message stores it under an `assistant:{session}:{eventId}:{chunk}` canonical id while re-fetched history re-keys the same Matrix event `matrix:{account}:{eventId}`, so an id-only check would insert a duplicate row. Scoping by `timeline_key` keeps two accounts sharing a room (same Matrix event id, different timeline keys) from deduping against each other. On a fresh insert, provider-resolved previews on `event.linkPreviews` (Discord payload embeds) are written as `link_previews` rows inside the same transaction (`Storage.insertIngestLinkPreviews`), so the `event_id` FK holds regardless of how the caller's async pipeline is ordered
3. **Enrich** — `updateTimelineEvent()` does read-modify-write on `event_json` (for caption results, echo metadata)
4. **Echo resolution** — `ingestAssistantEcho()` finds existing assistant events by `external_id` or fuzzy body match (±5min window, max 100 candidates), then enriches or appends; `ingestAssistantSend()` is the send-side mirror (see "Assistant echo enrichment")

### Routing

`TimelineRouter` directs inbound events to the correct timeline by `timelineKey`, deduplicating and appending in a single write-queue transaction.

### Trigger group resolution

When a trigger fires, the hold-grouped event IDs and a lookback query are unified into a single **trigger group**. The lookback finds the most recent same-sender message with a media attachment within `trigger_group_lookback_ms` (default 20s) of the trigger timestamp, then includes all same-sender messages between that attachment message and the trigger — not just the single attachment message. A deleted message (§6 "Message edits") is left out of the lookback. All events in the group get their `trigger_group_id` column updated in one DB write, making their media assets visible to caption workers. `resolveTriggerGroup` is gated on `ProviderCapabilities.singleAttachmentPerMessage`; providers that allow multiple attachments per message (e.g. Discord) return early without a lookback, since each user message already carries all its attachments together.

### Trigger coordination

`TriggerCoordinator` enforces per-timeline concurrency:

- Per-timeline active session count tracked in `activeByTimeline`
- Limit is `max_concurrent_dm` for DM timelines, `max_concurrent` for group timelines
- Under limit → `"spawn"`, at limit → `"queued"` (up to `max_queued_per_timeline`), queue full → `"ignored"`
- On session completion, the next queued trigger is dequeued and launched
- No TTL-based expiry; backpressure via configurable cap and logging
- No global concurrency limit — only per-timeline

---

## 7a. Enrichment Pipeline

Enrichment is a post-persistence, provider-agnostic system that processes timeline events after they are stored. It replaces the earlier approach where enrichment happened inside the Matrix layer before persistence.

### Design principles

1. **Persist first, enrich later.** Events are stored immediately with bare metadata. If enrichment fails or the app crashes, the message is never lost.
2. **Provider-agnostic.** Enrichment workers use an `EnrichmentCapabilities` interface provided by the chat provider, not provider-specific code. Adding a new provider means implementing this interface.
3. **No inference in enrichment.** Enrichment workers handle I/O (downloads, fetches, resolution). Captioning (inference) is a separate worker pool with its own concurrency limits.
4. **Atomic results.** All enrichment data for one event is written in a single DB transaction — reply context, link previews, and media assets are either all present or all absent.

### Enrichment worker pool (`src/enrichment/`)

A pool of workers (configurable count, default 3) continuously polls the DB for events with `enrichment_status='pending'`, most recent first. Each worker claims an event (CAS to `'processing'`), then executes all enrichment for that message. The channel id for channel-bound capability calls is extracted from the timeline key by the shared `channelIdFromTimelineKey` (`src/storage/timeline-key.ts`) — **never** a naive `split(":")`, which truncates classic `!local:server` room ids at the server colon and makes every room-bound call fail on an unknown room. If the key is present but doesn't parse, the worker logs `timeline_key.malformed` and skips the channel-bound steps (1, 2) while still running the body-only steps.

1. **Download attachments** — per-attachment routing based on what each attachment needs: if the attachment has a `remoteUrl` (a pre-signed external CDN URL, e.g. from Discord), it is streamed to disk via `FetchClient.downloadUrl()`; if there is no `remoteUrl` but a channel id is available, the provider `downloadMedia()` RPC is called (Matrix path, streams directly to disk); if neither is present (malformed timeline key), the attachment is silently skipped and no row is created. Downloaded files are written with content-addressed filenames (SHA-256 hash, base32 prefix, 13 chars). **In legacy mode** (no `[agents]` table) they land in `<workspaceRoot>/msg-attach/<filename>` and `local_path` is `"msg-attach/<filename>"`. **In agents mode** the pool resolves the owning agent's workspace root per-event from the event's `timeline_key`; files land in `<agentRoot>/msg-attach/<provider>.<accountKey>/<filename>` and `local_path` is `"msg-attach/<provider>.<accountKey>/<filename>"` — the workspace-relative path includes the account-scoped subdir. Temp files always land in `<workspaceRoot>/msg-attach/.tmp-<id>` (the root of `msg-attach/`, not the subdir) so the rename stays on the same filesystem. Move uses `rename()` with EXDEV fallback (`copyFile` + `unlink`) for cross-filesystem scenarios. **When `[attachment_store].enabled` is true**, all file writes are routed through `AttachmentStore.integrateDownload()` / `integrateBuffer()` instead: each downloaded file is stored once under `<store>/<hh>/<sha256>` (two-level fan-out) and hardlinked into the workspace destination, deduplicating identical content across all agents' workspaces at the inode level (see §7a "Content-addressed attachment store"). The full sha256 hex is recorded in `media_assets.content_hash`. If the per-event resolve returns `undefined` (§4.3), all file downloads are skipped for that event; DB-only enrichment (link previews, reply context text) continues.
2. **Resolve reply context** (`EnrichmentWorker.lookupReplyTarget`) → store sender, body, timestamp. The target is described by a **provider-neutral** `ReplyTargetSummary`: `{ eventId, sender, senderName?, body, timestamp, attachments? }` where `attachments` is an array of `{ mediaType, filename?, mimeType?, remoteUrl? }` objects (no `msgtype` — provider-specific vocabulary is translated before this point). It is obtained from the first applicable source:
   1. **Provider lookup** — `capabilities.messageSummary()` when the provider implements it (optional on `EnrichmentCapabilities`, like `resolveLinkPreviews`). When present it is **authoritative**: its answer, including `null`, is final and no fallback runs. Matrix lives here — the native summary applies the reply-fallback stripping and UTD handling of §6 that no stored copy could reproduce, and a redacted target must not be resurrected from the DB. The one exception is an **edited** target: the provider returns the original event, so the stored post-edit body (`Storage.getEditedBody`, §6 "Message edits") replaces the summary's body; sender, timestamp and attachments stay the provider's.
   2. **Ingest-time snapshot** — the event's own `replyTo`, when it carries a body or attachments. Providers whose payload includes the referenced message populate it at normalization (Discord `referenced_message`, §6c); it is refreshed on every reply, so it reflects edits and carries currently-signed CDN URLs. A sender-only stub (author known, empty body, no attachments — what the Discord normalizer builds on a message-cache miss) does not count as resolved.
   3. **Stored copy** — `Storage.getTimelineEventByExternalId(provider, replyTo.externalId, timelineKey)`: the target was ingested earlier on this timeline even though the provider could not quote it now.

   When attachments are present, **all** are downloaded using the same per-attachment routing as step 1, creating `reply_attachment` rows for each index. A target that every applicable source misses (provider says redacted/non-message, or — without a provider lookup — neither the snapshot nor the store knows it) or a thrown resolution failure degrades to a **stub row** (`reply_external_id` only) and is always logged (`enrichment_reply_target_missing` / `enrichment_reply_resolution_failed`) — never swallowed silently; the renderer marks a stub as unavailable (§9). The stub is written deliberately even though the event's `replyTo` may carry an external id: the hydrator (§9) applies the `reply_contexts` row over the persisted `replyTo`, so a stub written for a resolvable target would *replace* a quoted message with the unavailable placeholder — which is exactly why the fallbacks above exist.
3. **Fetch link previews** for message body — a partition step: X status URLs go to the FxTwitter stage (see "X.com enrichment via FxTwitter" below); remaining URLs go to the link preview stage. `resolveLinkPreviews` is **optional** on `EnrichmentCapabilities`: when present (Matrix path), it calls the provider's Synapse `preview_url` endpoint; when absent, `DirectLinkPreviewClient` (`src/enrichment/link-preview-client.ts`) scrapes `og:`/`twitter:` meta tags from the URLs directly via `FetchClient` (plain HTML fetch, no JS rendering, entity-decoded), using `twitter:` as a fallback when `og:` tags are absent, and produces rows with `source_kind = "direct_scrape"`. Before scraping, the worker queries `getIngestLinkPreviewUrls(eventId)` to find URLs already covered by `source_kind = "discord_embed"` rows (ingest-time Discord embed previews) and passes them as `excludeUrls` so they are not re-fetched or overwritten. `persistEnrichmentResults` preserves `source_kind = "discord_embed"` rows when it deletes stale link_previews (the DELETE excludes rows where `source_kind = 'discord_embed'`), so ingest-time Discord previews are never clobbered by worker-time scraping. `enrichment.max_previews_per_message` is one shared cap across all kinds, allocated by order of first appearance in the body.
4. **Fetch link previews** for reply body (if reply was resolved) — identical partition and fallback treatment
5. **Extract and download linked media** from message body (URLs ending in media extensions)
6. **Extract and download linked media** from reply body
7. **Detect character cards** on all image assets (reads PNG tEXt chunks, no inference)
8. **Set caption eligibility** — images with successful downloads get `caption_status='pending'`, others get `'skipped'`

Steps within a job run concurrently where possible (`Promise.all`), with reply-dependent steps (4, 6) awaiting reply resolution (2). Individual download/fetch failures do not fail the whole job — each asset tracks its own status. The job fails only on unexpected errors (DB failures).

On completion, all results are written atomically (link previews first due to FK constraints, then media assets) and `enrichment_status` flips to `'complete'`. Failed jobs are retried up to `max_retries` via the durable `timeline_events.enrichment_retries` column (incremented on each failure), so retry state survives a restart and feeds the pipeline monitor's counts (§11). On startup, stale `'processing'` claims are reset to `'pending'`.

### Media asset roles

The `media_assets` table tracks every downloaded file with a `role` distinguishing its origin:

| Role | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `attachment` | Direct attachment on the message |
| `reply_attachment` | Attachment on the replied-to message |
| `preview_media` | Media from a link preview (OG image, tweet photos) |
| `reply_preview_media` | Media from a link preview on the replied-to message |
| `linked_media` | Media URL found directly in message body text |
| `reply_linked_media` | Same, from the replied-to message body |

All media is saved as the exact original file — processing (resize, re-encode, truncate) is always ephemeral and handled by `src/media/` at inference or context-build time.

### Content-addressed attachment store

`src/enrichment/attachment-store.ts` — `AttachmentStore` class. Default-off: only constructed when `[attachment_store] enabled = true`. When enabled, all enrichment file writes route through the store instead of the plain rename/write path.

**Store layout**: `<storePath>/<hh>/<sha256hex>` — two-level fan-out keyed by the first two hex characters of the sha256 hash (`hh`), limiting top-level directory entries to at most 256 (one per hex pair) regardless of corpus size. `storePath` defaults to `./attachment-store`; configurable via `[attachment_store].path`.

**Write path** (`integrateDownload` / `integrateBuffer`):
- **Hash new**: rename (or copy on EXDEV) the source file into the store, set chmod 0444, then `link()` the store file into the workspace destination.
- **Hash already in store**: `link()` store → destination; discard the source. The redundant download is used only to confirm the content before dedup.
- **EXDEV at link time** (store and workspace on different filesystems, which the startup probe should have prevented): log warn once per destination directory, fall back to a plain rename/copy to the workspace without store participation.
- `integrateBuffer` writes the buffer to a temp file inside the store directory (same filesystem as the store is guaranteed; same filesystem as the workspace roots is guaranteed by the startup probe), then delegates to `integrateDownload`.

**Read-only discipline**: every store file is set chmod 0444 after landing. Because workspace paths are hardlinks to the same inode, any write attempt through any path fails loudly rather than silently corrupting other agents' copies.

**Startup probe** (`init(workspaceRoots)`): creates a temp file in the store directory and calls `link()` into each workspace root's `msg-attach/`. If any root is on a different filesystem, the probe receives EXDEV and throws a descriptive error — the process exits before any production I/O. The temp file is always removed in a `finally` block. `isReady()` returns true only after a successful `init`.

**Adoption sweep** (`adoptSweep(workspaceRoots)`): background reconciliation, called at startup (30 s delay) and daily. Walks every `msg-attach/` tree under each workspace root:
- **Not in store**: `link()` the workspace file into the store; chmod 0444.
- **In store, different inode**: atomic swap — `link(store → tmp); rename(tmp → workspace)` — after which the workspace path points to the canonical store inode, freeing the duplicate block allocation.
- **Same inode already**: skip (idempotent).
- **`.tmp-*` files**: always skipped (in-flight downloads).
- EXDEV per-file: logged once per directory; file left un-adopted.

No persistent cursor is needed: the inode comparison makes every re-walk idempotent. `media_assets.local_path` is never modified — workspace filenames are preserved by the swap, so existing DB references remain valid.

**`media_assets.content_hash`**: nullable `TEXT` column (v9→v10 migration). Set by the enrichment write path to the full sha256 hex whenever the store is enabled. NULL on pre-Phase-5d rows and rows written without the store. Enables future dedup lookups without re-hashing files on disk.

**Config**: `[attachment_store] enabled = false | true; path = "<string>"`. The store is entirely absent when the block is omitted or `enabled = false` — no probe runs, no extra I/O, byte-identical behaviour to before this feature.

### Caption worker pool (`src/captioning/`)

A separate pool of workers (configurable count, default 2) continuously polls the DB for media assets eligible for captioning. **In agents mode**, each claimed asset's `timeline_key` is used to resolve the owning agent's workspace root (via the same `resolveWorkspaceRoot` resolver as the enrichment pool); the `local_path` is then expanded under that root. If the account is unresolvable, or the asset's `timeline_key` is NULL (§4.3), the asset is marked `failed` without retry and the event `caption_workspace_unresolvable` is logged. **Operator note**: assets failed with "workspace unresolvable" remain in the `failed` state permanently — the pool never retries them. If the removed account is re-added to config later, affected assets must be manually reset to `pending` (e.g. `UPDATE media_assets SET caption_status='pending', caption_error=NULL WHERE caption_error LIKE 'workspace unresolvable%'`) before they will be captioned. In legacy mode (no resolver) every asset resolves under the global `workspaceRoot`. An asset is eligible when:

1. `caption_status = 'pending'` (set by enrichment)
2. `download_status = 'complete'` (file is on disk)
3. `media_type = 'image'`
4. The event is in a trigger group, **or** `caption_all` is true, **or** the event's role is `assistant` and `caption_assistant_messages` is true

Trigger-group media is prioritized over non-trigger-group media. The `caption_assistant_messages` flag enables captioning of **all** assistant-sent media regardless of trigger group membership — this is intentionally asymmetric with user-sent media (which require a trigger group unless `caption_all` is set). Each worker claims an asset, determines its effective modality (image/video/audio), and routes to the corresponding per-modality `InferenceClient`. The inference client calls the shared `src/media/` processing pipeline before sending to the API: images are scaled to the pixel budget and iteratively JPEG-compressed (`processImageForInference`), videos are re-encoded to target resolution/duration/size (`processVideoForInference` with optional GPU acceleration and a SHA-256-keyed file cache), and audio is re-encoded and truncated (`processAudioForInference`). For animated images (GIF, animated WebP/AVIF — detected via `sharp.metadata().pages > 1`), the worker converts to MP4 via fluent-ffmpeg and processes as video, falling back to first-frame image captioning if ffmpeg is unavailable or video captioning fails. The shared default captioning model is configured via `captioning.model` (id, endpoint, api_key) with per-modality overrides available under `captioning.image.model`, `captioning.video.model`, `captioning.audio.model`. Each modality has its own prompt and max_chars; in-flight caption-inference concurrency is governed by the model's LLM rate-limit group (`max_in_flight`, §8a), not by a per-modality knob. **Per-agent captioning overrides** (spec PER-AGENT-MODEL-OVERRIDES §4): at startup, for each agent that declares `[agents.<name>.models.captioning]`, one `InferenceClient` is built per modality whose resolved chain ref differs from the global baseline — agents whose ref matches the baseline reuse the same client instance (no allocation, no duplicate teardown). All behavioral settings (prompt, max_chars, max_tokens, media-processing options, scheduler) are taken from the global captioning config; only the chain differs. All distinct clients (baseline + per-agent) are tracked in a teardown `Set` for exactly-once stop. **Per-asset client resolution**: the caption pool already resolves the owning agent per asset from the asset's `timeline_key` (§4.3 unresolvable → existing `failed` path, unchanged); it passes that agent name into `resolveAgentCaptionClient`, which returns the per-agent client when the agent has an override that differs from baseline, or the baseline client otherwise — `null` agentName always returns the baseline. The same resolution governs the **per-session tool-site caption clients**: the `media` tool, danbooru's non-vision `preview`, and the `x_search` inline caption lane each receive the session's agent's client rather than the global baseline. The **captioning ladder** uses strict same-rung shadowing (owner sign-off): `agents.A.models.captioning[M]` shadows `captioning[M].model` at rung 1; `agents.A.models.captioning.model` shadows `captioning.model` at rung 2 — a globally-configured per-modality assignment keeps winning over an agent's shared override unless the agent overrides the modality by name. Caption transport is selected per serving fallback member from `[models.*].api`. `openai-responses` uses `/responses` for image input, `max_output_tokens`, `store: false`, and the configured `thinking_level` after `thinking_level_map` remapping (`off` becomes `none` unless remapped). Captions retain only assistant `output_text` blocks; native reasoning and tool items are discarded. Incomplete, refused, empty, and unsupported-modality results are content failures: they do not mark the model unhealthy or trigger model fallback. The Responses path rejects direct audio/video input and names the per-modality model selector needed for a compatible Chat Completions model. Other API selections retain the existing OpenRouter-compatible Chat Completions fetch with `image_url`, `video_url`, and `input_audio`. These are standalone caption calls: agent grammar prefill is not applied, even when the selected model also backs prefilling agent sessions. Media whose duration exceeds `media.video.max_duration_seconds` or `media.audio.max_duration_seconds` is truncated; for tool-initiated captions a warning is prepended indicating the processed range and suggesting `start_time` for other segments. Failed captions are retried up to `max_retries` via the **durable** `media_assets.caption_attempts` counter — incremented inside the claim CAS (mirroring `enrichment_retries`), so retry state survives a restart and is visible to the pipeline monitor's DB-derived counts (§11 "Pipeline monitor"); every caption write also bumps `media_assets.updated_at`, the monitor's reverse-chron sort key. On startup, stale `'processing'` claims are reset to `'pending'`.

**Refusals (§8j).** A refused caption (`CaptionRefusalError`: a refusal finish reason or a refusal message part, on Chat Completions or Responses) is billed as a `caption` ledger row and recorded in `refusal_events` (no session); a `[[refusal_fallback]]` rule for site `caption` re-runs the call on its entries' chains (`runFetchWithRefusalRules`), and an exhausted walk fails the asset terminally (no re-run).
