An unhealthy model's waiters are *skipped over, not waited behind*, so they never head-of-line-block healthy models sharing the group. When everything queued is gated behind probe windows, a timer re-pumps at the earliest window.
- **Properties** (spec P6): during an outage, any number of waiting sessions on the broken model produce exactly **one upstream request per probe window** (every Layer-0 retry re-enters `acquire()` and queues — no redundant hammering), and the capped backoff bounds the long-outage tail at `llm_probe_backoff_max_ms`. Priority survives the outage: waiters queue at their class rank, so when the probe succeeds, interactive requests drain first. Logged via `llm_model_unhealthy` / `llm_model_probe` / `llm_model_recovered` (with outage duration and waiter count).

### Per-agent model resolution (spec PER-AGENT-MODEL-OVERRIDES)

Before the fallback chain is built, the factory resolves the logical model key via a three-rung ladder through `resolveModelKey(sessionType, timelineKey)`. The ladder runs in `src/agent/agent-model-overrides.ts` (`buildAgentModelOverrides`), built once at startup; all resolvers are pure O(1) lookups. `null` agentName (legacy single-agent mode) short-circuits every rung to the global-only path — byte-identical to pre-override behavior.

**Chat-lane ladder** — for a session owned by agent A with session type T (where `agentOverrides = agents.A.models.session_types`, `t = agent.session_types[T]`):

1. `agentOverrides[T]` (agent type-specific), else `t?.model` (global type-specific, may be absent even when `t` exists)
2. `agentOverrides["default"]` (agent default), else — only when the type-specific block `t` is **absent entirely** — `agent.session_types["default"]?.model` (global default). The block-level fallback subtlety: when `t` exists but carries no `model` key, `resolveSessionType` returns `t`, so the chain resolves to literal `"default"` — not the default type's model. The ladder reproduces this invariant exactly: when `t` is present, the global half of rung 2 is `undefined` regardless of `t.model`, so a declared type block without a model key still lands on literal `"default"` rather than the default type's model. The agent's `"default"` override applies at rung 2 in both cases.
3. Literal `"default"` (always present in the global registry)

An agent overriding only `"default"` inherits that override wherever the global config falls past the type-specific altitude; a session type with an explicit global model keeps it unless the agent also overrides that type by name. The same `resolveModelKey` seam is threaded through every chat-lane consumer: `factory.create`, admission gates (`resolveModelChainLogicalIds`, `resolveSessionContextCeiling`, `resolveModelId`, `resolveLogicalModelId`), proactive model resolution, diary/summarization provenance stamps, and the three `BudgetEngineOptions` callback signatures — all accept an optional `timelineKey` and resolve through the ladder when the factory has both `resolveAgentName` and `agentModelOverrides` wired. Without a `timelineKey` (or either wired option absent) they resolve the global-only path — backward-compatible for all legacy callers.

**`replyModelCanSeeImages`** is derived from the per-agent resolved `modelConfig.input_modalities` at `factory.create` time (BEFORE `buildContext`), then threaded explicitly into `ContextBuilder.buildContext` (fresh launch), `buildResumeTurn` (resume), `buildPreview` (room preview), and the steer interjection paths so the pixel-block gate uses the per-agent model's actual capability. A text-only agent model suppresses all image-block creation regardless of what the global session-type config declares.

**`resolveSessionContextCeiling(sessionType, timelineKey?)`** — the text-editor budget, the console preview, and all admission gates call this with the session's timeline key so the ceiling reflects the per-agent resolved head's operative window. Without a key it falls back to the global path (backward-compatible).

**Claim-gate global-lanes note.** `makeAgentLoopClaimGate` (the worker-pool pause-while-blocked check) keys on `factory.resolveModelChainLogicalIds(sessionType)` **without** a timeline key — the claim gate has no per-session context at evaluation time. Under diverging per-agent models a session whose agent's override is in-budget may be held while the global model chain shows over-budget. This is a conservative over-pause (the gate never incorrectly admits; it can only over-refuse temporarily). The per-session admission gates, which are agent-aware (they call `resolveModelChainLogicalIds` with the session's timeline key), are the correct enforcement point.

### Model fallback — transparent composite models

A logical model `X` with a fallback chain `[X, Y, Z]` is a **composite model** (spec MODEL-FALLBACK): a request to `X` is served by the first chain member that is up, and **the caller never sees that `X` was unavailable**. Fallback sits *below* the failure-handling layer — it is model **selection** in front of §8a's per-model health (which **is** the circuit breaker; no new breaker is built) plus a return-to-primary canary policy. Chains are declared on the model: `[models.X].fallback = ["Y", "Z"]` (logical ids in `[models.*]`); the model is the implicit head and the chain is exactly the one written (a member's own `fallback` does **not** transitively extend it). Role-specific fallback comes from pointing a role at a **virtual model** (`[models.*].inherits`, §4) — there is no per-tool/per-session-type fallback config.

`src/agent/model-fallback.ts` is the one shared helper. **Build time (once)** does only what must be fixed: a **capability pre-filter** (drop members that can't serve the request's fixed needs — image blocks → `multimodal`; never drops the head); **per-member operative windows** — each surviving member's `min(context_window, session_type.max_context_tokens)`, stored in `memberWindows` keyed by logical id, with `maxOperativeContextWindow` = max over all survivors (the enforcement threshold) and `operativeContextWindow` = min-over-chain, retained as a backward-compat field; the planning ceiling is NOT this field — code needing the head's own window reads `memberWindows[headLogicalId]` (the factory's `contextCeiling = fallback.memberWindows[modelKey]`); the Model descriptor each member's dispatch pipeline carries uses that **member's own operative window**, not the chain min; and a per-candidate dispatch pipeline (`withSchedulerAdmission(base, …)` per member, with the member's group/key/probe-cap). **Per attempt** (inside the composed `streamFn`, wrapped by `withRequestRetry`, so each Layer-0 attempt re-resolves) it chooses one member in chain order:

The **agent path** applies the capability filter too (`factory.create`): `buildModelFallback` is called BEFORE `buildContext`, so image-presence is read from the **raw session inputs** available at create time — the trigger event's own/reply image attachments and (on resume) any prefix-snapshot message carrying `imageBlocks` (`rawInputsRequireMultimodal`). Whether those images are shipped as pixels is a property of the session's **reply model** — the per-agent resolved `modelConfig` (resolved via the chat-lane ladder above, or from `sessionType.model` when no per-agent override applies — in which case `default` genuinely *is* its model when the type block has no `model` key), the one that will actually serve the turn — and of that model **alone**: the builder gates image-block creation on `ContextBuilder.replyModelCanSeeImages` (resolved from `modelConfig.input_modalities` at create time and threaded explicitly to every context-build path), never on `[models.default]`-as-a-fixed-reference or any fallback member's modality. So the requirement is "the reply model accepts images **and** a raw input carries one": when it holds every viable chain member must also accept image input (`input_modalities` includes `"image"`), so a fall-over never ships image blocks to a text-only fallback (the head is never dropped); when the reply model is **text-only** no pixels are created at all — the captions (always rendered) carry the image — and the trigger imposes **no** requirement, so the full fallback chain stays usable. This is a deliberate **safe over-approximation** — "any raw image, *when the reply model can see it*, ⇒ require multimodal for the whole session" — and generation (summarize/condense/diary) and proactive sessions impose no requirement (they send no pixels). **Per-member context fits (spec PER-MEMBER-CONTEXT-FITS).** At select time `chooseChainMember` receives the running observed-context count (`getObservedContextTokens()`, fed from the factory's token counter) and skips members whose operative window is smaller than that count — a member **fits** the context iff `observed ≤ member.operativeWindow`. The head's window is tested the same way; only members that fit AND are healthy AND in-budget are viable. `maxOperativeContextWindow` (max over survivors) is the **enforcement threshold** used by the hard pre-flight (`checkContextBudget`): termination fires only when `observed > maxOperativeContextWindow`, i.e. when no member can possibly serve — a context that exceeds the head but fits a larger fallback continues cleanly via that fallback. **Planning ceiling.** `resolveSessionContextCeiling` (text-editor read budget, console — no per-session image info) returns the **head's own operative window** (`min(head.context_window, session_type.max_context_tokens)`); the chain min is removed. Per-member fits are enforced at select time, not by conservatively shrinking the planning ceiling to the smallest member.

- **head viable** (`modelHealth(head) === "healthy"` *and* `budget.isModelAvailable(head-logical, requestScope)` *and* fits — `observed ≤ head.operativeWindow`, or `observed` not yet available) → the head (`primary`);
- **head unhealthy + probe window open + in-budget + fits + NO background prober** → the head as the **canary** — this attempt enters admission keyed on the head and §8a admits it as the half-open probe. A head with a background prober (the agent path) is **never** canaried with live traffic: it recovers out of band (§8a "Background probes") while requests ride the chain. The canary is budget-gated AND fits-gated: a probe on an over-budget or context-exceeding head is suppressed (traffic can't route back anyway until the budget resets or the context shrinks); `nextProbeAt` only advances when a probe fires, so the head is immediately probe-due again once the window resets;
- else the **first downstream member** that is healthy *and* in-budget *and* fits *and* not exhausted in this request's pass (`health-fallback` when the head is unhealthy, `budget-fallback` when over a model-scoped cap, `context-fallback` when the head's window is smaller than the accumulated context but a downstream member's window is not, `failover` when the healthy head already used its attempts in this request);
- else (nothing healthy + in-budget + fits) → the head (`all-unhealthy`), so it fails, Layer-0 retries the *composite*, and the §8 per-class wall-clock budget decides whole-chain park/wait. A member that lacks `reasoning` is **not** filtered — it degrades to no-thinking with a warn. The chosen member's `Model` descriptor (carrying **its own** operative window, not the chain min) **and** per-request `api_key` are substituted at the one seam pi-agent-core exposes (`config.model` + `apiKey` passed to `streamFn`); this is not mid-stream switching — each attempt is a whole fresh request to one model.

**One pass per request** keeps a longer chain from ever meaning more downtime. Layer 0 creates a `RequestAttemptState` per request and threads it to every attempt under the `REQUEST_ATTEMPT_STATE` symbol on the stream options; the resolver counts dispatches per member **health key** in it. Within one request the head gets `recovery.llm_primary_attempts_per_request` attempts (default 2 — one retry absorbs a blip; the head is still only marked unhealthy globally at `llm_unhealthy_threshold`) and every other member **one**; an exhausted member is not viable while a non-exhausted one is, so a request never re-hits a member it watched fail while an untried member remains. At dispatch the resolver also sets `failoverOnFailure` — whether a failure of this attempt would move to a *different* member — and Layer 0 then skips its local backoff (backoff paces re-hitting the same upstream; moving on to a working member never waits). When every usable member has failed, the next attempt (after Layer 0's backoff) clears the counts and starts a new pass. Cost bound: a request reaches member *i* after at most `primary_attempts + (i − 1)` failed attempts, and only if all of those members actually failed; each failing member also trips globally, so later requests skip it outright. Driven outside Layer 0 (no state on the options) the resolver applies no pass rule.

**Refusals.** A provider refusal arrives from pi-ai as `stopReason: "error"`; `isRefusalSignal(rawStopReason, errorMessage)` (`src/agent/request-retry.ts`) recognizes it, structured signal first. The raw stop reason (`AssistantMessage.rawStopReason`, kept on the error event through the admission wrapper and Layer 0's tagging) is one of: `refusal` (Anthropic; its error text is `stop_details.explanation` or "The model refused to complete the request"), `sensitive` (Anthropic safety filter), `content_filter` (OpenAI chat completions and compatible gateways), `incomplete.content_filter` (OpenAI Responses), `content_filtered` / `guardrail_intervened` (Bedrock Converse), `SAFETY` / `PROHIBITED_CONTENT` / `BLOCKLIST` / `SPII` (Google), compared case-insensitively; an Anthropic refusal also carries its category (`AssistantMessage.stopCategory`, §8j). Without a raw stop reason (a re-classification from the flattened string), only the exact texts pi-ai writes for those stops match the whole de-tagged message (`The model refused to complete the request`, `Provider stopped with: <one of the reasons above>`, `Provider finish_reason: content_filter`, `Response incomplete: content_filter`), so "connection refused" or a content filter named inside an HTTP 400 body (still `content`) never match; a free-text Anthropic explanation is detected only through the raw stop reason. Handling:
- **No health strike, no throttle.** The admission wrapper classifies the failure with the raw stop reason and notes it neutral (above).
- **Refusal rules first.** Layer 0 asks the session's refusal controller (`RequestRetryContext.onRefusal`) on every refused attempt: the refusal is classified against the check catalogue and a matching `[[refusal_fallback]]` rule **replaces** the implicit fallover below with a redo on the rule's entry (which may be the model that refused, `@same`), a sticky pin, and its own exhaustion handling (§8j "Hard refusals", "Refusal rules"). The bullets below describe the behaviour with no matching rule. Every refused attempt writes a `refusal_events` row.
- **Never re-sent to the member that refused** (implicit fallover). `RequestAttemptState.refused` holds the health keys that refused this request; `chooseChainMember` (`refused` dep) never picks them, in any pass, and never as the canary or the `all-unhealthy` target while a member that did not refuse remains.
- **Fallover within the call** (no matching rule). At dispatch the resolver records the serving member (`servedKey`) and whether another member could take a refusal right now (`refusalFalloverAvailable`: not refused, healthy, in budget, fits). On a `refusal` verdict Layer 0 adds `servedKey` to `refused` and, when the request allows fallover and the wall-clock budget is not spent, re-issues at once (no backoff) to that member (reason `refusal-fallback`). Otherwise it surfaces the error terminally, tagged `[llm-request:refusal]`: the wall-clock retry loop never re-runs a refusal, interactive or background. A single-member chain (no resolver state) fails on the first refusal.
- **Opt-out.** `RequestRetryContext.refusalFallover` is read once per request; the factory binds it to `CreatedAgent.setRefusalFallover(enabled)` (default on). The session-record turn turns it off (§8i); it disables only the implicit fallover, so a rule naming the `record_turn` site still redoes the turn.
- **Downstream** an unrecovered `refusal` is content-like: a chat session parks `failed-resumable` (failure notice as for content, no auto-retry), a worker-pool run takes the semantic path (§9b) unless a rule was exhausted for it (the job then fails with no output, §8j). A rule exhausted with `on_exhausted = "withhold"` instead ends the request with a synthesized clean `NO_REPLY` turn (`harness: { kind: "refusal_withheld" }`, zero usage). The request ring records the attempt with outcome `error`, class `refusal`.
- **Log.** Every refused attempt logs `llm_refusal` (warn) `{sessionId, timelineKey, sessionType, group, member (served logical id), model (wire id), rawStopReason, explanation (error text, ≤300 chars), attempt, fallover, site, checkCode, reason, subReason, category, rule, outcome, toModel}` (`fallover` = the decision was the implicit fallover), so refusals are visible per model; it is not logged as `llm_request_attempt_failed`.
- **Billed.** Unlike other terminal errors, a refused attempt's usage is captured: pi-ai keeps the request's usage on the refusal error, and when it is non-zero Layer 0 records it on the request ring and fires `onRequestCommitted` with the error message, so the refusing member gets an ordinary `agent_loop` ledger row (§8b, §8f). A refused caption is billed as a `caption` row the same way.

**Recovery is a single probe success** (no anti-flap machinery): a successful probe (background, or a live canary for a model without a prober) flips `X` healthy and all traffic resolves back at once — the 3-failure threshold dampens flapping for free, and prompt-cache retention (~5 min) makes a flip-flop cost-free. A non-head resolution (or a canary) logs one rate-limitable `model_fallback_resolved { consumer, chain, chosen, reason }`. A single-member chain degrades to the bare admitted stream/fetch (no health reads, no log). The **console scheduler view** annotates each unhealthy model with its **logical id(s)** and labels a fallback-bearing model's probe window **"canary pending / in flight"** (vs a no-fallback model's "next probe") — a config-derived `modelHealthAnnotations` map (health key → logical ids + has-fallback, `buildModelHealthAnnotations`) bridges the config-blind snapshot to the names on `GET /api/scheduler`.

**Unified registry + all consumers (spec MODEL-FALLBACK §2.3/§6).** For virtual models and fallback to apply *uniformly*, every consumer resolves its model through `[models.*]` by **name** — the non-agent inference clients (captioning, `image_generate`, `x_search`, remote embedding) no longer define models inline (their `cost`/`provider`/`rate_limit_group`/`fallback` now live on the referenced block; image-gen's per-image charge is `[models.*].cost.per_image`). The agent loop composes the **StreamFn** resolver (`buildModelFallback`); the four raw-fetch clients compose the **fetch-shaped** equivalent (`runFetchWithFallback`) — same per-attempt member selection, scheduler admission, both-axes `noteOutcome`, and canary, but each supplies a per-member fetch. Captioning additionally supplies a per-lane **capability predicate** (`input_modalities` includes the lane's modality — image/video/audio), dropping a fallback member that can't serve the lane; the other three fetch chains are homogeneous by config so they rely on that rather than a predicate. The fetch helper tries each member **at most once per call** (the consumer's own retry layer re-drives across calls, by which point §8a health has shifted), so a single-member chain makes exactly one attempt. Every consumer threads the billed member's **logical id** into its ledger row (§8f) for exact attribution; the paid-tool gates — and captioning's own pre-call gate (so the on-demand x_search/media/danbooru caption lanes refuse too, not just the worker pool) — refuse only when *every* chain member is over budget. (Remote-embedding fallback members must be **vector-compatible** — same `dim` **and** embedding space — since the index/cache keys on the head's wire id; **only `dim` (width) is enforced**, so a same-dim/different-space fallback silently degrades retrieval — an operator-config contract, not enforced because one model has different wire ids across backends.)

---

## 8b. Token-Usage Tracking & Context Limits

The harness tracks **actual** provider-reported token usage per request and per session, persists the session-level aggregate, derives a single cost, and enforces a configurable maximum context size — all on actuals, never on the `gpt-tokenizer` estimate (`token_estimate`, the frozen-prefix estimate, is kept unchanged and clearly separate; it measures a different thing — the artificial seed context — and stays useful for the room preview where no actuals can exist).

### Per-request capture at the Layer-0 commit point

Every `AssistantMessage` carries a pi-ai `Usage` (`input`/`output`/`cacheRead`/`cacheWrite`/`totalTokens` + a `cost` object with per-factor and `total` USD, computed upstream by pi-ai's `calculateCost` from the model descriptor's `cost.*` per-MTok factors). `input` is always *uncached* input across providers; cache-write charging is provider-specific and needs no special-casing (Anthropic, and OpenAI on the Responses API from GPT-5.6, bill cache writes and report `cacheWrite > 0` — the responses provider reads `input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` as of pi-ai 0.80.x; providers that don't charge report `cacheWrite: 0`, and `calculateCost` applies each model's own `cost.cache_write`). Two derived quantities: a request's **prompt size** is `input + cacheRead + cacheWrite`; the **context size after** a request is `totalTokens` (prompt + output), the value the *next* request grows from. Not assumed monotonic (Anthropic strips prior-turn thinking on later requests) — we always report the last observation.

`withRequestRetry` (Layer 0, §8) buffers each attempt to its terminal event and commits only on a clean `done`. That `done` branch is the **single authoritative capture point**: it fires `ctx.onRequestCommitted(message)` (best-effort, exceptions swallowed) and records the usage on the request ring's `done` row. Terminal errors carry stub-zero usage and are never captured (a token-producing attempt that then errors is a known, accepted slight undercount — the data simply does not arrive on error events). The one exception is a **refusal**: the provider's usage does arrive on it, and Layer 0 commits a refused attempt that carries usage through the same `onRequestCommitted` hook (§8a "Refusals"). A request the run aborts is the other exception (below). The observe-only `onAttemptEvent` tap is *not* reused for accounting (it fires for attempts that are later discarded).

### Aborted requests

A request the run aborts (`agent.abort()`: operator Stop, a tool/turn cap, a drain, a redo) after it reached the wire is billed by the provider although its stream reports at most the input usage (Anthropic's `message_start`), never the output produced so far, and nothing at all before the first event or on transports that report usage only at the end. Layer 0 hands such an attempt to `RequestRetryContext.onRequestAborted(info: AbortedRequestInfo): Usage | undefined` once, with the terminal `aborted` message (its reported usage), `firstEventSeen` (any stream event arrived; pi-ai's `start` follows the response headers), `streamedText` (the text, thinking and tool-call argument deltas seen so far, concatenated; collected only when the hook is wired), `streamingMs` (from the first stream event to the abort) and the attempt number. The hook fires only when the caller's signal aborted the attempt: not for a wall-clock stall (environmental, retried), not for an attempt whose signal was already aborted when it started, and not for one aborted while it waited for a scheduler slot (`withSchedulerAdmission` sets `RequestAttemptState.awaitingAdmission` around its acquire, so such a request reached no wire). When the hook is wired it replaces the reported-usage capture of that attempt (one row, never two); an aborted attempt is never retried, and earlier failed attempts of the same request keep their own reported-usage rows. Without the hook the old behaviour holds (reported nonzero usage through `onRequestCommitted`).

The factory binds the hook to `estimateAbortedRequestUsage` (`src/agent/usage.ts`) and then to the **same commit path** as a committed request (`commitRequest(message, estimate)`): reported input, cache-read and cache-write counts are kept; without them the prompt is estimated from the running context counter (§8g) plus the served member's model-prompt tokens, credited as a cache read up to the session's last billed prompt when that prompt was billed within the cache TTL (5 min) by the same cache domain (the served member's health key), the rest uncached input; the output is the largest of the reported output, the primary tokenizer's count of `streamedText`, and a floor of `ABORTED_OUTPUT_TOKENS_PER_SECOND` (20) per second of `streamingMs` (an abort before the first event has output 0): reasoning a model keeps hidden (encrypted, or not streamed) produces no deltas but is billed, and the floor is set low enough to stay under what a model generates in that time; the cost is pi-ai's `calculateCost` over the served member's `[models.*].cost` block. The result feeds `SessionUsageTracker.record` (cost ceiling, `agent_sessions.usage_*`), `budget.record` with `estimated: true` (the `[[limits]]` engine and, through `recordUsageEvent`, the per-user engine and shared pools, exactly like a committed row), and the ring's attempt row (`usage` + `estimated: true`). Under per-user selection an aborted request whose stream started advances the prompt-cache baseline (its prompt was written to the cache), reconciling the running counter only against a reported input; one aborted before its first event leaves the baseline as it was. Log: `llm_request_aborted {sessionId, model, inputTokens, outputTokens, estimated, inputReported, costUsd, firstEventSeen}` (info; `inputTokens` is the whole prompt). Thinking a provider streams only as a summary is still undercounted when it outpaces the floor.

### Session aggregation & persistence

`SessionUsageTracker` (`src/agent/usage.ts`) is a pure in-memory accumulator — one per created agent, owned by the factory, bound as `onRequestCommitted: (msg) => tracker.record(msg.usage)`. It holds cumulative `{llmRequests, inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens, cost}` plus `contextTokens` (the **last** committed request's `totalTokens`, or null before any commit). On resume-in-place the factory seeds it from the persisted row (`CreateAgentOptions.usageSeed`, built by `usageSeedFromRow` in `app.ts`) so a resumed session continues accumulating rather than resetting.

`attachSessionCapture` subscribes `tracker.onUpdate` → `Storage.updateAgentSessionUsage(id, totals, tracker.lastModelId() ?? ctx.model)` (single-writer queue, one write per committed request — negligible at single-digit-to-low-tens requests/session, no debounce), unsubscribed on `detach`. Persistence lives in **denormalized columns on `agent_sessions`** (`llm_requests`, `usage_input_tokens`, `usage_output_tokens`, `usage_cache_read_tokens`, `usage_cache_write_tokens`, `usage_cost` REAL, `context_tokens`; all nullable → a row without committed usage reads "unknown", not zero). The same write also rewrites `model_id` with the **actually-billed** model (via `coalesce`, so a null arg never clobbers a recorded value), making the session's model authoritative per request rather than a placeholder guess. "Actually-billed" means the tracker's own record: `onRequestCommitted` feeds `SessionUsageTracker.record(usage, message.model ?? model.id)` — the **same** expression that stamps the ledger row's `model_id` — and the tracker keeps it as `lastModelId()`. `ctx.model` (the session type's `resolveModelId(sessionType)`, fixed at wiring time) is only the **pre-commit fallback**, used until this run commits its first request. The distinction is load-bearing wherever the served model can differ from the configured one — **model fallback** (§8a) and **per-user model selection** (§8g) both do exactly that — and using `ctx.model` there made a session that ran entirely on a per-user-selected model display the session type's configured model instead, contradicting its own ledger rows. The `session_usage` settle log applies the same precedence, so the log line and the row never disagree; `createPlaceholder` separately **seeds** `model_id` with `resolveModelId(sessionType)` at creation so even a zero-commit session is never blank. (Before this seed was added, the default/proactive chat path left `model_id` NULL — only the worker pools seeded it — so cost-bearing sessions could display no model.) There is **no per-request table** — per-request usage already persists verbatim inside each assistant message in `transcript_json`; the columns are the cheap rollup so list views and future cost queries never parse transcripts, and the request ring covers operator-facing per-attempt diagnostics. Both the chat path and the worker pools attach capture, so all session types are tracked uniformly. At detach, one greppable `session_usage` line is logged with the totals snapshot. These counters track **only** the agent loop's own context-bearing requests; provider calls made *outside* the runner (captioning, the `image_generate` tool) are accounted in a separate lane (§8c) and never enter these columns.

### Context-size limits — one model ceiling, one per-session override, one resolver

`context_window` is **the** model-level context ceiling AND the always-on enforcement base (spec CONTEXT-LIMIT-UNIFICATION). Operators set it deliberately *below* the physical provider window (the shipped 128 000 against this model's ~200 k real window) to stay clear of edge-case degradation/cost. `max_context_tokens` survives **only** on a session type (`agent.session_types.*`) as an artificial, tighter **override**; there is no model-level `max_context_tokens` knob. The **operative per-session ceiling is `min(context_window, session_type.max_context_tokens)`** considering the override only when set (`composeSessionContextCeiling`); since `context_window` is always present, it is **never null — enforcement is always wired**, including for interactive sessions (`default`/`proactive`), which previously resolved to no ceiling.

The ceiling is resolved **once per session** (`AgentSessionFactory.resolveSessionContextCeiling(sessionType)`) and fed to **every** consumer, so no call site reaches for `config.models.*.context_window` independently (the structural fix for the prior split's drift):
1. **Enforcement** — the pre-flight `checkContextBudget` (below).
2. **The pi-ai `Model` descriptor** `contextWindow:` field — fed the resolved operative ceiling (not the raw window), so any future window-keyed mechanism (compaction, SDK overflow math) triggers against the ceiling the session is actually judged against. Inert today (miku uses neither), but the descriptor is honest and the old `?? 128_000` literal fallback is gone.
3. **The text-editor read budget** (`createTextEditorTool({ contextWindowTokens })`, wired in `buildSessionTools(…, sessionType)` from the same resolver) — so a single `view` is sized against the budget it will actually consume. Worker session types build minimal tool sets without the text editor, so this only affects interactive sessions; it is a correctness fix that matters the day an interactive type gets an override or a non-`default` model.

Cross-field validation at app wiring (`validateContextTokenCeilings`) fails fast when a model a session type resolves to has **no `context_window`** (it is mandatory — `default` is always resolvable, plus each session type's own model), or when a session type's `max_context_tokens` exceeds the resolved model's `context_window`. The only legitimate consumer of the *physical* model window is recognizing a provider-side overflow rejection — pattern-matched on the error string (`isContextOverflow`), not a config number; the physical window is intrinsic model metadata, not a config knob.

Enforcement is a **per-request pre-flight** (`RequestRetryContext.checkContextBudget`, evaluated once before the first attempt — every Layer-0 attempt replays the identical context, so per-attempt re-checking is meaningless). When per-user selection is inactive, the factory binds it to compare the tracker's `contextTokens` (the last committed request's actual size) against `fallback.maxOperativeContextWindow` — the **largest** surviving member's operative window. A context that exceeds the head's window but fits a larger fallback member does NOT terminate here; termination fires only when `observed > maxOperativeContextWindow` (no member can serve), logging `session_context_limit_exceeded` (warn, with `membersSkippedOnFits` listing the members whose window the context exceeds) and synthesizing a terminal error classified **`content`**, surfaced through `withRequestRetry` *without consuming retry budget*. When per-user selection IS active, `checkContextBudget` defers entirely — fits are tested per attempt inside `resolveUserSelection` via `chooseChainMember`, and the per-user terminal distinguishes three causes: **budget** (a fitting+healthy member exists but the engine says unaffordable), **context** (no selectable's `maxOperativeContextWindow` accommodates the observed count — `session_context_limit_exceeded` with `contextDenied: true` in `usage_limit_blocked`), or **outage** (fits+in-budget but all healthy members are down). Properties:

- **Actuals only, first request never blocked.** Enforcement uses the provider-reported truth, never the estimate. No actuals exist before the first commit, so the first request is never blocked locally — if a seeded context is already oversized, the provider rejects it and the existing content-class path handles it (now via pi-ai's `isContextOverflow` pattern set, which `classifyLlmError` consults to recognize provider-side overflow rejections from any supported gateway, broader than the old hand-rolled keyword list).
- **Graceful by construction.** The limit only blocks *issuing another request* from an oversized context; an in-flight response always completes, and a session that terminates cleanly (send_message `final:true` / `NO_REPLY` / worker finalize) never fails even if its final response pushed it over.
- **Reuses the content-class path end to end** (no new error class or session status). For interactive sessions the run parks `failed-resumable` (and a manual console resume re-fails the pre-flight deterministically — honest and harmless, no request issued); for worker sessions it routes to the job's semantic-retry path, so a fresh attempt rebuilds context from scratch — exactly the "restart a runaway diary/summary" behavior, bounded by the job's attempt budget.

**Upstream guard: tool-result shaping (§10 "Tool-result shaping").** The §8b enforcement backstop is a last resort. The tool-result shaping layer (§10) is the upstream prevention: it bounds each tool result's text tokens (Layer 1) and the aggregate of all tool results in a turn (Layer 2: `servingWindow − runningContext − reserve`) *before* those results are appended to the context, so a single over-large tool-result batch cannot blow the context in one turn. The floor-overshoot bound (`(N−1) × result_min_tokens`) is the maximum by which the Layer-2 invariant can be exceeded when the per-result floor fires for multiple results in a parallel batch; the §8b enforcement absorbs this. The two guards compose: §10 reduces the frequency of §8b firing; §8b remains the authoritative ceiling.

### Console surfacing

`sessionMeta` adds `llmRequests`, `usage` (the four consumption values + cost, null until first commit), `contextTokens` (actual, last-observed), and `maxContextTokens` (the operative ceiling resolved from **current** config via `factory.resolveSessionContextCeiling`, **not** persisted per session — the console shows today's config). Now that `context_window` is the always-on base, `maxContextTokens` resolves to a non-null number for every session, so the `ctx X / Y` display always shows the `/ limit` denominator (the API field stays nullable for legacy/headless rows). The request ring's `usage` flows through `GET /api/llm-requests` (an aborted attempt's carries `estimated: true`). The session view renders a session-level actuals line (`ctx 46.3k / 80k · in … · out … · cr … · cw … · $… · N req`), the rollout annotates each committed assistant message with its per-request usage (`ctx …` = that request's `totalTokens`; rendered once per message, nothing for messages without real usage — including tentative partials, which have no usage until commit), and the scheduler request table gains `ctx`/`tok`/`cost` columns for `done` rows. Cost renders as `—` when all factors are zero (unconfigured model), never a misleading `$0.00`.

## 8c. Auxiliary (Out-of-Loop) Model Usage

Several model-call paths bypass the agent runner entirely — captioning (`src/captioning`, a detached enrichment worker), the `image_generate` tool (`src/tools/image-gen.ts`, a raw Gemini `:generateContent` fetch), and the `x_search` tool (`src/tools/x-search.ts`, a raw OpenRouter chat-completions fetch to Grok **plus** its inline captions). None flow through `withRequestRetry`'s Layer-0 commit point, so §8b never sees them. Their spend is tracked in a **separate accounting lane** (spec AUXILIARY-USAGE-TRACKING), parallel to §8b and **never merged into it**.

**The §4 invariant.** Auxiliary usage is *never* added to `agent_sessions.usage_*`/`usage_cost`/`context_tokens`. Those stay pure agent-loop actuals: `context_tokens` feeds `max_context_tokens` enforcement, and image-output tokens (billed on a different $/tok scale and not part of the agent's context window) would corrupt that if blended. The lanes are summed only at the presentation layer.

**Shared cost helper.** `computeUsageCost(rates, usage)` in `src/agent/usage.ts` is a pure, I/O-free calculator mirroring pi-ai's `calculateCost` (`rate/1e6 * tokens` per component) plus a flat `perImage * images` term. Both paths import it; the formula lives once, guaranteeing parity with §8b. `CostRates` (USD/1M tokens + optional `perImage`) and `RawTokenUsage` are its shared types. Rates come from config, not a pi-ai model descriptor (these paths never construct one): `[captioning.model].cost` / per-modality `cost`, and `[image_gen.costs.{pro,flash}]` (with `per_image`). Caption rate resolution (`resolveCaptionCost`, `src/captioning/cost.ts`) treats cost as a property of a **specific model** that is never inherited across models: a modality's own `cost` block wins; otherwise `[captioning.model].cost` applies **only when the modality runs the shared model** (no `model.id` override, or the same id). A modality that overrides `model.id` to a *different* model without its own `cost` block has **unknown** cost (untracked) — the shared model's rates are not borrowed for it — and startup logs a `caption_cost_untracked_model_override` warning when top-level pricing is configured (so the gap is visible). Unset/all-zero rates ⇒ usage still captured, cost 0 ("untracked"); usage *absent* (gateway omitted it) ⇒ null ("unknown"), distinct from 0.

**Captioning lane.** Captured in `describeMedia`, priced in the `InferenceClient`, persisted by `updateCaptionResult` into the `media_assets` caption usage columns (§7a) — one durable row already exists per caption job, so usage lives there. Pool aggregates derive by `SUM`/`COUNT` (`getCaptioningUsageAggregate`).

**Tool-use lane.** `image_generate` reads Gemini `usageMetadata` (`parseGeminiUsage`: `promptTokenCount − cachedContentTokenCount → input`, `candidatesTokenCount → output` (the generated image, billed as tokens), `images` = count saved), computes cost from the tier's `[image_gen.costs.*]`, and calls a per-session `recordToolUsage` callback that appends one row to the generic **`tool_invocations` ledger** (`id`, `agent_session_id`, `tool_name`, `tool_call_id`, `model_id`, `provider`, the four token columns, `images`, `cost`, `ref`, `created_at`). The tool is built per-session (`buildSessionTools`), so the factory closes over `agentSessionId` for attribution; the callback enqueues the insert on the single-writer queue, and a sink failure never fails the tool (the image is already saved). One row per billable call; no row when usage is unknown. The per-session rollup is **derived on read** (`getSessionToolUsage`: `SUM`/`COUNT` by `agent_session_id`) — no columns on `agent_sessions`. The ledger is generic over `tool_name`, so any future raw-fetch tool reuses it (spec §13). **`x_search` is the first such reuse**: one row for the Grok call (`parseOpenAiUsage` → `[x_search.cost]` per-MTok, `provider:"openrouter"`, `ref:"grok"`) **and** one per inline caption (`ref:"caption:<statusId>"`, priced by the caption client) — both written through the *same* per-session `recordToolUsage` callback `image_generate` uses (hoisted in `buildSessionTools`). This gives **tool-context captions a durable home for the first time** (previously they computed usage but had nowhere to land), exactly what the generic-over-`tool_name` ledger anticipated. The remaining two tool-context caption lanes reuse it the same way: the **`media` tool** appends one row per captioned item (`tool_name:"media"`, `ref:"caption:<source>"`) and **danbooru**'s non-vision `preview` one row per described post (`tool_name:"danbooru"`, `ref:"caption:<postId>"`) — model/provider/usage/cost from the caption client's `CaptionResponse`, no row when usage is unknown — so every paid tool-context caption lands in the ledger and counts against the §8d per-session cost ceiling.

**Console surfacing.** Captioning: per-item `in · out · cr · $cost` chip in the pipeline item detail, and a pool aggregate (`N captioned · in … · out … · $X spent`) on the captioning pool card. Image-gen: the rollout's `image_generate` tool block carries an `in · out · $cost` chip (ledger rows matched into the transcript by `tool_call_id`), and the session view adds a **second, visually distinct** `tools: N calls · … · $…` line beneath the §8b actuals — the two lanes shown side-by-side, never blended (different pricing currencies; tool tokens are not context-bearing). `x_search`'s Grok + caption rows feed this same line and the `/api/cost-overview` tool lane for free (the ledger is generic over `tool_name`). A global `/api/cost-overview` (`getCostOverview`) sums the three lanes — agent-loop (`Σ agent_sessions.usage_cost`), tool (`Σ tool_invocations.cost`), captioning (`Σ media_assets.caption_cost`) — rendered side-by-side in the pipelines column footer. All reuse `formatTokens`/`formatUsd` (null → "—"; cost hidden when 0). Both `SUM` queries are covered by dedicated single-column indexes (`idx_agent_sessions_usage_cost`, `idx_media_assets_caption_cost`) so each aggregate reads only the compact index rather than the full row (index-only scan).

## 8d. Per-Session Cost Limits

A configurable **USD cost ceiling per session run** that bounds an autonomous session's total spend, counting **both session-scoped lanes**: the §8b agent-loop cost (`SessionUsageTracker.cost`) and this session's §8c tool-use cost (`tool_invocations`, fed by `recordToolUsage`). Captioning is excluded as an input — it is a detached enrichment pool (§7a), not attributable to a session. The §8c §4 invariant holds: the two lanes are summed **only in-memory and at the presentation layer**, never in the persisted `usage_*` columns.

### Combined accounting (in-memory)

`SessionUsageTracker` (§8b) carries the tool lane as a separate `toolCost` field — outside `SessionUsageTotals` (whose shape maps 1:1 to the agent-loop `usage_*` columns), so persistence stays agent-loop-pure. `recordToolCost(cost)` accumulates it; `combinedCost()` returns `totals.cost + toolCost` (the ceiling's enforcement basis). Two notification channels are kept distinct: `onUpdate` (agent-loop `record()` only → the persistence subscription) and `onBudgetChange` (fires on **both** `record()` and `recordToolCost()`, passing `combinedCost()` → the soft-warn watcher). **The tracker is constructed in `app.ts`** (which owns seed computation) and passed into the factory via `CreateAgentOptions.usage`, so the same instance receives both the tool-cost feed (wired into `buildSessionTools`' `recordToolUsage`, alongside the unchanged durable ledger write) and the factory's Layer-0 commits; worker pools/tests that have no tool lane let the factory construct it from the seed. On resume the tool lane is seeded from `getSessionToolUsage(id).cost` (continue mode) or 0 (fresh mode), parallel to the agent-loop `usageSeed`.

### Configuration — global default + per-type override

`[agent].max_session_cost_usd` is the global default; `[agent.session_types.*].max_session_cost_usd` overrides it per type (USD). `AgentSessionFactory.resolveSessionCostCeiling(sessionType)` resolves once per session: the override when set, else the global default, else `undefined` (unlimited). A resolved value of `0` (either level) means **no cap** — so a session type can set `0` to opt out even under a global default. `[agent].cost_warn_fraction` (default 0.8, strictly in (0,1)) is the soft-warn point. Bounds are enforced by the TypeBox schema; cost has no cross-field dependency (unlike the context window), so there is no app-wiring validator. Like the context ceiling, the cost ceiling is operator config, **not persisted per session** (the console shows today's config).

### Two-tier, agent-facing enforcement

A console-only warning is useless for an autonomous session (no operator is watching), so the soft signal is delivered **to the agent**:

1. **Soft threshold → interjection (one-shot).** When `combinedCost()` first crosses `cost_warn_fraction × ceiling`, `wireCostBudgetWarner` (subscribed via `onBudgetChange`) steers a single `<interjection>` into the running agent (`sessions.steer(id, { type: "interjection", content })`, rendered by `convert.ts`), quoting spent-vs-limit and instructing it to wind down (send its final message, avoid further tool calls). A `warned` latch makes it one-shot; logs `session_cost_warn`. No-op when no ceiling resolves. Reaches the model before its next request — including between tool-call rounds of an in-flight `continue()` — so it is effective exactly for the runaway multi-request case. The warner is wired on the **chat launch + resume** paths (interactive + proactive, the sessions that can conversationally wind down and that own the tool-cost lane); **worker-pool sessions** (summary/diary) rely on the hard cap (+ semantic-retry) alone — they have no "send final" affordance and no tool spend.
2. **Hard cap → pre-flight block (backstop).** The factory binds `checkCostBudget` into `withRequestRetry`'s pre-flight (alongside `checkContextBudget`; context is checked first, first violation wins). It compares `combinedCost()` against the ceiling and, on a violation, synthesizes a `content`-class terminal error **without consuming retry budget**, logging `session_cost_limit_exceeded`. The first request is never blocked (combined cost is 0 before any commit/tool call), an in-flight response always completes, and a cleanly-terminating turn never fails. It reuses the content-class path end to end: **interactive** sessions park `failed-resumable` (a manual resume re-fails deterministically once the seeded combined cost reloads); **worker** sessions route to the job's content-class semantic-retry. *Known, accepted imperfection:* a fresh worker attempt is a new session run whose combined-cost counter resets to 0, so total worker spend across retries can reach ~`ceiling × attempts` — chosen for consistency with the context ceiling over introducing a new terminal class.

### Console surfacing

`sessionMeta` adds `maxSessionCostUsd` (resolved from current config via `resolveSessionCostCeiling`; null = unlimited). The session view renders a **combined cost-budget line** — `budget · $0.82 / $1.00 · 82%` — the **only** place the two lanes are summed (`usage.cost` + `toolUsage.cost`); the §8b actuals line and the §8c `tools:` line above keep them separate. The indicator turns destructive at ≥100%. The `session_usage` settle log gains `combinedCost` and `maxSessionCostUsd` (the resolved ceiling, threaded once per run into the capture ctx — from the chat launch/resume wiring, where it is shared with the soft-warn watcher, and equally from the summary/diary worker pools, which have the §2.2 hard cap but no watcher; `null` when unlimited) so the greppable line is self-contained — combined spend next to the ceiling it was measured against, for every session type.

---

## 8e. Period Cost Limits (BudgetEngine)

Configurable **USD budgets over a rolling or calendar window**, enforced across the whole app and **scoped** by any combination of consumer *class*, *session type*, *tool*, and *model*. Distinct from and orthogonal to the §8d per-run ceiling (which caps a single session, no time window): §8d is unchanged, and the per-request pre-flight now evaluates **both**. Source: `src/budget/` (`engine.ts`, `window.ts`, `normalize.ts`, `zero-cost.ts`); enforcement is wired across the factory, the worker pools, the proactive scheduler, and the paid tools.

### Counting model — own-scope only, with layering

Every rule counts **only its own scope**: it sums only the `usage_events` (§8f) matching its selector within its window. A prospective spend is **allowed iff every rule whose selector covers it has headroom** (blocked if **any** covering rule is at/over cap). The "keep summaries/diary running after sessions are suspended" behavior is **not a counting mode** — it is the emergent consequence of layering a narrow rule (e.g. `session_types=[default,proactive]`) under a broad one (`global`, no selector): `default`/`proactive` stop at the narrow cap while `summarize`/`condense`/`diary` keep running until the broad `global` cap halts everything.

**Dependency cascade (structural, in code — not config).** Triggered (`default`) and proactive sessions additionally require their summarization prerequisite to be *available*: admission needs **both** (a) the session's own covering rules have headroom **and** (b) every class it depends on (`summarize`, `condense`) is not blocked. Encoded in `app.ts` as `dependencies` and consumed by `BudgetEngine.checkAdmission`. Diary depends on nothing.

**Zero-cost bypass (`§2.2`).** A model whose *configured* cost rate is zero (`collectZeroCostModelIds` scans every pricing site — agent models, captioning, image-gen tiers, x_search, remote embeddings; a paid appearance in any lane wins) has $0 spend, so `check()` short-circuits to allowed: it can never move or be blocked by a budget rule. The bypass is **budget-only** — zero-cost consumers still obey the dependency cascade. Zero-cost events are still written to the ledger (for token/request counts) but are invisible to the engine.

### The engine

`BudgetEngine` is seeded from the ledger at startup (`SUM(cost_usd)` per rule over its window) and answers admission/pre-flight/tool-gate questions **without a SQL SUM on the hot path**: each rule keeps an in-memory running total + the window's `resetsAt`. `record(event)` (which rejects any non-positive cost — NaN/0/negative — so a stray cost can't poison the total) increments every covering rule (synchronous, called by the ledger recorder before the durable insert). Every read/decision path (`check` / `isClassAvailable` / `ruleStatuses`) and `record` first calls `rollIfNeeded`, which on a passed **calendar** boundary resets that rule's total to **0 in place — no SUM** (a fresh calendar window is empty by construction), so a rule that hit cap yesterday stops reporting blocked the instant the boundary passes rather than lagging up to one tick. A periodic tick (`tickMs`, default 60 s) is the authoritative reconciler: it recomputes rolling windows from the ledger (shedding aged-out spend) and **re-SUMs** a calendar rule when its boundary passes (correcting any drift from the cheap in-place zero). `check(descriptor)` → `{ allowed, blockingRules[], primary }` (primary = earliest-resetting, for the user message); `checkAdmission(sessionType, modelId)` folds in the dependency cascade (it now delegates to `checkAdmissionChain` with the single head logical id; the launch gate calls `checkAdmissionChain` directly with the whole fallback chain so an in-budget fallback admits, spec MODEL-FALLBACK §6.1); `isClassAvailable` checks a session class; `isModelAvailable(logicalId, scope)` requires the consumer spend scope and delegates to the same `check()` matcher for fallback eligibility. All selector dimensions apply together, so an exhausted audit-only rule cannot exclude paid chat models. Agent requests (including refusal pins and mechanical-job reruns) carry class, session type and timeline; paid tools also carry their tool name; caption and embedding clients carry their ledger class without inventing unavailable per-request context. Unscoped wildcard and model caps still apply; `ruleStatuses()` returns one entry per configured rule (never filtered) for the console. A rolling rule's `resetsAt` is only a `now + duration` upper bound on the hot path; **off** the hot path — `ruleStatuses()` (console countdown) and `accurateResetsAt(name)` (the human-facing refusal/defer message) — it is sharpened to `min(contributing ts) + duration` (the instant the oldest contributing spend ages out) via a `minUsageTs` ledger query, so the surfaced "back at X" isn't pinned at the full duration. `logBlocked` emits one structured `usage_limit_blocked` line naming **every** hit rule (the rule `name` is the join key across logs, console, and config).

### Configuration — a centralized `[[limits]]` array

Rules live in one top-level `[[limits]]` array (not per-consumer). Each: `name` (unique), `max_usd` (≥ 0; `0` = no spend allowed for the scope), an optional `reserve_usd` (≥ 0, default 0: the headroom a new spend needs, so the rule blocks once `spent ≥ max_usd − reserve_usd`; the gates only check spend so far, so on a rule over expensive single calls such as `x_search` a reserve of about one call's cost keeps the last admitted call from overshooting the cap far; `reserve_usd ≥ max_usd` warns, the rule always blocks), `window` (`{ type:"rolling", duration:"24h" }` or `{ type:"calendar", period:"day"|"week"|"month", tz? }` — tz defaults to `agent.timezone` then UTC), optional selector dimensions (`classes`, `session_types`, `tools`, `models` — AND across, OR within, omitted = wildcard, none = global), and an optional `trigger_rejection_message` (templated with `{resets_at}`). TypeBox covers shape; cross-field semantics (`normalizeLimits`, called from `app.ts` per the project's cross-field-validation-in-app.ts convention) enforce name uniqueness, a parseable duration, a valid **named** IANA tz (bare offsets rejected), and warn (never fail) on unknown tool/session-type/model-id references (the model warning uses the union of every configured model id, `collectKnownModelIds`; `models` stays free-form) or a `trigger_rejection_message` on a rule that cannot cover a triggered session.

**Agent/account-scoped rules.** Each rule may carry an optional `agent = "<name>"` or `account = "<provider>:<key>"` matcher — never both on the same rule (fatal normalizer error). Absent both = global rule, unchanged behaviour. **In legacy mode** (no `[agents]` table) any rule that sets `agent` or `account` is a fatal startup error. **In agents mode**: `agent` must name a declared `[agents.*]` block; `account` must be a `provider:key` string for a configured account; either validation failure is fatal. At normalization time the matcher resolves to a `timelineKeyPrefixes: string[]` on the `RuleSelector` — for `agent`, the union of all `provider:accountKey` prefixes for accounts mapped to that agent; for `account`, the single `["provider:key"]` pair. `selectorMatches` returns false immediately when the rule carries `timelineKeyPrefixes` but the `SpendDescriptor` carries no `timelineKey` — this is how scoped rules stay silent at gates that lack per-session context (worker-pool claim, proactive admission, paid tool call). At the three gates that do carry `timelineKey` (triggered admission, dependency gate, per-request pre-flight) a scoped rule matches only descriptors whose `timelineKey` starts with one of its prefixes followed by `:`.

### Enforcement points (six gates)

| Gate | Anchor | Behavior when blocked |
|---|---|---|
| Triggered admission | `launchSession` (`app.ts`) | Do not spawn; mark discarded, drain the next queued trigger. A human trigger posts the templated `trigger_rejection_message` (if a covering rule supplies one); proactive is silent. Not queued. **Chain-aware (spec MODEL-FALLBACK §6.1):** `launchSession` resolves the session type's whole fallback chain (`factory.resolveModelChainLogicalIds`) and admits when **any** member is in-budget (`BudgetEngine.checkAdmissionChain`), so a model-scoped cap on the primary does not refuse a session an in-budget fallback could serve; a wildcard rule covers every member and still refuses. **The dependency cascade is chain-aware too:** a prerequisite (summarize/condense) is judged unavailable only when **every** member of *its* chain is over budget (`BudgetEngine.resolveModelChainLogicalIds`, wired to `factory.resolveModelChainLogicalIds`), so a model-scoped cap on a prerequisite's head (e.g. summarization on GLM) does not refuse a dependent reply the prerequisite could still produce on a fallback (DeepSeek) — only a cap covering the prerequisite's whole chain refuses. |
| Proactive admission | `ProactiveScheduler` `budgetDeferUntil` | Clamp next-eligible to `max(normal_schedule, resets_at)` — wait out the window rather than post into a refusal. |
| Worker pools | summary/diary/caption/embed claim gate | Pool stops *claiming* while its class is blocked; resumes on the next poll after reset (parked, nothing dropped). On pause each pool emits one rate-limited (≤1/min) `usage_limit_blocked` (gate `worker_claim`) naming the hit rules. All four gates are **chain-aware (spec MODEL-FALLBACK §6):** a lane parks only when **every** member of its fallback chain is over budget (mirroring the image-gen/x_search `chain.some` tool gates), so a head-only model-scoped cap lets the per-attempt resolver fall to an in-budget fallback instead of stalling the pool. **summary/diary** serve multiple `agent_loop` session types (summarization does `summarize` + `condense`), so their `shouldPause` closures — built in `app.ts` *after* the engine exists — use `makeAgentLoopChainClaimGate`, which parks if **any** lane is stuck where a lane is a session type that can progress iff **any** member of its own chain (`factory.resolveModelChainLogicalIds`, head-first logical ids the `[[limits]].models` rule matches) has headroom; the head's upstream id rides along for provenance, an unresolvable type contributes no lane and never parks. **caption/embed** each gate a single chain: they park only when **every** chain member is over budget. **caption** gates on the pool itself (`CaptionWorkerPool.shouldPauseForBudget` reads `budget.engine` + the resolved caption chain `captionModelIds` at call time, `chain.some` over `check`, carrying its own rate-limited-log pattern); **embed** is the retrieval subsystem's `shouldPause`, the shared `makeChainClaimGate` over the resolved `embeddingChain` with a **late-bound engine source** (`() => budget.engine`) because the subsystem is constructed *before* the engine — it resolves the engine per call and never parks while undefined, so the embed lane is genuinely bounded once startup completes. |
| Dependency gate | triggered/proactive admission | Additionally require the summarization prerequisite (`summarize`/`condense`) to have chain headroom — unavailable only when **every** member of its chain is over budget (`checkAdmissionChain`'s dependency loop, chain-aware; see Triggered admission above). |
| Per-request pre-flight | `checkCostBudget` (`factory.ts`) | `check({class:'agent_loop',…})` after the §8d ceiling; over budget → a `content`-class terminal error (no retry burn), same path §8d uses. |
| Paid tool call | `image_generate` / `x_search` `checkBudget` | Returns a tool **error result** (not a throw) naming the limit + reset, before the paid call (x_search gates only the live call, never a cache hit). The agent sees it and adapts. |

**Two gate approximations to note.** Both are model-dimension simplifications; the *ledger* always records the true per-event model, so spend is attributed exactly even where the gate checks a stand-in:

- **Per-tool gate checks only the tool's primary model.** The paid-tool gate (`makeToolBudgetGate`, `src/budget/engine.ts`) checks `{class:"tool", tool, modelId, timelineKey}` against the **one** model id the tool passes; `timelineKey` is the calling session's, so agent/account-scoped rules (`agent = …`) match tool calls too — without it a scoped rule never matches — for `x_search`, the resolved Grok model (`config.model`/`deep_model`), and only on the live call (a cache hit is free and ungated). But `x_search` also captures **inline-caption** rows, priced under the *caption* model and recorded with `class:"tool"`, `tool:"x_search"`. Those rows are therefore governed by any rule whose selector covers `tools=["x_search"]`, `classes=["tool"]`, or the caption model under `models` — **not** by the x_search gate's model dimension (which only ever names the Grok model). A rule meant to cap x_search's caption spend specifically must target one of those, not the Grok model id.
- **Caption pool gates on a representative chain.** `captionModelIds` is the resolved fallback chain (logical ids) of the representative caption model ref (`captioning.model ?? image ?? video ?? audio`), while capture records the true per-modality model (`result.logicalModelId`). The gate parks only when **every** chain member is over budget, so a model-scoped cap on the head still lets the per-attempt resolver fall to an in-budget fallback (the pool keeps claiming); a zero-cost member short-circuits `check` to allowed, so the chain is "available" and the pool never pauses on that member. (The per-request pre-flight and the ledger are unaffected; this is only the pool's coarse claim gate.) The chain is the representative ref's only — a paid *non-representative* modality over its own budget is still governed by the per-attempt resolver + ledger, not this coarse gate.

Free enrichment (link previews, fxtwitter, ingestion) is unaffected. **Reset & resume:** background work parks and resumes by not-claiming; proactive clamps; human triggers get an immediate refusal (re-trigger later); in-session tool calls error at call time with the reset ETA; global exhaustion halts everything that spends while ingestion + free enrichment continue.

## 8f. Unified `usage_events` Ledger

A single append-only table (`usage_events`, schema **v25**) is the source of truth for all cross-cutting usage queries — the BudgetEngine seed/recompute (§8e) and the console "Usage & Cost" page (§11). One row per **billable event** across six classes: `agent_loop` (one row per committed request, at the `onRequestCommitted` hook — additive to the §8b `agent_sessions.usage_*` aggregate), `tool` (at `recordToolUsage`, **additive** to the §8c `tool_invocations` write, which is retained for its `tool_call_id` transcript-annotation link), `caption` (at the caption worker's persist funnel, alongside `media_assets.caption_*`), `embedding` (the remote provider only — §9d; local embeddings are zero-cost and emit nothing), `decision` (one row per billed decision-model attempt, `tool_name` = the decision point, `ref` = the dated served model id — §8h), and `audit` (the offline audit worker's decision calls, `tool_name = "audit"`, never metered against a payee; `[[limits]].classes` accepts `"audit"` — §9i). Refused agent-loop attempts are ordinary `agent_loop` rows of the refusing member (§8a "Refusals"); a request the run aborted is an `agent_loop` row with `estimated = 1` (schema v30; null on every other row; `UsageEventInput.estimated?: boolean`), its usage estimated as §8b "Aborted requests" describes, and it counts toward every limit like any other row (`GET /api/usage/tool-calls` returns `estimated` as a boolean). Agent-loop rows also carry `system_prompt_hash` (§8k). `model_id` (the **upstream wire id**) is always present, alongside `logical_model_id` (the **config block name**; schema **v30**, spec MODEL-FALLBACK §2.2) — distinct so virtual models that share an upstream are budgeted/grouped separately while health keys on the shared wire id. The agent loop stamps the chain member actually billed (so a request that fell to `Y` is attributed to `Y`); other lanes default `logical_model_id` to `model_id`. The `[[limits]].models` selector and the zero-cost bypass key on `logical_model_id` (v30 backfills it `= model_id` for legacy rows); the console "Usage & Cost" **by-model** grouping (the summary card + timeseries chart) instead keys on `model_id` — the upstream wire id actually billed — so real-model spend is reported as one row regardless of which virtual/logical block routed it (a virtual model such as `default` does not appear as its own bucket, and legacy rows predating the logical-id column collapse into the same real model rather than splitting by column semantics). The **session** attribution columns (`agent_session_id`/`session_type`/`trigger_sender_id`) are null for background (caption/embedding) events — but `caption` rows still carry `timeline_key` (the asset's room, recovered via the caption claim's `event_id → timeline_events` join) and `provider` (from `[captioning.model].provider`), so caption spend stays room-attributable. `cost_usd` defaults 0 so a zero-rate free-model event still records its token/request counts while staying invisible to the engine (§8e zero-cost bypass).

The §8b/§8c **storage invariant is preserved**: per-lane spend still lands in its own columns; `usage_events` is an *additional* unified write, never folded back. A single `recordUsageEvent` (`app.ts`) is the fan-in for every billable event — it increments the engine in memory (synchronous, authoritative) then appends the durable row (best-effort; a ledger failure never fails the underlying work, and the engine re-seeds from the ledger on the next tick / restart). The `usage_events` table is part of the genesis schema (`USAGE_EVENTS_SCHEMA`). Storage exposes `insertUsageEvent` (which rejects a non-finite or negative `cost_usd` at the door — a code-level guard, not a DDL `CHECK`), `sumUsageCost(filter)` (the engine's seed/recompute; the result is `Number.isFinite`-clamped as defense-in-depth), `minUsageTs(filter)` (earliest contributing `ts` for the accurate rolling-reset ETA, §8e), and the console aggregations `getUsageSummary` / `getUsageTimeseries` / `getUsageRecentSessions` / `getUsageRecentToolCalls` / `getUsageLeaderboard` (a humans-only spend ranking attributed by `trigger_sender_id`, **plus** a separate system/self actor breakdown — Summarization/Diary/Proactive — attributed by `session_type` so the spend split across the synthetic `system` sender and null-sender tool rows is captured whole; each carded entry carries its own per-bucket series, and the result also returns `userStats` mean/median over the non-zero humans; §7.1 leaderboard tab).

**Agent/account-scoped rule seeding (§8e).** A scoped rule's `RuleSelector.timelineKeyPrefixes` flows into `UsageCostFilter.timelineKeyPrefixes` at seed and recompute time, generating `(timeline_key LIKE 'provider:accountKey:%' OR …)` WHERE clauses so each `SUM(cost_usd)` counts only rows whose `timeline_key` is owned by that rule's agent or account. SQLite LIKE on NULL evaluates to NULL (false), so `embedding` lane rows — which always carry a NULL `timeline_key` — are excluded from every scoped rule's seed with no extra predicate. Global rules (no `timelineKeyPrefixes`) are unaffected. No new column is added to `usage_events`; attribution is derived at read time from the existing `timeline_key` column. `record(event)` stamps `timelineKey: event.timelineKey ?? undefined` on the in-memory `SpendDescriptor` so the running total is also scoped correctly at check time.

**Remote-embedding cost (§9d).** The remote embedding provider captures `usage.prompt_tokens` from the response (else estimates from input chars ÷ a configured `chars_per_token`, default 4), prices it at the configured `cost_per_mtok`, and emits a `class='embedding'` row. Local (zero-cost) embeddings emit nothing and run unconditionally.

**Per-user-limits columns (§8g).** `usage_events` carries four nullable columns, written only for the human agent loop (null for every other lane): `requested_model_id` — the **requested** virtual model the per-user selector chose (distinct from `logical_model_id`, the *served* chain member, under active fallback), so a sub-cap scoped to `opus-premium` still counts an outage backup of that model; `budget_partition` — the **first** rendered **shared-pool** key (a literal like `staff`/`public`, or `room:<id>`/`space:<id>`/`hs:<server>`) the event belongs to, denormalized because pool membership is a cascade outcome irreducible from intrinsic columns (an event joining **2+** distinct pools spills the remaining keys to the `usage_event_partitions` child table below); `room_id` — the bare Matrix room id derived from `timeline_key` at insert (`roomIdFromTimelineKey`), the sturdy room-scoped seed for room-matched per-user counters + per-room pools; and `space_id` — the canonical parent space id, resolved + frozen at admission (§11), supplied by the per-user recorder from the frozen ctx (it cannot be derived from intrinsic columns). Five seed indexes back them (`idx_usage_events_sender_ts`, `_partition_ts`, `_requested_model_ts`, `_room_ts`, `_space_ts`). `UsageCostFilter` gains `triggerSenderIds` / `partitionKeys` / `roomIds` / `spaceIds` / `requestedModelIds` (the last folds in null-requested legacy rows via a `logical_model_id` fallback) — the seed/recompute filters of the §8g meters. `Storage.listUsageIdentities({ since, includeRoom, includeSpace })` returns the `DISTINCT` `(sender, room?, space?)` identities present since a timestamp (non-null sender), the enumeration `UserLimitEngine.seedFromLedger()` replays to re-materialize meters at startup (§14).

**Overlapping shared pools (`usage_event_partitions`, schema v4).** A rule may declare **several** shared pools at once (e.g. a per-space cap *and* a global fleet cap) — an event then belongs to more than one model-agnostic pool simultaneously, which the single `budget_partition` column cannot hold. The store denormalizes the **first** pool key on that scalar (the unchanged fast-path — per-user-only and single-pool events write nothing extra) and **spills each additional membership** to a `without rowid` child table `usage_event_partitions(event_id, partition_key, ts, cost_usd, requested_model_id, room_id, space_id, timeline_key)` (index `idx_uep_partition_ts on (partition_key, ts)`), one row per overflow `(event, pool)`, carrying the seed-relevant columns denormalized so the reseed needs no join back. A shared-pool meter re-seeds by **UNION ALL** of its scalar-column matches (`usage_events.budget_partition`) and its child matches (`usage_event_partitions.partition_key`), each windowed and requested-model/room/space filtered identically, plus the `timeline_key` prefix filter when the pool belongs to an agent- or account-scoped rule (`timeline_key` was added to the child table in v21 and back-filled from the parent rows; before that, such a rule failed startup with `no such column: timeline_key`) (`poolReseedUnion` in `database.ts`); since a given `(event, key)` pair lives in exactly one half, the union never double-counts. This is purely additive — a pool's pre-v4 spend stays on the scalar column and the scalar half of the union finds it unchanged, so **no back-fill** is needed. The recorder stamps the full model-aware key set for **both** the agent loop and the tool lane in one place (`recordUsageEvent` → `UserLimitEngine.sharedPoolKeys`, which mirrors `record` coverage: model-agnostic pools always, a model-scoped shared sub-cap only when the requested model is in scope, so the tool lane never joins a sub-cap — issue #14). The `normalizeUserLimits` cap is `MAX_SHARED_POOLS_PER_RULE = 8` distinct shared partitions per rule, bounding the per-event child-write amplification (≤ N−1 extra inserts). The in-memory metering engine is unchanged — it already meters every covering constraint independently; overlapping pools were only ever a ledger-durability gap.

---

## 8g. Per-User Cost Limits & Model Selection

`UserLimitEngine` (`src/budget/user-limits.ts`) is a sibling to the §8e `BudgetEngine` that gates **only the human-triggered agent loop and its tools** (never background/proactive). It adds per-user spending bounds *and* per-user model selection/degradation over the unified ledger, off by default (an absent/empty `[[user_limits]]` array = feature off, zero behavior change). It is a **separate mechanism** from §8e — partitioned counters, a per-field cascade, a selection action, and a narrower enforcement surface — and the two never merge into one rule list. Spec: `spec/PER-USER-LIMITS.md` (IMPLEMENTED — `user`/`room`/`space` matching all shipped; only user model *choice* (§4.3) is deferred). `[[user_limits]]` rules also support the same optional `agent`/`account` matchers as `[[limits]]` (see §8e): normalization validates and resolves them identically, storing `timelineKeyPrefixes` on `NormalizedUserLimitRule`; `resolve(ctx, timelineKey?)` filters out scoped rules when called with a `timelineKey` that does not match their prefixes; scoped constraints carry a distinct `meterKey` identity from global constraints over the same dimensions (the `timelineKeyPrefixes` are included in the JSON key tuple).

**Three orthogonal layers.** *Budget* — a user's bound is a **set of constraints** `{ models?, window, max_usd, partition }`, **ANDed** (allowed only if it fits under every covering constraint). A constraint with no `models` is the **fungible total** ("≤ $5/day on anything"); one scoped to `models = [...]` is a **sub-cap** that only *carves* the total — its sole purpose is to reserve headroom for cheaper continuation (degradation). Multiple windows are first-class (daily **and** monthly = two constraints). *Estimation* — overshoot is bounded by **capping, not prediction**: before each request the engine sizes `max_tokens` to what the remaining headroom can pay for (`max_output = floor((remaining − input_cost) / output_price)`), priced at the **requested** model's face cost. The input is the **exact** running context — the factory maintains it incrementally, tokenizing each new live message of `agent.state.messages` exactly once with the §9 primary tokenizer, applying the same `isLiveRuntimeMessage` filter the wire context uses so the counter never charges a message the wire drops. Image blocks in the live slice are charged a **flat per-image cost** (`estimateLiveSliceTokens` — `PER_IMAGE_TOKEN_ESTIMATE`, 1600, an upper bound on what providers bill per image), never their serialized base64: tokenizing the raw JSON counted every base64 character (~1 token per ~3 chars — one 200KB screenshot ≈ 100k phantom tokens), so a single image-bearing tool result (browser screenshots, `read_image`, `image_gen`, …) pushed the counter past every model's operative window and the Gate-B fits check terminated healthy rollouts at a real context far below any ceiling. The seed is the build estimate for a fresh launch and, for a **resume** (where no context is built), the resumed baseline — the last committed request's actual context size (`usage.snapshot().contextTokens`), falling back to the summed snapshot+transcript token estimates — so a resumed/recovered session's first request is capped on its real accumulated context rather than a 0-token baseline. After **every committed request** the counter additionally **reconciles to that same actual** (`onRequestCommitted` snaps the running estimate to the committed request's `totalTokens` before advancing the prompt-cache baseline), so estimator error is bounded to a single inter-commit window instead of accumulating monotonically over a rollout — the committed assistant turn lands in `state.messages` after the hook, so its re-estimate briefly overlaps the output already inside the actual (one turn's output, conservative), erased at the next commit. Within the prompt-cache TTL (`PROMPT_CACHE_TTL_MS`, ~5 min) the prior prompt is priced at `cache_read` and only the new material at `cache_write`, otherwise cache-write throughout (conservative). The cache-read credit is additionally **scoped to the upstream cache domain**: a prompt cache lives at the (endpoint, wire-model) pair that served the request, so the commit hook stamps the served chain member's health key (`baseUrl::model-id`) as the baseline's domain, and the pre-flight credits the within-TTL discount only to a candidate whose predicted serving member (the same `chooseChainMember` probe that decides viability) has that same health key — any other candidate is priced as a cache miss even inside the TTL, because its upstream holds no cached prefix and the request would otherwise be under-priced at the cache-read rate, admitted past the user's caps, then billed at full cache-miss price. The estimate also reserves the **additive extended-thinking budget** the provider bills on top of the issued `max_tokens` (`additiveThinkingBudgetTokens` — non-adaptive Anthropic + Google/Gemini are additive at the pi-ai per-level budgets minimal 1024 / low 2048 / medium 8192 / high 16384; adaptive Anthropic Opus/Sonnet 4.6+ and the OpenAI effort path add nothing) so the issued base cap = `affordable_output − thinking_budget` and the post-provider wire `max_tokens` never exceeds the authorized output. Anthropic adaptivity is read from the model config's `adaptive_thinking` flag when set (`true` ⇒ reserve 0, `false` ⇒ the flat additive budget); unset falls back to a hardcoded id heuristic (Opus 4.6/4.7, Sonnet 4.6), so **declare `adaptive_thinking = true` for adaptive Anthropic models newer than that list** (e.g. Opus 4.8+) — otherwise the heuristic mis-classifies them as non-adaptive and reserves a phantom budget that can spuriously deny a within-budget user. A model whose affordable output (text portion, after reserving thinking) falls below `viable_min` (`agent.user_limit_min_output_tokens`, default 256) is **unaffordable**. *Selection* — among the models a user can currently afford, the picker chooses one; degradation is automated selection over the affordable set (the only place an order lives, isolated so a future user-choice picker is a drop-in swap).

**The partition template (§3.5)** generalizes the per-user counter to shared pools.
