Each constraint carries a `partition` string rendered from the trigger ctx — `{user_id}` (default; seeds off `trigger_sender_id`), or a literal (`staff`) — plus provider-scoped vars: `{channel_id}` / `{room_id}` (canonical / alias for the channel/room id), `{server_id}` / `{space_id}` (canonical / alias for the guild/space id), `{homeserver}` (Matrix-only; resolves to the MXID's homeserver suffix, empty for non-Matrix providers; `normalizeUserLimits` warns at config-load when `{homeserver}` is used but the Matrix provider is not enabled). The counter is keyed per `(rendered key, model-scope, window, room-scope, space-scope)`. The **matcher** (`user`/`room`/`space` globs, OR within a dimension, AND across; `space` matches if **any** parent space matches — a room may belong to several) scopes *whose* spend a rule counts; the **partition** scopes *which meter* it shares. **Space matching (§11)** extends `matrix-core`'s `MatrixChannelInfo` with `parent_space_ids` (all spec-legitimate parents — Reciprocal over WithPowerlevel, best-first — via the NAPI `channelInfo`), resolved + frozen on the session at admission **only when a rule references space** (`UserLimitEngine.usesSpace`, so space-less deployments pay no lookup); the canonical (first) parent is the `{space_id}` partition value + the denormalized `space_id` ledger column. A constraint whose partition renders to a value common to several users is a **group budget**: ANDed with each user's personal constraints, so when the shared pool binds, every member fails affordability on the premium model *at once* and **degrades together** rather than the agent being denied. A shared-pool constraint whose partition **variable resolves empty** (e.g. `space:{space_id}` on a space-less room — no parent space) keys no meaningful meter, so `resolveConstraint` **skips it entirely** (mirroring how an empty `space` *match* skips the rule); space-less rooms are **not** pooled together under a bare `space:` bucket, and the rule's fungible total / other non-empty constraints still apply. A rule may declare **multiple** shared pools (up to `MAX_SHARED_POOLS_PER_RULE`): each event's first pool key is denormalized on `budget_partition` and any additional keys spill to the `usage_event_partitions` child table, reseeding via the scalar+child union (see the ledger §8f note above); per-user meters reseed off `trigger_sender_id`. A malformed partition template (a lone unmatched `{`/`}`) is a normalizer **fatal** — it can never silently degrade to a literal global pool.

**Cost identity under fallback (§7): gate on virtual, count actual, estimate on face.** A sub-cap scoped to `opus-premium` owns all spend under that assignment regardless of fallback — so the per-user counters scope on the **requested** model (`requested_model_id`), the cost summed is the **actual served** cost, and the estimate prices the **requested head's** face cost (conservative, since chains are non-increasing in cost). This is why per-user selection stays a distinct axis from the MODEL-FALLBACK outage chain: an outage of `opus-premium` first fails over within its own chain (same-tier alternate), and the per-user preference order only catches it as a last resort once the inner chain is exhausted.

**A sub-cap bounds agent-loop model SELECTION only — never tool usage of the same upstream model.** Tool spend has no requested model, so it counts the user's fungible **total** and any shared **pool** (both model-agnostic) but is excluded from every model-scoped sub-cap — both in memory (`recordUsageEvent` passes no coverage model for a `class = 'tool'` event, so `UserLimitEngine.record` skips sub-caps) and in the ledger reseed (the `requestedModelIds` null-fallback in `usageCostClauses` is gated to `class = 'agent_loop'`, so a null-requested tool row never seeds a sub-cap). The consequence is deliberate: once a user exhausts their sub-cap on model X, the agent loop degrades **off** X (the sub-cap's purpose — reserving cheaper-continuation headroom), but tools hardwired to X (e.g. `x_search`→Grok) keep using X, bounded only by the user's total / pools. Charging a sub-cap for tool spend that merely shares a model name would be an over-restriction footgun (it does not serve the sub-cap's degradation-headroom purpose). Attribution is preserved regardless: a tool row keeps its own `model_id`/`logical_model_id` for §8e per-model aggregates and console top-models, and still draws down the total (by sender) and pools (by partition). A `decision` row (§8h) is metered exactly like a tool row: it has no requested chat model, so `recordUsageEvent` passes no coverage model and it draws down the payee's total and pools, never a sub-cap.

**Enforcement.** *Gate A* (`resolveUserLimitGate`, before the §8e gate): build `ctx = { userId, roomId }` from `inbound`, resolve the per-field cascade (the model-budget block cascades atomically; `trigger_rejection_message` independently), refuse a banned / fully-out-of-budget user with the optional templated reply (richer tokens than §8e: `{display_name}` from the inbound sender, `{limit}`/`{window}`/`{resets_at}`/`{resets_in}`), pick the initial model (so §8e gates on the **selected** model's chain, not the default), freeze the resolution on the session, and tighten the §8d ceiling to `min(static, user-total-headroom)`. Gate A is shared by **every** human agent-loop entry point — a fresh launch (`launchSession`), a reply / follow-up **resume** (`runResumeSession`), and the manual console **recovery** of a parked session (`resumeSessionRun`) — because a resume is the same event from the per-user view (same replying user/room/budget), merely continuing an existing session; only proactive/background paths skip it. *Gate B* (`checkCostBudget`, per request inside `factory.create`): the factory builds **one `BuiltModelFallback` per preferred model** at create; before every request the resolver re-picks the first model satisfying **affordable ∧ healthy ∧ fits** (each a cheap per-model check — affordability vs the live partitioned counter, health via `chooseChainMember` over the model's own chain, fits vs its operative context window), stashes it + the budget-derived `max_tokens` for the outer-selector `StreamFn`, and terminates (content-class, no retry burn) only when **no** preference qualifies — so budget *and* outage degradation both happen transparently mid-rollout instead of guillotining the session. When the capability pre-filter empties the whole preference set (an image-bearing trigger whose **reply model** ships pixels, §8a, against an all-text-only user model set — so no preferred model can serve the pixels), that is itself a **terminal per-user content-class deny** (spec §4.2) — never a fall-through to the ungated session-type default; the session still launches so per-user counting and the §8d ceiling apply, but the first request denies. The initial pre-pick also seeds a **defensive `max_tokens`** on the first selection (the first model's affordable cap at a ≈0-context estimate, mirroring Gate A) so that even if the per-request pre-flight throws — `withRequestRetry` swallows it — request 1 ships capped rather than uncapped. A budget-capped (`stopReason: "length"`) turn is **failed, not delivered** (§5.4): its real spend is recorded, then `request-retry.ts`'s `onBudgetTruncation` hook re-selects the next-cheaper model and re-issues — discarding the truncated content so the rollout finishes a *complete* turn on the degraded model instead of shipping a half answer (the re-drive is bounded by the preference-set size and wired only for per-user sessions; a `length` stop is read as a budget cap vs a legitimate long answer by comparing the issued cap against the **requested** model's own `max_tokens` — not the served fallback member's — and a stop at the requested model's full `max_tokens`, or with no cheaper model left, is delivered normally). Recording is centralized in `recordUsageEvent`: it increments every covering meter (agent loop **and** tool lane) for the session's frozen resolution, keyed on the requested model, by the actual cost — live for fresh, resumed, and recovered sessions alike.

**Refusal pin (§8j).** A session pinned by a refusal redo leaves per-user selection: Gate B checks only the pinned model's affordability (an unaffordable pin ends the session content-class with `usage_limit_blocked {cause: "budget", pinnedModel}`), the preference list and routed cascade are not consulted again, the requested model recorded on its ledger rows is the pin, its output is capped at the pin's affordable `max_tokens`, and a budget truncation is accepted rather than re-driven. A rule entry is usable under per-user selection only when affordable at that moment.

**Meter seeding (§14).** Per-user meter keys depend on the runtime trigger sender / room / parent space, so — unlike the fixed `[[limits]]` rule set `BudgetEngine` seeds in its constructor — they can't be enumerated from config. `UserLimitEngine.seedFromLedger()` (run once at startup before `start()`, wired in `app.ts`) instead reads the distinct spend identities present in the current windows (`Storage.listUsageIdentities` — non-null `trigger_sender_id` only, `DISTINCT` narrowed to the room/space dimensions any rule actually uses via `usesRoom`/`usesSpace`) and **replays each through the same `resolve()`→`meterFor()` path the live gates use**, so the meterKey/seed logic is identical (no drift) and each meter re-sums its true accumulated spend. Zero-spend meters (an unused sub-cap, a cap-0 ban) are then pruned — only *consumed* budget is pre-materialized; enforcement is unaffected (bans still gate at `resolve`, not from a meter). Seeding (and the grouped console view) also **skip non-human senders** via `isEnforceableUser` — a partition is only surfaced when the injected `isUserIdentity` predicate accepts the sender id (today: `id.startsWith("@")`, the Matrix-only case) AND it is not one of the agent's own account ids (`selfUserIds`, built from `config.matrix.accounts` at startup — the provider `getSelf()` API is not available at this pre-`start()` seeding point, so the Matrix config remains the authoritative source for the self-id set here). Per-user limits govern only human triggers that pass Gate A; proactive / background / self / system sessions skip it (§8g) and never `record` to a per-user meter at runtime, so the bot's own account and non-MXID system senders (e.g. `"system"`) must not appear as rate-limited "users" — the seed's ledger re-sum would otherwise re-materialize them. The one gap: a shared pool whose window spend is exclusively autonomous (no human trigger, e.g. proactive-only) re-materializes on the next human turn that resolves it, not at startup. Without this seed a partition partially consumed before a restart read $0 until a live turn lazily re-created its meter.

**Console (§14).** `GET /api/usage/budgets` stays a small always-polled payload: the §8e `rules` **and** `userSelections` (each live per-user session's currently-selected model) — both few. The **unbounded** per-user / shared-pool meters move to a **paginated, grouped** endpoint so the view scales to any number of users: `UserLimitEngine.groupedStatuses()` folds every materialized meter into partition groups, splits them into **individuals** (👤 per-user) vs **shared pools** (👥), and sorts each side **hottest-first** (worst state, then peak fill, then key — the *same* order the client's `buildLadder` renders in, so a page is a contiguous top-slice); `GET /api/usage/user-limits?scope=individuals|shared&page=N` returns one page (all meters for the page's partitions, `USER_LIMITS_PAGE_SIZE = 20` **groups** per page) plus both scope counts (`totals`, for the tab badges + pager). The "Per-user limits" section renders a **scope tab** (Individuals / Shared pools) over partition **strips** (`console/src/lib/user-ladder.ts`, pure + unit-tested): one strip per partition, each cap its own bar. A user strip's header renders the sender as **"Display Name (handle)"** — the handle is the Discord unique username when resolved, else the raw partition key (for Matrix the key IS the human-meaningful MXID) — truncating long names with the full label + raw id on a hover tooltip; the labels ride on the meters (BFF-resolved per page via `Storage.getUserLabels`, see the endpoint table) and a sender with no known name falls back to the bare id exactly as before. The live `userSelections` chips carry the same labels. A **single-model** cap is a **health-colored** bar (green/amber/red by its own fill; an over-cap bar clamps to 100% and labels the true `>100%`) — the red bar *is* the exhausted cap. A **composite** cap (≥2 models, e.g. `sol + terra`) is a **segmented** bar so its composition stays visible — one slice per member (per-member spend read from the sibling single-model caps), colored from a **non-health palette** (blues/purples/teals) so model identity never masquerades as health; the composite's own fill health shows via its percent label. Caps order by `orderIndex`, the backend's **preference-order key** (`ResolvedConstraint.orderKey` = `maxPrefIndex*1000 + memberCount` over the rule's `models` list) — singles at their model's preference position, a composite right after its last member (e.g. `sol, terra, sol + terra, glm`), **not** by fill % or authored constraint index. There is deliberately **no per-user aggregate state badge** — a maxed sub-cap means "degrade to the next tier", not "user blocked", so a single worst-of badge (over a bar showing a different cap) misleads; each cap speaks for itself. The tab + `Prev`/`Next` pager change the query's scope/page so each slice refetches. The **global `[[limits]]`** section reuses the same composite treatment: a multi-model rule (e.g. `openai-56-daily` = `sol,terra`) carries a per-model breakdown in `RuleStatus.components` (a ledger `sumUsageCost` per constituent model, off the hot path in `ruleStatuses`), which the console renders as the identical segmented bar + color legend (`buildSegments`, shared). Meters are ledger-seeded at startup (above), so a partition partially consumed before a restart shows immediately rather than reading $0. A refused human trigger emits `usage_limit_blocked` with a `gate: "user_admission" | "user_preflight" | "user_resume"` discriminator.

---

## 8h. Decision Models

A **decision model** returns typed, calibrated answers over options the caller defines (`choice`, `score`, `noul`), in a few hundred milliseconds, at a fraction of a cent per call. It cannot write text. MikuSwarm uses it at a few *decision points* where today's code chooses among options by heuristic. Everything here is **off by default**: a deployment without `[decisions]` never constructs a client and behaves exactly as before. Source: `src/decisions/`. Design record: spec DECISION-MODEL.

### Wire API: `api = "system-one"`

A decision model is an ordinary `[models.*]` block with `api = "system-one"`. Its `endpoint` is the **full URL** of the decisions route (OpenRouter's, a gateway's, a vendor's native one, or a self-hosted server), its `id` is the pinned model id, and its `cost` block states the real per-token prices. The request body is `{ model, state, questions }`, plus OpenRouter's `provider` object when the block sets `compat.openrouter_routing` (the field chat models use; e.g. `{ zdr = true }` restricts a member to zero-data-retention endpoints). The response is `{ model, answers, usage: { input_tokens, output_tokens, cost? } }`; Cloudflare's native `{ result: { … } }` envelope is accepted too.

A system-one model is never offered to pi-ai. Startup (`validateDecisionsConfig`, `src/decisions/config.ts`, called from `app.ts` next to the other cross-field checks) refuses one anywhere a chat-side config site names a model: a session type's model, a per-agent model override, a `[[user_limits]]` preference or sub-cap, captioning, image generation, `x_search`, remote embedding (a walk over the config tree; `[[limits]].models` is exempt because it is a budget selector). Chains are homogeneous: a system-one model's fallback members must be system-one, and a chat model's must not be. A `[models.*.decision]` block requires `api = "system-one"`.

### Client (`src/decisions/client.ts`)

`DecisionClient.decide(modelKey, request, options)` is a **fetch-shaped consumer** like captioning and `x_search`: it composes `runFetchWithFallback` (§8a) over the model's chain, so per-model health, the group throttle on 429/503 with `Retry-After`, 529 as a health strike, the canary, scheduler admission, and at most one attempt per member per call all apply unchanged. The outcome taxonomy:

| response | outcome |
|---|---|
| 2xx with well-formed answers | success |
| 2xx with a missing or malformed answer, or an unparsable body | environmental: falls over to the next member (the 2xx is still billed) |
| 400 / 413 / 422 | content: this request's fault, never falls over |
| 401 / 403 / 404 | **configuration failure of the member** (`kind: "skip"`, new in `runFetchWithFallback`): neutral for health and throttling, not retried, logged once per member and status as `decision_member_config_error` (with `dataPolicy: true` for OpenRouter's "No endpoints found matching your data policy"), falls over |
| 429 / 5xx / 529 / 402 / network error / the attempt's own timeout | environmental: health and throttle as §8a, falls over |

One hard deadline (`timeout_ms`) bounds the whole call, admission waits included. Each attempt gets a **slot** (`attemptSlot`): while a later candidate member (one that fits and is in budget) remains, at most the member's `[models.*.decision].attempt_timeout_ms` (default two thirds of the call's timeout), so a stalled head leaves time to fall over; the last candidate gets whatever remains. An attempt that runs out of a full slot is environmental (a health strike, falls over). One whose slot the deadline cut short ends the call as a neutral abort, since a truncated wait says nothing about the member. The call's own teardown timer fires a short grace after the deadline, so the attempt's timer always decides.

**Fits.** `[models.*.decision]` declares what a member accepts: `question_types`, `max_questions`, `max_choice_options`, `max_score_levels`, `state_shapes` (`"text_or_conversation"` marks a judge-only member that takes only a string or an `{input, output}` conversation: it is skipped for an object state and answers the checks point's conversation-shaped `noul` calls, `DecisionRequest.stateShape`, §8j), `state_budget_tokens` (the largest state the member actually reads; defaults to `context_window`), and `billing` (`"per_request"`, the default, or `"per_question"` for routes that re-bill the state for every question), and `attempt_timeout_ms` (the member's slot while a later member remains, "Client" above); `max_images`, `max_image_bytes` and `images` govern vision requests ("Vision decision chain" below). A request carrying images never reaches a member without `"image"` in `input_modalities` (misfit `image_input`). `runFetchWithFallback` gained a per-call `memberFilter` that may drop the head: a member whose limits the request exceeds, or whose effective state budget is below the point's `min_state_tokens` (default 1000), is never sent the request. When no member fits, the call throws `NoFittingMemberError` without a request.

**State clamping.** The point's state builder is called with a token budget per member: `min(point.state_max_tokens, member state budget) − question tokens − a small margin`, using the context builder's tokenizer (§9 "Tokenization"). Builders pack newest-first (`packNewest`); the client re-measures and rebuilds smaller if a builder overshoots. So a route that silently truncates sees exactly the window the log records, and provider truncation is never relied on.

**Usage and cost.** Every 2xx attempt is reported through `onBilled`, parsed or not, so the ledger matches the provider's invoice. The cost is the provider's `usage.cost` when present (as `x_search` records OpenRouter's reported cost for Grok), else `usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens` priced from the member's `cost` block, else an estimate from the state size (multiplied by the question count on a `per_question` member). The dated served id (`vendor/model-20261001`) is recorded.

**Rate-limit isolation.** `applyDecisionRateLimitGroups` (startup, before the group validation and the scheduler) gives every system-one model without an explicit `rate_limit_group` its own declared group `decision:<model key>` (default `max_in_flight` 2). A decision model hitting a provider or free-tier 429 pauses only itself, never chat traffic or the other decision members.

### Decision points and `evaluate()` (`src/decisions/registry.ts`)

A `DecisionPoint<I, V>` declares `questions(input, settings, view?)`, `state(input, budgetTokens, view?)`, a pure `resolve(answers, input, threshold) → V | null` (null = not confident enough), `fallback(input)` (today's behaviour for that decision), `describe(verdict)` for the log, and optionally `images(input)`, its subject images for the vision chain (below; `view` is set only on a vision attempt). `DecisionEngine.evaluate(point, input, ctx)`:

1. Resolves the point's settings for the session's agent; a disabled point returns the fallback verdict with no call and no log.
2. **Budget**: each chain member is checked with `BudgetEngine.check({ class: "decision", tool: <point>, modelId, logicalModelId, sessionType, timelineKey })`; a blocked member is skipped by the fetch chain, and with every member blocked the point falls back (`reason: "budget"`) without a call. A blocked decision budget means "decide the old way", never "refuse the work".
3. **Health**: when every member is unhealthy with no probe due, it falls back (`unavailable`) without a call, logging `decision_model_unavailable` at most once a minute per chain.
4. Calls the client. Any failure of the whole chain falls back with a reason: `no_fitting_member`, `timeout`, `aborted`, `error`, or, when `resolve` returns null, `low_confidence`. When the evaluation uses the vision chain, steps 2–4 run on it first and any failure (including `low_confidence`) retries once on the text chain ("Vision decision chain" below).
5. Logs one `decision_evaluated { point, agent, timelineKey, sessionId, model, source: "model"|"heuristic", reason?, verdict, answers (compact: "choice@confidence" / noul probability), servedModel, servedVersion, stateTokens, billing, inputTokens, costUsd, latencyMs, heuristicVerdict?, and on an evaluation that planned a vision attempt imageCount, visionServed, visionReason? }`. `heuristicVerdict` is the cheap verdict of today's code, logged alongside so the log doubles as an agreement record. Nothing gates on it. Besides the log line, every evaluation of an enabled point is recorded as one `decision_evaluations` row ("Decision visibility" below).
6. Records one `usage_events` row per billed attempt (§8f): `class = "decision"`, `tool_name` = the point, `model_id`/`logical_model_id` = the member that billed, `ref` = the dated served id, plus the caller's attribution (`agent_session_id`, `session_type`, `timeline_key`, `trigger_sender_id`).

**Billing follows the session.** A session-bound evaluation carries the session id, so the per-user fan-in (`recordUsageEvent`, §8g) meters it against the session's payee exactly like a tool row: total and pools, never a model-scoped sub-cap. An evaluation without a session carries only `timeline_key` (and the sender) and counts toward `[[limits]]` rules only. The aggregate cap is an ordinary rule: `[[limits]].classes` accepts `"decision"`.

**Calibration.** Thresholds are per point (`min_confidence`, default `[decisions].min_confidence` = 0.6). Because models calibrate differently, `[decisions.calibration.<member>]` may override a threshold for answers that member served: `"<point>.<name>"` beats a bare `<name>`, which beats the point's own value. Calibration keys must name system-one models.

**Per-call options** (`EvaluateContext`): `decisionGroup` (shared by the calls of one decision), `onEvaluation` (a per-call row sink that replaces the engine's, used by the output gate to write anchored rows and learn their ids), `timeoutMs` (a per-call deadline over the point's `timeout_ms`), `usageClass` (`"decision"`, or `"audit"` for the audit worker: the budget class checked and the ledger class written, §9i), plus a point's optional `stateShape(input)` (`"object"` | `"conversation"`). `DecisionEngine.usableMembers(point, agent, attribution, usageClass)` lists the chain members that pass the same budget and health checks `evaluate` makes, so a caller can plan calls for the member that will serve (the checks point's fits split, §8j).

**Nothing else imports the client.** Call sites depend only on `evaluate(point, input)` and the typed verdict.

### Routing (`src/decisions/points/routing.ts`)

**When.** At the creation of a fresh, human-triggered chat-lane session (session type `default`; not proactive, not bot-triggered, not a resume) whose agent has the point enabled. `launchSession` passes a `route` hook to `AgentSessionFactory.create`, which loads the workspace first and calls it with the session's listed skills, *before* model selection. The hook runs after `awaitTriggerReadiness`, so the trigger's captions are already in the state. Its ledger row is bound to the new session (and so billed to its payee, §8g).

**State.** `{ request: { id, from, text, reply_to?: { from, text }, attachments? }, recent: [{ from, text, self?, attachments? }] }`: the trigger (hydrated, so attachments are caption strings and the reply target is resolved) and up to `recent_messages` (default 10) messages before it, packed newest-first to the member's budget. Bodies are clipped (2000 characters for the request, 400 for the others).

**Questions** (one call, each only when it has options). Tasks are **multi-label** (DECISION-MODEL §5.1a): a request may select several, and a task may exist only as a label for rules and statistics.
- `task__<key>`: one `noul` per `[decisions.routing.tasks.<key>]`, its description as the criterion.
- `difficulty`: `score` over `[decisions.routing.difficulty].levels`, when configured.
- `skill__<name>`: one `noul` per listed skill of the session (description as criterion), when `preload_skills` (default true).

With no question to ask, the point is not evaluated at all.

**Verdict.** A task is selected at `p ≥` its own threshold (`tasks.<key>.threshold`, else the point's `min_confidence`; calibration keys `"routing.task.<key>"` / `"task.<key>"`), a skill at `p ≥ min_confidence` (`"skill.<name>"`), the difficulty at `confidence ≥ min_confidence`. The point falls back (`low_confidence`) only when no task question was answered, the difficulty is not confident and no skill was selected; otherwise the verdict's `tasks` are the selected tasks in authored order, or `["other"]` when none was (`task` = the first, kept for logs and the console label). Over the selected tasks:
- their `models` (or `model`, shorthand for a one-entry list) are concatenated, duplicates dropped, into one **preference cascade**; their `skills` and `tail_files` are unioned; the **highest** `thinking_level` wins (`off < minimal < low < medium < high < xhigh`);
- the difficulty axis applies only when no selected task names models: `difficulty.models["<level>"]`, and `difficulty.thinking_levels["<level>"]` when no task set a level;
- selected skills join the skill union.

**Applying it** (`factory.create`):
- **Model cascade, no ranking.** The operator decides which model suits which task; the code never checks that a routed model is "better". Without per-user limits, the first cascade entry whose chain can serve right now (`chooseChainMember` over its members: healthy or probe-due, and in budget) heads the session, with its own fallback chain. With per-user limits the cascade is prepended to the user's preference list, so each entry gets the same per-request affordable ∧ healthy ∧ fits check as any preference (a cascade entry no rule's sub-cap names is bound by the user's total and pools). With every entry exhausted, selection is exactly as if routing had picked nothing. `routing_model_selected` logs the cascade and the pick.
- **Thinking level.** A routed level replaces the head model's own `thinking_level` for the session, unless the head declares `reasoning = false`.
- **Skill preloads via synthetic calls.** Each routed skill must be a listed skill of the workspace (an unknown one is skipped with `routing_skill_unknown`; an always-loaded one is already in the system prompt). Each preload is one **synthetic `load_skill` call** (`src/agent/synthetic-calls.ts`, spec SESSION-RECORDS §4) stamped `harness: { kind: "injection", decisionGroup }` with the routing evaluation's group (the router hands `decisionGroup` back with a model verdict; a heuristic fallback routes nothing). `create()` executes them as real `load_skill` calls (`executeSyntheticCalls`) after the agent and the registry's `onChange` are wired, so each load updates `agent.state.tools` and its `addedToolNames` drive the native load point exactly as an organic skill load does; the `{ assistant toolCall, toolResult }` pairs are appended after the final user turn (`CreatedAgent.kickoff`, ahead of any session-record injection, §8i). The system prompt and frozen prefix are byte-identical to an unrouted session's. Per-task `tail_files` render in the final user turn as `<tail_instructions source="…">` blocks.
- **Session tasks.** `create` computes the session's task labels (`sessionTasksFor`): a routed session's `tasks`; a resume's persisted ones; a proactive session (`opts.proactive`, or the configured proactive session type) the built-in **`proactive`** task, with no decision call; otherwise none (routing off or fallen back, bot-triggered, internal jobs). They scope the refusal rules' `tasks` condition, the refusal events' `tasks_json` and the gate's judged-state scope (§8j), and the model behaviour statistics' task dimension (§8k).
- **Persistence.** What routing changed is stored on `agent_sessions.initial_preloads` (`SessionRoutingState`: preloaded skill names, routed head model, routed cascade under per-user limits, routed thinking level, the session's `tasks`); a proactive session stores `{ skills: [], tasks: ["proactive"] }`. The loaded tools are not stored: the transcript's synthetic pairs carry them. A row written before synthetic preloads may still hold a `tools` array; `getSessionInitialPreloads` exposes it read-only as `legacyTools`, which the resume branch loads into the registry before `seedFromTranscript` (never written again). An unrouted session stores nothing.
- **Resume.** A resume is never routed again: `create` reads the persisted state and keeps the session's tasks, the routed head model (or, under per-user limits, the routed cascade ahead of the user's preferences), the routed effort, and the preloaded skills. The skill bodies are already in the transcript's synthetic call pairs, and `seedFromTranscript` re-derives the loaded tools from their `addedToolNames`. Tail files are not re-rendered on resume.

`routing_applied` logs the tasks, preloads, tail files and effort. **Fallback:** today's behaviour exactly: the session-type model, no preloads, `TAIL.md` only. With the point off, `create` does not load the workspace early and the build is unchanged.

**Config** (`[decisions.routing]`, besides the common point knobs): `preload_skills`, `recent_messages`, `tasks.<key>.{ description, models | model, thinking_level, skills, tail_files, threshold }`, `difficulty.{ levels, models, thinking_levels }`. Startup validation: a task's models must be chat models, `model` and `models` are exclusive, `other` and `proactive` are reserved, difficulty indices must be in range, tail files must be workspace-relative and (when routing is on) exist.

### Deleted messages in recent-chat windows

The recent-chat windows of the decision points represent the visible chat, so they treat a deleted message like the recent tiers do (§9 "Deleted messages"): it keeps its place and sender, and its text is the placeholder (`[message deleted]`, `[message deleted by <deleter>]` for a moderator), with no attachments or captions. `toTranscriptMessage(event, maxChars, { deletedPlaceholder })` does this for routing's `recent`, the checks state's `recent` (§8j), the implicit-reply window, and the audit's `recent` (§9i), which passes the session's start time so only a message deleted by then shows as deleted; the late-addition point's `before`/`between` chat and the records point's recent chat do the same. A quote of a deleted message (routing's and the records point's `reply_to`) is the placeholder too. The request itself (the trigger group, the candidate message) keeps its content: late input decides what belongs to it.

### Decision visibility

Every decision is recorded and inspectable (spec SESSION-RECORDS §8). `DecisionEngine.evaluate()` emits one `DecisionEvaluationRow` per evaluation of an **enabled** point (model verdict or fallback alike) to the optional `DecisionEngineOptions.onEvaluation` sink, called synchronously once per outcome; a disabled point produces no row (nor a log line). The engine imports no storage: `app.ts` wires the sink to `Storage.insertDecisionEvaluation` (fire-and-forget on the single-writer queue; a failed write logs `decision_evaluation_persist_failed`, a throwing sink `decision_emit_row_failed`). One row per evaluation request, in the `decision_evaluations` table (§8i "Storage"):

- `decisionGroup` (nanoid) identifies one **decision instance** and is returned on `DecisionOutcome.decisionGroup`: `EvaluateContext.decisionGroup` when the caller passes one, else a fresh id per `evaluate()`. Routing is one row in its own group; the records point is one row per candidate, all in one group made by `selectRecordsToInject`, never shared with routing; the checks point writes one row per call (plus pattern rows) of one output's evaluation in one group, through its per-call sink with the anchor and consequence (§8j); the audit point's send-contract calls are rows of their own groups (prefix `audit:`, §9i). Synthetic calls a decision produced carry the same group on their harness marker, which is how the console places the decision's card (§11).
- Attribution: `point`, `agent`, `timelineKey`, `agentSessionId` (the session the decision is for, so billing and the console both find it), `triggerEventId` (set by the records point; routing leaves it null), `candidateSessionId` (records point only).
- `source` (`"model"` | `"heuristic"`), `reason` (the fallback reason), `verdictJson` (the point's `describe(verdict)`), `answersJson` (the full answer map with probabilities and confidences, when answers came back).
- `stateJson`, `questionsJson`: **what the member was actually sent** (on a vision attempt the wire form with image markers instead of pixels), captured through the client's `onSent` callback right before each fetch (the last attempt's payload, after any shrink-and-rebuild). Fallbacks that sent nothing (`disabled`, `budget`, `unavailable`, `config`, `no_fitting_member`) leave both null; fallbacks after a sent attempt (`error`, `timeout`, `low_confidence`) carry it. Capped by `capJsonBytes`: state at 64 KiB, questions at 16 KiB, with a `…[truncated]` marker.
- `servedModel`, `servedVersion`, `latencyMs`, `inputTokens`, `costUsd` (null when zero or unknown).

### Records (`src/decisions/points/records.ts`)

**Purpose.** Which session records a fresh session starts with (spec SESSION-RECORDS §6.2). The point judges each candidate record's relevance to the trigger; the app's candidate gathering and the injection itself are §8i "Injection".

**Input** (`RecordsInput`): `{ request: { from, text, attachments? }, replyTo?: { from, text }, recentChat?: RecordsChatMessage[], record, candidateSessionId, isReplyTarget }`; `RecordsChatMessage` = `{ from, text, self?, age?, ofRecord? }`. The request also carries its actual `reply_to` when present, including when judging a different candidate.

**State**, shaped so as not to imply a relationship that is not known:
- Reply framing (`replyTo` set, the reply target's candidate): `{ request, reply_to, record }`.
- Non-reply framing: `{ request, recent_chat, record }`. The candidate's message is explicitly marked `record_message: true`, and messages carry precomputed age labels. Context is a continuous suffix ending immediately before the request. Packing may drop leading context before the candidate, but never bridges omitted messages between it and the request. The record is clipped to fit beside that required suffix using the same tokenizer as state packing; if the suffix cannot fit, evaluation falls back to skipping this unsolicited candidate.
- Clips: request text 1200 characters, chat and reply texts 400.

**Question:** one `relevant` (`noul`), asking whether the request continues or refers to the **same specific work**, explicitly identifying the `record_message`/`reply_to` anchor and saying that a similar topic alone is insufficient.

**Resolve:** `inject = relevant ≥ inject_threshold` (`[decisions.records].inject_threshold`, default 0.6), with `relevance` = the probability. Calibration uses the threshold-name convention: `[decisions.calibration.<member>]` takes `"records.inject_threshold"` over a bare `"inject_threshold"`. The point has no confidence separate from that probability, so `[decisions.records].min_confidence` is **rejected** at startup (`validateDecisionsConfig`). An answer that is not a `noul` resolves null (`low_confidence` fallback).

**Fallback** (every per-candidate fallback): the reply target's candidate → `inject: true` when `[session_records].inject_on_reply` is on (`RecordsInput.injectOnReply`, absent = on; the §8i default rule), else `inject: false`; any other candidate → `inject: false`. A model verdict below the threshold on the reply target is honoured: that record is not injected.

**`selectRecordsToInject`** (`src/decisions/points/records-select.ts`): makes one `decisionGroup`, runs one `evaluate(recordsPoint, …)` per candidate **in parallel** (one request per candidate: packing several records into one request would only make each answer harder), each row carrying its `candidateSessionId` and the trigger's event id; a rejected evaluation (defensive) takes the point's fallback with reason `error`. `SelectRecordsInput.injectOnReply` carries `inject_on_reply` into every candidate's input. It returns `{ inject, decisionGroup, outcomes }`: the candidates with `inject: true`, highest relevance first, at most `max_injected` (default 2).

**Capacity.** One trigger can send `candidates + 1` records requests plus one routing request at once. When the point is enabled, `validateDecisionsConfig` sums that demand per rate-limit group of the chain heads (records `candidates + 1`, routing 1 when enabled) and warns `decisions_records_capacity_low` `{ where, group, maxInFlight, needed, hint }` where a group's effective `max_in_flight` (its `[rate_limits.llm.<group>]` value, else the scheduler's `DEFAULT_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` = 2 that implicit `decision:<key>` groups get) is below it. A warning, not an error: an undersized group only queues.

**Config** (`[decisions.records]`, besides the common point knobs `enabled` (default false), `model`, `timeout_ms`, `state_max_tokens`, `min_state_tokens`): `inject_threshold` (0..1, default 0.6), `candidates` (0..20, default 3: bot-message sessions besides the reply target), `candidate_max_age_ms` (positive integer, default 3600000; unsolicited candidates only), `max_injected` (0..10, default 2).

### Checks (`src/decisions/points/checks.ts`)

The output gate's point (§8j): `CheckItem`s (one per question of each enabled check that takes part, id `<code>__<name>` for a named question, else `<code>__<source>`, `_2`… on repeats) become `noul` or `choice` questions, `{persona}` filled from `[decisions].persona`; in the conversation shape, backticked field references become plain words ("the assistant's output", "the user's input"). `resolve` never returns null: a `noul` fires at `p ≥ threshold("<code>", question.threshold)` (a named question first tries `"<code>.<name>"`), a `choice` when it picks its fire option with enough confidence. `fallback` is `{ results: [], unjudged: true }`. `planCheckCalls` splits the items into calls by the serving member's fits (§8j "One evaluation per output"); the duplicate check's items go through `planDuplicateCalls` (state scope `duplicate`: the `{ earlier, draft }` object or its judge conversation, chunked to `max_questions`) on its own chain (`EvaluateContext.chainHead`, §8j "Duplicate sends"). Enabled by `[decisions.checks].enabled` (with `[decisions].enabled` and a model); its knobs are in §8j "Configuration"; `min_confidence` is rejected.

### Audit (`[decisions.audit]`)

The offline audit worker's point (§9i): its send-contract diagnosis is `contractAuditPoint`; its history pass runs the checks point's questions under the audit point's chain, timeout, priority and ledger class (`CheckEvaluatorOptions.judging`), while the rows it writes stay `point = 'checks'`. `DECISION_POINT_NAMES` = `routing`, `records`, `checks`, `audit`, `late_addition`, `implicit_reply`; every one resolves, merges per agent and validates like the others (`pointSettings`, `validateEffective`).

### Vision decision chain (`src/decisions/images.ts`)

Text decision models see images as their captions. A point may also use an optional **vision chain**: a system-one chain whose members read images (DECISION-MODEL §3.5).

**Settings.** `[decisions.<point>].vision_model` → `[decisions].vision_model` names the chain head; `[decisions.<point>].vision` (`"off" | "uncaptioned" | "always"`) the mode, defaulting per point (`DEFAULT_VISION_MODES`): `routing` `uncaptioned`, `late_addition` `always` (its media candidates have no caption yet by construction), `records` / `checks` / `audit` / `implicit_reply` `off`. `pointSettings` resolves them into `PointSettings.vision` = `{ model, mode, timeoutMs ([decisions].vision_timeout_ms, default 8000), maxImages ([decisions].max_images, default 4), imageMaxPixels (image_max_pixels, default 1,000,000), maxImageBytes (max_image_bytes, default 200,000) }`, or undefined when no vision chain is configured or the mode is `off`. Startup validation: every vision chain (global and per point) must name a system-one model and every member of it must declare `"image"` in `input_modalities`; a point's `vision` set without any vision chain is a warning (`decisions_vision_without_chain`).

**When it is used.** Only a point that declares `images(input)` (its **subject images**, newest first, as `DecisionImageRef { id, messageId, from, caption?, localPath?, mimeType? }`) ever uses the chain; today that is `late_addition` (routing has the setting but declares no images). Mode `uncaptioned` uses it when some subject image has no caption; `always` whenever there is a subject image. At most `max_images` refs are taken.

**Images.** The engine loads them through `DecisionEngineOptions.loadImage` (`app.ts` passes `createDecisionImageLoader`, which reads the downloaded file at `localPath` and runs the inference conditioning `read_image` uses, `conditionImageBufferForInference`: downscaled to `image_max_pixels`, re-encoded JPEG under `max_image_bytes`, mozjpeg per `[media.image]`), in parallel; an image that cannot be loaded is dropped. The loaded ones are labelled `image 1`, `image 2`, … in order. With no loader, or no loadable image, the evaluation goes to the text chain directly (`visionReason` `no_image_loader` / `no_loadable_image`).

**Members.** The client never sends a vision request to a member without image input (misfit `image_input`). Each member gets at most its `decision.max_images` of the images (newest first), and an image over its `decision.max_image_bytes` is re-conditioned under that cap (memoized per image and cap) or dropped; a member left with no image is skipped (`kind: "skip"`, neutral). The state is built per member with the labels of the images it is actually sent (`DecisionStateView.imageLabels`, ref id → label), so its attachments name exactly those.

**Wire shape** (`wireImageState`), per member `decision.images`:
- `"state_parts"` (default): `state = [ { type: "text", text: <the state as JSON> }, { type: "text", text: "image 1: attached to message $abc by Alice" }, { type: "image_url", image_url: { url: "data:image/jpeg;base64,…" } }, … ]`.
- `"images_field"`: the plain state (an object state gains `image_labels`, the label lines in array order) plus a top-level `images` array of data URLs.

A text request is byte-identical to one without the feature. Vision attempts get `questions(input, settings, { vision: true })`, whose instructions refer to images by label, and all of the point's questions (they are not split between the chains).

**Fallback.** The vision attempt is a full chain run (budget, health, fits, `vision_timeout_ms`, or a per-call `timeoutMs`). Any failure, `low_confidence` included, retries the evaluation **once** on the text chain, whose state carries captions only (and the point's placeholders for undescribed images); a caller abort does not retry. A text-chain failure then gives the point's fallback verdict. The log line and the outcome carry `imageCount`, `visionServed` and `visionReason` (why the vision attempt did not serve); the evaluation row carries `imageCount` and `visionServed` for the sink (not `decision_evaluations` columns), and its `stateJson` is the wire form with each image replaced by a marker (`[image 1: image/jpeg, 41233 bytes]`), never pixels. Billing is unchanged: every billed attempt of either chain is a `decision` row, image tokens included in `usage.input_tokens`.

### Late addition (`src/decisions/points/late-addition.ts`)

**Purpose.** Whether a message the trigger's sender sent after the request belongs to that request (spec LATE-INPUT §5.2 "Membership"). The point, its input builder and its knobs are pure; eligibility and what a "yes" does are the caller's.

**Input** (`lateAdditionInputFrom({ before, request, between, candidate, selfIds?, recentMessages? })`, from hydrated timeline events): the last `recent_messages` (default 5) messages before the request; the request (the trigger group, merged into one post: texts joined, attachments concatenated); up to 12 messages between the request and the candidate (newest kept); the candidate. Ages are precomputed labels relative to the request: `"40s before"` against its first part's send time, `"6s after request"` against its last part's. Texts are clipped (request and candidate 1200 characters, the others 400). Senders render as in the shared transcript (`senderName`), the bot's own messages marked `self: true` (`isSelf`, role `assistant`, or `selfIds`). Subject images: the candidate's image attachments, then the request's (latest part first).

**State**: `{ before: [{ from, text, age, self? }], request: { from, text, attachments }, between_omitted?, between: [{ from, text, age, self? }], message: { from, text, attachments, age } }`, attachments as `{ kind, image?, caption }` where `caption` is the existing caption or null and `image` is the label on a vision attempt. Nothing in it implies the candidate is addressed to the bot. Packing drops the oldest `before` messages first; only when none fit are the oldest `between` messages dropped, counted in `between_omitted`.

**Question**: `belongs` (`noul`): "`message` supplies something `request` refers to or expects, or continues, corrects or adds to it, written by the same person for the same purpose." (on a vision attempt it adds that images follow the state, labelled as in `attachments[].image`).

**Verdict** `LateAdditionVerdict { belongs, probability, judged }`: `belongs = probability ≥ threshold` (`[decisions.late_addition].threshold`, default 0.7; calibration `"late_addition.threshold"` / `"threshold"`). **Fallback** `LATE_ADDITION_NOT_JUDGED` = `{ belongs: false, probability: null, judged: false }`. Vision mode default `always`.

**Knobs** (`lateAdditionKnobs(decisions)`, defaults applied, readable with the point off): `threshold` 0.7, `candidateWindowMs` 60000, `maxJudged` 8, `maxFolded` 3, `recentMessages` 5. `min_confidence` is rejected at startup (one `noul`, gated by `threshold`).

### Implicit reply (`src/decisions/points/implicit-reply.ts`)

**Purpose.** Whether a bare group message responds to a specific recent bot message M without the reply function or a mention (spec LATE-INPUT §6). One evaluation per (candidate, M).

**Pre-gate** (`implicitReplyPreGate`, pure, over `ImplicitReplyGateEvent { id, timestamp, author: "self" | "bot" | "human" }`): the timeline is a group; the candidate is from a human, has no reply, no mention of the bot, no trigger of its own, and was not consumed by late input. Walking back from the candidate over the preceding messages, every message of this agent within `max_messages_after` messages (the candidate is the 1st, 2nd, … message after it) and `max_age_ms` of it is an M; the walk stops at the first message of another bot (a sibling agent or any bot account), at the message bound, or at the age bound. The result is `{ eligible: true, botMessageIds }` (newest first) or `{ eligible: false, reason }` (`not_group`, `not_human`, `has_reply`, `mentions_bot`, `has_trigger`, `consumed`, `no_bot_message`). `implicitReplyGateEventOf(event, { selfIds?, otherBotIds? })` classifies a timeline event (`otherBotIds` first, then self, then bot accounts; webhooks count as human).

**Input** (`implicitReplyInputFrom({ recent, botMessage, candidate, selfIds?, recentMessages?, now? })`): up to `recent_messages` (default 6) messages before M, M marked `bot_message: true`, and every message from M up to the candidate; ages are `"40s ago"` labels relative to `now` (default the candidate's send time); attachments are caption strings as in the shared transcript.

**State**: the records point's non-reply framing, `{ recent_chat: [{ from, text, age, self?, bot_message?, attachments? }], message: { from, text, age, attachments? } }`. The suffix from M to the candidate is always kept whole; only context before M is dropped by packing, and a suffix that cannot fit is not judged (`error` fallback). **Question**: `replies` (`noul`): "`message` responds to the message marked `bot_message` in `recent_chat`: it answers it, reacts to it, or asks about it."

**Verdict** `ImplicitReplyVerdict { replies, probability, judged, botMessageId }`: `replies = probability ≥ threshold` (default 0.8). **Fallback**: inert (`replies: false, judged: false`). Vision mode default `off`. **Knobs** (`implicitReplyKnobs`): `threshold` 0.8, `maxMessagesAfter` 3, `maxAgeMs` 120000, `recentMessages` 6. `min_confidence` is rejected at startup.

### Memory (`src/decisions/points/memory.ts`)

**Purpose.** The final filter of auto-retrieval (§9d "Judged retrieval"): does a memory passage help respond in this conversation. **On by default** whenever `[decisions]` is on and a chain resolves (the only point with that default, `pointSwitchedOn`); `[decisions.memory].enabled = false` turns it off, and `[retrieval.auto].judge = false` stops auto-retrieval from using it. Each request carries one diary entry with the conversation, the same class of data the routing, records and check points send to the decision chain.

**One request per passage**, all sent in parallel by the pipeline (bounded by the member's group concurrency), in one `decisionGroup`, billed to the session (class `decision`). Several passages in one state would degrade every answer, and cost is not a reason to accept that. At most `[retrieval.auto].max_judged` (default 12) passages per build, person-cued included. The requests go at priority `proactive`, below routing, records and the send/ending checks (`interactive`) in the same `decision:<model>` group, so they never delay those. Startup warns (`decisions_memory_capacity_low`) when the chain head's rate-limit group's `max_in_flight` is below one trigger's whole demand: the most passages one build sends (`judgedPerBuildMax`: the cross-encoder's `top_n` or 12, plus `person_recent_max`, capped by `max_judged`), plus routing and records when they share the group. No warning when retrieval, auto-retrieval or `auto.judge` is off.

**State** `{ conversation: [{ from, text, self? }], request?: { from, text, reply_to? }, participants: [names], entry: { date, room?, text } }`: the last `conversation_messages` (default 8) messages, newest last, deleted ones as placeholders; the request (the trigger group's text and its reply target), absent for a proactive session; the display names the user lanes searched; the whole block, cleaned (§9d "Excerpts"). The entry is fitted first (clipped with a marker only if it alone overflows), then the newest conversation that fits. Persona and system prompt are left out.

**Questions** (independent `noul`s): `relevant` ("`entry` contains information that would help respond to `request` in this `conversation`: facts, history or earlier events about the people, things or topics being discussed"; proactive: "… help respond in this `conversation` …"); `about_participant` ("`entry` describes one of `participants` or an interaction with them", only with participants); and one `filter__<key>` per judged memory filter the passage has no fresh cached verdict for ("`entry` matches: <description>", worded the same on every surface, examples as `criteria.true`/`criteria.false`, §9c "Memory filters").

**Verdict** `MemoryPassageVerdict { keep, relevant, aboutParticipant, filters, judged, meta }`: `keep = relevant ≥ relevance_threshold` (default 0.7; calibration key `"memory.relevance_threshold"`), each filter `hidden = p ≥` its threshold (calibration key `"memory.filter.<key>"`). A missing answer resolves null (`low_confidence`). **Fallback**: not kept, not judged. `describe` carries the citation, content hash, scores (hybrid, late, cross-encoder) and `hiddenBy`, so the decision rows hold the candidates' citations and scores. `min_confidence` is rejected at startup.

`memoryFilterPoint` is the same point name asked only the filter questions about one block (`{ entry: { date, room?, text } }`, the same "`entry` matches: …" questions), for the filter surfaces that are not auto-retrieval. A relevance state has `conversation`, a filter-only state does not; rows written before the state named the block `entry` call it `passage`, and the calibration audit reads both.

### Configuration

```toml
[decisions]
enabled = false            # master switch; a point runs only when this AND the point's `enabled` are true
model = "decider"          # default chain for every point (a system-one [models.*] key; its fallback applies)
timeout_ms = 3000
min_confidence = 0.6
state_max_tokens = 8000    # clamped further to each member's state budget
persona = ""               # short operator-written summary, used in question instructions (never in state)
vision_model = ""          # optional vision chain (system-one, every member with "image" input)
vision_timeout_ms = 8000
max_images = 4             # per evaluation; min with a member's decision.max_images
image_max_pixels = 1000000
max_image_bytes = 200000   # JPEG; min with a member's decision.max_image_bytes

[decisions.calibration.decider_alt]
"routing.min_confidence" = 0.8

[decisions.<point>]        # per point: enabled, model (per-point chain), timeout_ms,
                           # state_max_tokens, min_state_tokens, min_confidence,
                           # vision_model, vision ("off"|"uncaptioned"|"always"), + point knobs

[decisions.checks.duplicate]
model = "decider"          # the duplicate check's chain (§8j); default [decisions].model

[decisions.memory]         # ON by default with [decisions]; enabled = false turns it off
relevance_threshold = 0.7
conversation_messages = 8
```

**Per-agent overrides.** `[agents.<name>.decisions]` has the same shape. `decisionsFor(config, agent)` deep-merges it over the global block (agent wins), except `routing.tasks`, which the agent replaces wholesale. So one agent can run a point the others do not, with its own task list.

---

## 8i. Session Records

A session does work the chat never shows: searches, pages read, results it looked at and left out, files it made. **Every completed chat-lane or proactive session that did tool work writes a session record** in one extra turn on the same agent right after it completes, while its prompt cache is warm: a compact handoff note written so that a later session holding only the chat and this record can answer questions about the work and carry it on. Every trigger starts a **fresh** session (reply-to-continue is off by default, §8 "Resumable sessions"); the records it needs are put into its context by **synthetic `read_session_record` calls** appended after its final user turn, the same call the agent can make itself. The agent can fetch more on demand: another record, the record a record builds on (`builds_on`, one hop per call), or the raw rollout (`read_session_transcript`). Source: `src/agent/session-records.ts` (`SessionRecordService`, prompt, eligibility, `buildsOnFromTranscript`), `src/agent/record-turn.ts` (gate), `src/agent/synthetic-calls.ts` (injection mechanism), `src/tools/session-record-tool.ts`, `src/tools/read-session-record.ts`, `planRecordInjections` / `startRecordTurn` in `src/app.ts`. Design record: spec SESSION-RECORDS.

### Storage (`src/storage/database.ts`, schema v24)

Both tables are in the genesis `SCHEMA` and created for existing DBs by the v23→v24 step `addSessionRecordsTables` (§7 "Schema versioning & migrations").

**`session_records`**: one row per session, `session_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY` (an `agent_sessions.id`; no FK), `timeline_key TEXT NOT NULL`, `agent TEXT` (owning agent; null in single-agent mode), `text TEXT NOT NULL`, `token_count INTEGER NOT NULL`, `builds_on TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` (JSON array of the session ids whose records were delivered into this session), `model_id TEXT` (the model that served the record turn), `created_at INTEGER NOT NULL` (epoch ms). `upsertSessionRecord` (`insert or replace`, single-writer queue; `builds_on` passed as `string[]`) — a resumed generation's record replaces the row, `created_at` included. `getSessionRecord(sessionId)` returns the raw row (`builds_on` still JSON). Indexed by session id only: every lookup starts from a known `agent_session_id` or a candidate list. `getRecentRecordedBotSessions(timelineKey, toTimestamp, limit, agent?)` is retained as a historical lookup helper (automatic injection now uses the bounded recent-chat window): one row per session (its newest `role = 'assistant'` event at or before `toTimestamp`), only sessions with a `session_records` row visible to `agent` (a null-agent row, or no `agent` given, matches any), newest first. It is a bounded newest-first walk of `idx_timeline_events_timeline_time` (an `iterate()` over the timeline's bot messages that have a record, deduplicated per session): it stops after `limit` sessions, or once every recorded session of the timeline was found, and never goes below the earliest recorded session's `agent_sessions.created_at` minus a one-day clock-skew slack (no floor when a recorded session has no `agent_sessions` row). Its cost tracks how far back the `limit`-th recorded session sits, not the room's history: on a synthetic 300k-event room, ~1 ms with dense records and ~0.03 ms with none, against 60–95 ms for the former window query.

**`session_record_generation`**: durable outcome metadata keyed by session id: `status` (`writing`, `written`, `skipped`, `failed`), nullable `reason`, and `updated_at`. Created additively by schema reconciliation. `SessionRecordService` records skips before returning (`no_work`, `disabled`, `session_type`, `tool_unavailable`), registers writing and then persists the terminal outcome before releasing its settle barrier. Empty finalization is `skipped/empty`; failures retain their classified reason. Relevance selection is independent: rejecting an injection never removes or prevents a record.

**`decision_evaluations`**: one row per decision-model evaluation (§8h "Decision visibility"): `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`, `ts INTEGER NOT NULL`, `decision_group TEXT NOT NULL`, `point TEXT NOT NULL` (`routing` | `records` | `checks` | `audit`), `agent`, `timeline_key`, `agent_session_id`, `trigger_event_id`, `candidate_session_id`, `source TEXT NOT NULL` (`model` | `heuristic` | `pattern`), `reason`, `verdict_json`, `answers_json`, `state_json`, `questions_json`, `served_model`, `served_version`, `latency_ms`, `input_tokens`, `cost_usd`, and (schema v25, written by the checks point, §8j) the anchor `checkpoint`, `branch_no`, `tool_call_id`, `attempt_no` and the `consequence` (all unmarked columns nullable). Indexes `idx_decision_evaluations_session (agent_session_id, ts)` and `idx_decision_evaluations_ts (ts)`. `insertDecisionEvaluation(row)` (single-writer queue; returns the row id), `getDecisionEvaluationsForSession(sessionId)` (`ts` ascending), `updateDecisionEvaluationConsequence(ids, consequence)`, `reanchorSessionBranch` (§8j).

### Tools

Wired by `buildSessionTools` for session type `default` and the proactive type on every run path (fresh launch, reply-resume, manual console resume), whatever `[session_records].enabled` says; each run's `SessionRecordHandles` (`{ gate: RecordTurnGate, draft: SummaryDraft }`) is created before the tools and captured by them. §10 "Session record tools" has the table.

- **`session_record_tool`** (`createSessionRecordTool({ draft, maxTokens })`): a `summary_tool` variant over the run's in-memory `SummaryDraft` (`create` / `view` / `str_replace` / `insert` / `finalize`; `finalize: true` on an editing call or on `view`, or the standalone `finalize` command, ends the loop with `terminate: true`). Every mutating command re-checks the draft against `[session_records].max_tokens`: an edit over budget is reverted and **throws** `… N tokens, limit L (O over). The edit was reverted …`; any thrown call never terminates, `finalize: true` included. `finalize` on an empty draft is the legitimate "nothing worth recording" skip. Flags: `harnessOnly: true`, `resumeWorkExempt: true`.
- **`read_session_record(session_id)`**: the record text, then (when `builds_on` is non-empty) `Builds on earlier session(s): … read_session_record one of them to follow the chain one hop`, then a pointer to `read_session_transcript(session_id, query)`; `details` = `{ session_id, tokenCount, buildsOn }`. Every failure **throws** an actionable error: unknown id (names where the id is shown), a session of an isolated channel this session is not in, another agent's session, a record still in flight (`SessionRecordService.isInFlight`: "call read_session_record(…) again in a few seconds"), and no record (points at `read_session_transcript`). The gate (`resolveReadableSession`) is the `read_messages` visibility gate (`ChannelVisibilityResolver.modeFor` + `sameChannel`) plus own-agent-only, and reads metadata only (`Storage.getAgentSessionMeta`). Always **immediate** under dynamic loading (§10): the factory adds it to the immediate set whenever it is in the catalog, since deployments replace `immediate` wholesale; the `sessions` skill also declares it.
- **`read_session_transcript(session_id, query?, range?, offset?)`**: the raw rollout as one entry per tool call in rollout order (turn = an assistant message with ≥1 tool call, 1-indexed; harness turns labelled `[harness]`): arguments clipped to 256 tokens with a marker, the result whole up to 512 tokens, else, when `query` matches inside it, windows of ±300 characters around each match up to 512 tokens (with a count of matches not shown), else its head plus a "pass query" marker; `isError` results render as `RESULT (error)`. Filter: `range` (inclusive turn numbers), then a case-insensitive `query` over name, argument JSON and result text. Output is bounded at 4000 tokens with an `offset` paging footer. Same gate as above, then `Storage.getAgentSessionTranscriptJson` (the payload only). Throws on a running session ("try again shortly"), no stored transcript, corrupt JSON, a reversed `range`, an `offset` past the end; zero matches is an answer with a hint. **Deferred**, declared by the `sessions` skill (`templates/workspace/skills/sessions/SKILL.md`, description cued on "where did you get that?", "what did you do in that session?", "what did you find earlier?").

The two read tools **count as work** for the work gate when the model calls them itself; `session_record_tool`, `load_skill`, `tool_search` and `no_reply` are exempt (§8 "The work gate"). A record the harness **injected** is never work (§8 "Nothing injected counts as work"): a session that was given a record but did no work of its own writes none (its record would only re-summarize the injected one); a later session retrieves the earlier record itself (selection, or `read_session_record`), and the injection's provenance stays in the decision rows and the synthetic call.

**Session ids in sight.** The argument is always on screen: a bot message renders `agent_session_id="…"` on its rich `<message>`, and so does a `<reply_to>` quote of a bot message (`ReplyContext.agentSessionId`, rich tier only; resolved at read time in `Storage.getEnrichmentData` through `botSessionIdLookup` — the stored row with that external id, a non-null `agent_session_id`, the same provider, in the quoting event's room or one of its threads, scoped like `getEditedBody` so another account's row never leaks; no schema change). `read_messages` labels bot messages `Name [agent_session_id: s-…]` (`[you, agent_session_id: …]` on the storage path), via `Storage.getAgentSessionIdsByExternalIds` on the provider-history and by-id paths. `TOOLS.md` carries a lookup row pointing at `read_session_record`.

**Record scope and cache reuse.** The appended record-turn instruction defines the record as work performed by this execution: its tool calls and results, changed artifacts, sent messages, and attempted but unfinished work. Supplied chat history, summaries, and earlier records are background, included only where needed to explain current work. This clarification changes only the appended kickoff; it does not relabel or rewrite the existing conversation prefix. No additional scope-judging model call is made.

**Missing-record responses.** `read_session_record` first enforces visibility/ownership. An active writer reports still writing; an unfinished session reports not generated yet. Durable skips distinguish the work gate, empty finalization, disabled generation and unsupported/unavailable tooling. Failures name the stored cause; persisted writing with no live writer reports an interrupted attempt. Interrupted/discarded main sessions name that status. Historical terminal harness markers are used when present; otherwise the reason is explicitly unknown, never guessed to be no work. Raw transcript lookup is the recovery path. These responses do not claim a relevance-gate rejection caused a missing record.

### The record-turn gate (`src/agent/record-turn.ts`)

`wrapToolsWithRecordTurnGate(tools, gate)` wraps every tool's `execute` against the run's `RecordTurnGate { active }`. While `active` is false, `session_record_tool` throws `session_record_tool is only used by the harness at the end of a session. Carry on with your other tools.`; while it is true, every other tool throws `Only session_record_tool is available while writing the session record. …` (naming the create/finalize calls and the empty-finalize skip). Definitions are untouched, so the wire `tools` array is byte-stable when the gate flips; only execution is restricted. The app passes the gate as `CreateAgentOptions.recordTurnGate`, and the **factory** applies the wrapper to the **final** tool list (the app's tools plus its own `load_skill` / `tool_search`, after the result-budget wrap), so the loading tools obey it too. Signal and `onUpdate` are forwarded; a blocked call throws before an outer wrapper (the editor's skill activation) can act.

**Harness-only placement.** `harnessOnly` (module-augmented on `AgentTool`, `src/agent/work-gate.ts`) keeps `session_record_tool` out of everything the agent can reach under dynamic loading: never immediate (the factory and the console preview's `splitDefsForDynamic` remove harness-only tools from the immediate set whatever the config patterns or an inlined skill match), never in the rendered deferred-tools index (`filterHarnessOnlyFromIndex`), never matched by a skill's `tools` patterns or the editor backstop (`DynamicToolRegistry.matchCatalog`), never found or loaded by `tool_search` (keyword, `select:` and the no-match catalog listing). Under `declare_deferred_tools` the declared array is therefore identical for the whole session. Without dynamic loading it is simply in `tools`, blocked by the gate. The console preview (`resolveToolDefs`) builds the tools with record handles and keeps the flag, so its tool block matches a real session.

### The record turn (`SessionRecordService`)

One shared `SessionRecordService` in the app owns the **in-flight registry** (session id → `{ done, waitDeadline, abort }`) and drives the turn. All three run paths end in the same app helper, `startRecordTurn({ sessionId, timelineKey, sessionType, inbound, created, handles, flush })`, so their eligibility, exempt set and priority cannot diverge.

**Settle ordering** (the run's success path: `launchSession`, `runResumeSession`, the manual `resumeSessionRun`):
1. `markCompleted` (status `completed`; the session is evicted, so the settle listeners release its claims and it leaves `activeForTimeline`; the follow-up watch is untouched). A run the operator interrupted (`status === "interrupted"`, read before `markCompleted`) writes no record. Parked, discarded and failed runs never reach this tail; a parked session that a console resume completes writes one then.
2. `startRecordTurn` → `SessionRecordService.start`, which checks eligibility and **registers the in-flight entry synchronously** (waitDeadline = now + `wait_timeout_ms`, falling back to legacy `timeout_ms` or 60000) before returning. An eligible session whose catalog lacks `session_record_tool` (a session-type `tools` allowlist or `disabled_tools`; under dynamic loading the registry's catalog, otherwise `agent.state.tools`) registers nothing and logs `session_record_skipped {reason: "tool_unavailable"}`.
3. **The timeline slot is released**: `drainNextQueuedTrigger` (fresh launch and reply-resume; their `.finally` drains only on the error path) or the manual resume's idempotent `releaseSlot()` (its `finally` call is then a no-op). Because step 2 came first, a queued trigger launched by this release that replies to the session already sees the entry and waits.
4. The run awaits the turn (so `activeRuns` keeps it inside the shutdown drain); the capture handle stays attached and is detached in the run's `.finally`.

**Eligibility** (`isEligibleForRecord`): `[session_records].enabled` not false; not a synthetic worker type (`summarize`/`condense`/`diary`); session type `default` or the proactive type (`proactiveSessionTypeName()`, default `"proactive"`); and the work gate (`hasResumableWork`, scope `any_in_history`; only the model's own calls, never a harness-made injection) over the agent's messages with the exempt set of the session's own context (`workGateExemptToolNames(inbound)` = the built-in exempt set ∪ `[agent.sessions.resume.work_gate.<dm|group>].extra_exempt_tools`, the same helper `tryReplyResume` uses). Pure conversation writes nothing, including a reply whose only tool call is an injected record; a session that ended in `NO_REPLY` after tool work writes one.

**The turn** (`SessionRecordService.run`):
- Refused when the service is shutting down (`session_record_failed {reason:"shutdown"}`).
- **No refusal fallover**: `CreatedAgent.setRefusalFallover(false)` for the turn (restored in its `finally`), so with no matching rule a refusal ends the turn at once on the member that refused instead of moving down the chain (§8a "Refusals"); a refused record turn writes no record. The turn runs at refusal site **`record_turn`** (`CreatedAgent.setRefusalSite`, reset in the `finally`), so a `[[refusal_fallback]]` rule naming that site (or no sites) redoes it on the rule's model, and a session pinned by an earlier redo writes its record on the pin (§8j).
- **Priority**: `CreatedAgent.setPriority("interactive")`. The factory passes `admission.priority` as a function reading the agent's current class, and the scheduler reads it on every acquire, so the turn's requests are admitted at interactive priority whatever the session type's class: it extends the interactive rollout that just finished, must land while its cache is warm, and triggers may be waiting on it. The Layer-0 retry budget keeps the session type's own class (§8 "Layer-0 request retry").
- A steer or follow-up message still queued on the agent is cleared (`clearAllQueues`, `session_record_queue_cleared`): the session is over. No timeline message is lost there: the app tracks every timeline-originated steer (follow-up, reply-steer, co-reply) per session (`trackSteer`), and when the session settles `completed` (`SessionManager.onSettle` now passes the final status) each one whose message object is not in `agent.state.messages` revives that session, once (`steer_unread_redelivered {sessionId, eventId, timelineKey, form}`, §8 "Late input"), or takes its native fate when the session cannot be revived (`steer-unread`). A reply steered on the trigger hold's immediate (trigger-less) emission is left to its trigger-bearing twin: when the twin arrived while the session was still live (suppressed) the entry takes the twin's inbound and is redelivered; when it arrives after the settle, it is consumed if the session read the reply (whatever the final status, the same outcome as a twin that arrived while the session was live: `reply_twin_consumed`, bounded FIFO of such event ids) and otherwise takes the native path. Non-timeline steers (cost-budget warning, `delegate_to_session`) are not tracked; other terminal states keep their fates (an operator interrupt drops the queue on purpose). Nothing is redelivered while draining.
- **Prompt**: one user message `RECORD_TURN_PROMPT` with `harness: { kind: "record_turn" }`. It states the purpose (a later session sees only the chat and this record), what is needed per kind of work (a lookup: the sources behind what was said, including things only mentioned in passing, and what was found but not used; something made or changed: the artifacts with paths and message ids, their state, how to continue or check them; anything left open), asks to tie each part to the message it belongs to by message id, and to keep it a handoff note (what and where, a one-line why). It never asks for reasoning. It ends: write it with `session_record_tool`, then finalize; no other tool is available.
- **Loading the tool** (dynamic loading only, when the record tool is in the catalog and not yet loaded): the prompt is followed by a synthetic **`tool_search {query: "select:session_record_tool"}`** call whose result is **supplied** by the harness (`buildSyntheticCallFromResult`; `tool_search` itself refuses harness-only tools): the same text a real load returns (`formatLoadedTools`) and `addedToolNames: ["session_record_tool"]`. Building it loads the registry, whose `onChange` sets `agent.state.tools` before the prompt. Both messages carry `harness: { kind: "record_load" }` and the current model's api/provider/id (`agent.state.model`). The load point is a strict suffix of the last request, so the whole rollout is read from cache, and each transport serializes the load at its native load point keyed on `addedToolNames` (`tool_reference`, `tool_search_output`, or the text load point); the call names `tool_search`, so the record tool is never called before its load point. A resumed rollout that already loaded it gets no load call; without dynamic loading there is none.
- **The draft starts empty**: `handles.draft.reset()` before the first kickoff. The handles are created once per launch and every run of the session reuses them (a revival, §8 "Late input"), so without the reset a revived run's turn would find the forked-away turn's draft (`create` refuses an existing draft) and finalize the stale record.
- `agent.prompt(kickoff)` + `waitForIdle()` with `gate.active = true` (reset in `finally`). There is no record-specific execution timeout: requests use normal LLM request handling and session/user cost limits. `max_turns` (counted `turn_end` events, default 4) and `shutdown()` can still call `agent.abort()`: an unfinalized turn is aborted at `max_turns`; a finalized one whose loop goes on (a finalize batched with another call does not end pi's loop, which terminates only when every call of the batch does) is aborted one turn later and its finalized draft is still judged (the pre-write judge, §8j) and written. A revival or shutdown that lands after the cap still stops the write. It runs on the bare agent, not through `SessionRunner`: no forced completion, no typing.
- **Finalized** = a `tool_execution_end` for `session_record_tool` that did not error and returned `terminate: true`. A draft never finalized is abandoned.
- **Judged before it is written** (only when a soft refusal rule could match the session, §8j): the finalized text goes through the background `artifact` check (`StartRecordTurnParams.judgeRecord`); a revival or shutdown that landed while the judge ran ends the turn (no rerun, no write); a judged refusal discards the turn (`discardTurn`: a fork at the turn's start, `reason: "refusal_redo"`), resets the draft and runs the turn again with a rebuilt kickoff on the rule's next entry while the site stays `record_turn` (log `session_record_refusal_redo`); exhaustion writes nothing (`session_record_failed {reason: "refusal", soft: true}`). Otherwise the record is judged after it is written, observe-only (`onRecordWritten` → `gate.judgeArtifact`).

**Outcome.** Aborted for a revival → `session_record_failed {reason: "revival", turns}`, even when the turn already finalized (the revived run writes the record at its new end). Aborted and not finalized → `session_record_failed {reason: "max_turns" | "shutdown", turns}`. Not finalized otherwise → `classifyUnfinalizedRecordTurn(rawStopReason, error)`: `refusal` (Layer 0's `[llm-request:refusal]` class marker on the error, or `isRefusalSignal` over the last assistant message's raw stop reason and error; a refused turn makes one request and ends at once), `budget_blocked` (the factory's pre-flight `cost limit exceeded` / `budget exhausted` messages), `llm_error` (any other error), `not_finalized` (the model stopped without finalizing); logged with `turns`, `stopReason`, `error`. Finalized on an empty draft → `session_record_skipped {reason: "empty"}`. Finalized with text, not shutting down → `upsertSessionRecord` with `token_count` from the draft, `builds_on = buildsOnFromTranscript(agent.state.messages)`, `agent` = the timeline's agent, and `model_id` = the `model` of the turn's last non-harness assistant message (the chain member that actually served it, the wire id as in `agent_sessions.model_id`) → `session_record_written {sessionId, timelineKey, tokenCount, turns, modelId, buildsOn?}`. In every case no session state changes: the row stays `completed`. The turn's requests are ordinary requests of the session (`agent_loop` ledger rows, the session's payee, its cost ceiling).
