The report gives the share of builds with a labelled-relevant item anywhere in the recall set that could have been shown (the ceiling a ranker cannot beat), among the items the judge scored, and among the kept items; relevant items already in context through the recency layer or hidden by a filter are not reachable, so they are left out of the ceiling and reported as their own share (`excluded`, per build `relevantExcluded`), plus label counts per stage (`cut_late`, `cut_rerank`, `hidden`, `dropped`, `not_selected`, `budget`, `kept`, …) and per-build counts. Same guards and the same no-text output as the check modes.

**Memory filters** (`--point filter --filter <key>`, core `src/audit/filter-calibration.ts`). Calibrates one judged memory filter's `threshold` (§9c "Memory filters"). **Filter** (`calibrationFilters`): the agent's effective filters (the global table with `[agents.<name>.retrieval.filters]`, as live), with `--filter-file` merged over them (a side TOML holding `[retrieval.filters.<key>]` or a top-level `[<key>]`), so a filter can be calibrated before it is in the configuration; only a judged filter (with a `description`) is accepted. **Items** (`loadDiaryBlocks`): the agent's diary blocks from `memory_chunks` (NULL-agent rows in legacy mode), the unit the filters judge: per path in ordinal order, a chunk opening with a diary header starts a block and any other chunk continues it (sub-split windows are joined, overlap dropped), then each block is split by `splitFileBlocks` so its date, room and content hash are the live ones. Blocks outside the filter's time scope or missing its keyword/pattern pre-gate are never judged live: excluded and counted. **Sampling** (`sampleFilterBlocks`, seeded): two strata, every block matching the enrichment set (`--enrich-keywords`, case-insensitive substrings; `--enrich-patterns`, one regular expression per flag; both repeatable; `--enrich-max` caps the stratum) and `--sample` (default 150) of the rest. **Labels**: the live question's wording (`` `entry` matches: <description> ``, examples as criteria) through the forced `submit_label` tool, the generic reasons, one call per block. **Judge** (`createFilterJudge`): the memory point's filter question alone over the block as the filter service builds it (cleaned text, agent-timezone date, room), the memory point's timeout and state budget, raw probabilities; the chain head is `--member`, else `[retrieval.filters].model`, else the memory point's chain; only the head is called unless `--chain` (its fallbacks may then serve as live, and every chain member's endpoint is allowed). **Report**: per stratum and population-weighted (each usable row weighted by its stratum's population / usable rows) precision, recall and F1 per threshold; blocks hidden at each threshold (sampled per stratum and estimated for the population, weighted by population / scored rows); histograms per stratum; label, invalid and unscored counts; the best-F1 and lowest precision-target thresholds against the head's effective threshold (`[decisions.calibration.<member>] "memory.filter.<key>"`, else the filter's); labeller and judge usage and cost (tokens, billed attempts, answers per serving member). The text report has no per-item lines; `--json` adds ids (`block:<hash prefix>`), strata, labels and probabilities. Same guards and the same no-text output as the other modes.

---

## 10. Tools

Up to 50 tools are available to default sessions (the 41 original tools, plus `search_summaries` (summary keyword search, split out of `search_messages` — see §9e), plus the 5 cross-channel messaging tools behind the contacts/chat-history skills — see §10 Cross-channel messaging tools; plus `load_skill`/`tool_search` under dynamic tool loading, below; plus `read_session_record` and `read_session_transcript` under session records — see §8i; the `bash` tool exists only when the Docker sandbox is enabled — see §11a; `recall_memory` only when `[retrieval].enabled` — see §9d; `browser` only when `[browser].enabled` — see §11b; `image_generate` only when `[image_gen]` is configured — see below; `x_fetch` only when `[fxtwitter.tool].enabled` — see below; `x_search` only when `[x_search].enabled` (default true when the block exists) — see below; `find_source` only when `[saucenao].enabled` **and** a non-empty `api_key` is set (the default ships `enabled = true` but no key, so it soft-disables until a key is configured) — see below; `youtube_fetch` only when `[youtube].enabled` (default true) **and** the yt-dlp binary probe passed at startup — see §7e/below; `yotsuba` only when `[features].yotsuba = true` — see §7f/below; the chat-search tools `search_messages`/`search_summaries`/`expand_summary`/`recap`/`user_activity` are always present — see §9e). Default and proactive sessions also carry the harness-only `session_record_tool` (`harnessOnly: true`): in the catalog, never reachable by the agent's own loading, and executable only during the end-of-session record turn — see §8i. Session types may specify a `tools` allowlist to restrict which tools are provided (e.g. the summarization session types only expose `summary_tool`). Each tool is a factory function returning an `AgentTool` with TypeBox schema and async execute.

### Dynamic tool loading (spec DYNAMIC-TOOL-LOADING)

The code/schema default is off (`enabled` absent ⇒ byte-identical legacy behavior — the state every test and any config without the block gets), but the **shipped `00-defaults.toml` turns it ON** with a lean immediate core (send/react/emoji_list, read/search/expand_summary, web — native and exa names, file tools, memory) so a fresh deployment is token-frugal out of the box; every seeded template skill declares its `tools` (§4b), so the deferred remainder is skill-covered from first run. Deployments override the `immediate` list wholesale (config-merge arrays replace) or set `enabled = false` to restore everything-always-loaded. When enabled, a session's post-filter tool catalog is split by `AgentSessionFactory.create()` into an **immediate** set — config `immediate` patterns (exact names or trailing-`*` globs) ∪ the two loading tools ∪ `no_reply` and `read_session_record` when in the catalog (forced, since deployments replace `immediate` wholesale; §8i) ∪ any `always_loaded` skill's `tools` matches, minus every `harnessOnly` tool whatever matched it (§8i "Harness-only placement") — and a **deferred** remainder, withheld from `Context.tools` until loaded. Gate: the global switch AND the session type's stance (`tools_dynamic`, unset default = dynamic only for types WITHOUT an explicit `tools` allowlist — a hand-picked set is already the operator's chosen full set).

**Transport — pi-ai's `addedToolNames` contract.** The app implements no per-provider logic. A loading tool's `AgentToolResult` carries `addedToolNames`; pi-agent-core stamps it onto the transcript `ToolResultMessage`; each pi-ai driver serializes the load point in the most cache-friendly way its wire API allows (Anthropic `defer_loading`/`tool_reference` behind `supportsToolReferences`; OpenAI Responses `tool_search_call/output` items carrying the added definitions with `defer_loading: true` behind `supportsToolSearch` — **MikuSwarm defaults this ON** via `createModelFromConfig` (`compat.supports_tool_search`, default true; pi-ai's own default is off), because the `tools` array leads the Responses prompt-cache prefix and growing it re-bills the *entire* cached context at the cache-write price ($5/M on GPT-5.6) on every load event; Kimi in-transcript system tools message behind `deferredToolsMode`; plain openai-completions and the rest simply grow `params.tools` — a one-time prefix-cache re-write per load event, re-cached from the next request). A prefix re-write is never free on any provider: the whole context is re-billed at the uncached input (or cache-write) price instead of the cache-read price, so a native prefix-stable mechanism is used wherever the wire API has one, and `supports_tool_search = false` exists only for a Responses-compatible endpoint that rejects the `tool_search_*` item types. On the Messages API, `compat.supports_tool_references` passes straight through to pi-ai's `supportsToolReferences` (unset = pi-ai's per-model detection); `false` turns the `tool_reference` load point off for an endpoint or intermediary that rejects the block. pi-ai declares a loaded tool only from its load point on, so on this API every load still changes `tools` (a `defer_loading` entry appears). `compat.declare_deferred_tools` (`src/agent/declared-tools.ts`, default false) keeps `tools` fixed instead, the arrangement the Messages API expects for mid-conversation loading: the member's base StreamFn is wrapped so `tools` is the session's WHOLE catalog on every request, and an `onPayload` injector (gated on the serving member's descriptor) puts the wire array in catalog order and marks every tool outside the registry's `immediateNames` with `defer_loading: true`, so it is declared and callable while its definition stays out of the model's context. The array is byte-identical for the whole session, so a load re-writes nothing and never invalidates prefix-bound thinking. Under this option the load point is explicit, never auto-detected: with `supports_tool_references = true` it is pi-ai's `tool_reference` block in the loading tool's result; otherwise the result gets one extra text block rendering the definitions named in its `addedToolNames` (name, description, input schema), for an endpoint or intermediary that rejects the block. The text form depends on the endpoint letting the model call a declared tool that no reference surfaced. It is also used, in reference mode, for the one case pi-ai emits no reference: a tool the model called before loading it. Both forms are derived from the transcript and identical on every replay. The agent's own tool table is unchanged: a call to a tool that was never loaded still gets the `Tool <name> not found` result. One replay detail is handled in a pnpm patch on pi-ai (`patches/`): a bare deferred function (a `tool_search_output` tool not declared inside a `namespace` tool) lives in a namespace named after itself, and the API requires that namespace on the replayed `function_call` item. pi-ai replays the namespace it captured from the model's item; some Responses-compatible endpoints omit it there (while still rejecting a namespace-less replay with 400 "Missing namespace for function_call"), so the patch defaults the replayed namespace to the function's own name whenever the call is to a deferred tool in tool-search mode and no namespace was captured. Direct OpenAI is unaffected (a captured namespace always wins).

**Stale thinking** (`src/agent/stale-thinking.ts`, `compat.drop_stale_thinking`, default false). Some models sign each thinking block against the request prefix that produced it (system prompt, `tools`, every earlier message) and reject a request that replays the block after that prefix changed. A session's prefix is append-only (§2b) except in two places: a resume, which re-renders the system prompt, and a tool load on a member whose transport changes `tools`. For a member that sets the option, the member's base StreamFn is wrapped (`makeBase` in the factory, so the gate follows whichever chain member serves the attempt, like the `onPayload` injectors): turns belonging to the resumed transcript are sent without their thinking blocks, and so are assistant turns before the latest `addedToolNames` tool result unless the member keeps `tools` fixed (`declare_deferred_tools`). Turns produced after the change replay their thinking unchanged, and neither the live rollout nor the stored transcript is mutated.

**Registry** (`src/agent/dynamic-tools.ts`, `DynamicToolRegistry`): one per created agent, holding the result-budget-**wrapped** catalog (loaded tools get result shaping identically to immediate ones; the wrapper spreads results so `addedToolNames` survives). `initialState.tools` is the immediate set. Mid-run load events reach the current run via the `prepareNextTurnWithContext` hook (the loaded set only grows, so a length comparison detects change); the registry's `onChange` reasserts `agent.state.tools` for the next run's snapshot and charges the running-context counter (`ctxCounter`) with the added definitions' `renderToolBlock` estimate — per-member context fits see loads exactly like organic growth. The frozen build estimate uses the initial set only.

**The loaded set is derived from the transcript**: (immediate ∪ every `addedToolNames` on any tool result). Harness-made loads are ordinary tool results here: routing's skill preloads are synthetic `load_skill` pairs and the record turn's load is a synthetic `tool_search` pair (§8h "Routing", §8i), so a declared-deferred `tools` array is identical to an unrouted session's. (A routed row written before synthetic preloads may carry a `tools` array in `initial_preloads`; the resume branch loads it read-only before seeding, §8h.) Resume recomputes it via `seedFromTranscript` (silent — resumed usage actuals already cover accounting) rather than persisting parallel state — definitionally consistent with what pi-ai's `splitDeferredTools` derives from the same messages. A model calling a deferred tool it never loaded gets pi-agent-core's synthesized `Tool <name> not found` error result and the loop continues; the index plus the loaders make recovery one call away.

**Load triggers**:
- `load_skill` (`src/tools/load-skill.ts`) — THE sanctioned way to use a skill: returns the skill's full body and loads its frontmatter `tools` matches. LISTED skills only (an always_loaded skill's name errors with an "already active" note), and the tool exists only when the session's skill filter yields ≥1 listed skill. The skill index is the session-creation scan; the body + tools list are read live from disk at call time. Unknown skill ⇒ error listing valid names; re-load is idempotent. Logs `skill_loaded { sessionId, skill, tools }`.
- `tool_search` (`src/tools/tool-search.ts`) — universal fallback: `select:name_a,name_b` loads exact names; any other query keyword-matches deferred names (weight 3) and descriptions (weight 1), loading the top `max_results` (default 5). Results carry names + clamped descriptions only — full definitions travel via the provider tools channel.
- **Editor backstop** (`wrapEditorWithSkillActivation`): after a successful text-editor `view` of any `.md` file whose frontmatter carries a `tools` key, the same load path runs and the view result is stamped — keyed on CONTENT, not path, so a skill authored mid-session activates when the agent proofreads it. Best-effort: hook failures never break the view. Sandbox shell reads remain a residual backchannel (instructions only; tools stay unloaded — and nothing in context suggests that route, since skill paths are hidden, §9a).

**Discovery**: skill descriptions (the always-visible entry point) plus the `<deferred_tools>` index (`index` mode: `"orphans"` default — only tools no skill covers, empty ⇒ omitted; `"names"` — all deferred, grouped by owning skill, first-alphabetical wins ties; `"descriptions"` — plus ≤80-char clamps; `"none"`). Rendered by the factory into `workspace.dynamicTools` BEFORE either system-prompt render (the field rides the shared workspace object, so the factory's render and the ContextBuilder's stay byte-identical) — a pure function of catalog + skills scan, preserving the deterministic-rendering invariant. A skill whose patterns match nothing in the session catalog logs `skill_tools_unmatched` once per session (not an error — catalogs vary per agent/session type).

**Observability**: every load event (any trigger path) logs `tools_loaded { sessionId, source: "load_skill" | "tool_search" | "editor_view", names, tokenEstimate }` (the wire-token cost of the added definitions); `load_skill` additionally logs `skill_loaded`.

**Console**: `resolveToolDefs` (app.ts) returns the full post-filter catalog; the dynamic split is applied by its factory consumers via `splitDefsForDynamic` (the same gate as `create()`). `buildPreview` is exact — it has the workspace in hand, so the preview renders the dynamic prompt (`workspace.dynamicTools`), the always_loaded promotions, and the initial tool block a real session would send. The session-detail inspector (`toolBlockFor`) is a documented approximation: sync and workspace-independent, so always_loaded promotions are skipped and `load_skill` is assumed present.

### Tool-result shaping (spec TOOL-RESULT-BUDGET)

Every tool result — native and MCP alike — passes through a generic two-layer shaping pass before being returned to the agent runtime. The shaping is wired at `AgentSessionFactory.create()` (not `buildSessionTools`): `factory.create` is the only seam that has all three required ingredients simultaneously — the per-session `filteredTools` array, the running-context counter (`ctxCounter`), and the `onRequestCommitted` commit seam that resets the accumulator. The wrapper is applied after `filterTools()` and the wrapped array (`wrappedTools`) is passed into `new Agent(…)`. `buildSessionTools` lacks the per-session counter; `factory.create` is the correct and only natural home.

**Layer 1 — per-result cap** (`[agent.tools] result_max_tokens`, default 16384, 0 = disabled). A flat token ceiling per individual result: hygiene that keeps any single result from dominating even when plenty of context remains. When a result's text tokens exceed the cap, text blocks are shaped in order — whole blocks fit, the first overflowing block is sliced at a UTF-8-safe newline-preferring boundary, later text blocks are dropped — and a marker is appended:
`[tool result truncated: showing ~N of ~M tokens (per-result cap). Refine the call — narrower query, pagination, filters — to see more.]`

**Layer 2 — per-turn aggregate clamp** (`result_reserve_tokens`, default 32768; `result_min_tokens`, default 1024). One `TurnResultBudget` per session run; the accumulator resets at each `onRequestCommitted` (the Layer-0 commit seam). For each settled result: `allowance = max(servingWindow − runningContext − reserve − accumulated, minTokens)`. A result larger than its allowance is truncated to the allowance and carries a distinct marker: `[tool result truncated: showing ~N of ~M tokens — this turn's combined tool results exceeded the remaining context budget. Issue narrower calls, or work with what is shown.]`

**servingWindow binding** (spec TOOL-RESULT-BUDGET §4): `servingWindow` is the largest operative context window any serving member offers — not the head's planning ceiling. When per-user selection is active, the candidate set spans all preferred-model composites and `servingWindow = max(s.fallback.maxOperativeContextWindow for s in selectables)`; otherwise `servingWindow = fallback.maxOperativeContextWindow` (the single default composite's chain-max). This binding is computed after `userSelectionActive` is known in `factory.create`, after `selectables` is fully populated, so the result is always exact.

**Settlement order, not fair share.** Parallel results consume the turn budget in the order their `execute()` promises settle. The first to settle gets the largest allowance; a late result in an over-budget batch gets at most `result_min_tokens`. `result_min_tokens` guarantees every result keeps a useful head regardless of order; the floor may overshoot the budget by at most `(N−1) × result_min_tokens`, which the §8b context enforcement backstop absorbs.

**Exemptions and pass-throughs.** Tool *error* results are naturally exempt: `execute()` throws on error by contract; thrown errors propagate through the wrapper unchanged, so no shaping ever runs on an error path. Throwing is also the only way to produce an error tool result at all: pi-agent-core sets `isError` on the transcript `toolResult` only when `execute()` throws, and ignores an `isError` field on a returned result (the wrapper would shape such a result as an ordinary success). Every built-in tool follows the contract, including the background editors `summary_tool` and `diary_tool` (§9b/§9c), whose draft failures throw. Image blocks are exempt from text truncation (slicing base64 corrupts them) but are flat-charged against Layer 2 at `PER_IMAGE_TOKEN_ESTIMATE` (1600 tokens/image, the same constant the §8b running-context counter uses) — consistent with how the counter later charges the same image in the context window. Tools that already bound their own output (e.g. `bash` via `max_output_bytes`, the text editor's view budget) simply also pass through the generic layer, which is a no-op when the tool-specific bound is tighter.

**Concurrency.** Tool `execute()` calls may settle concurrently. Allowance computation and `consume()` are called synchronously after each `await` settle, with no further `await` between them, so concurrent settlements cannot interleave within that critical section (single-threaded JS microtask guarantee).

**Observability.** `tool_result_truncated` (info): `{ sessionId, tool, layer: "per-result"|"turn-budget", fromTokens, toTokens, turnAccumulated }`. Rate-limited to 20 events per session via a simple per-session counter (no existing codebase helper fit this use case). Cross-reference: §8b describes the context enforcement backstop that absorbs floor-overshoot; the MCP adapter (§11c) inherits this shaping layer automatically since every MCP tool returns an `AgentToolResult` through the same wrapper.

**Config summary** (all three ship as defaults in `config/00-defaults.toml`):
```toml
[agent.tools]
result_max_tokens     = 16384   # Layer 1 per-result cap (0 = off)
result_reserve_tokens = 32768   # Layer 2 reserved headroom
result_min_tokens     = 1024    # Layer 2 floor per result
```

### Output-gated tools and tool effect classes

**Gated tools** (§8j). The posting tools (`send_message`, `send_dm`, `send_to_channel`, `edit_message`, `create_poll`; checkpoint `send`) and `no_reply` (checkpoint `ending`) are wrapped by `wrapToolsWithOutputGate` when the session has a gate. The wrapper runs the tool's `gatePrecheck` first (`send_message`: `sendMessagePrecheck`, the reply-without-id check, the live claim guard and the empty-send check), then the gate, and a blocked call returns the gate's message as the tool error the agent sees. Tool definitions are untouched, except for the optional **`override_checks`** argument (an array of check codes to skip after a revise rejection), which is added only when an enabled `revise` check can fire at the tool's checkpoint for the session's agent (`no_reply`: only with judged checks on), and is stripped before the tool runs (§8j "The override argument"). A gated call that goes through and succeeds reports a delivery to the policy (`OutputGate.delivered`; a result whose first text starts with `error` is not one).

**Tool effect classes** (`src/tools/side-effects.ts`). Every tool is classified once: `toolEffect(name, args?)` → `redo_safe` | `repeatable` | `undoable` | `irreversible`, `isPostingTool(name)`, synchronous and cheap. `redo_safe`: no external effect. `repeatable`: no effect anyone else sees, but repeating the call costs money or time. `undoable`: visible, with a compensating call. `irreversible`: anything else. The fork core (§8j) never discards an effect that is not `redo_safe` (it does not compensate), and the refusal walks end at a delivered post. Posting: `send_message`, `send_dm`, `send_to_channel`, `edit_message`, `create_poll`. Redo-safe: the reads, searches and fetches (`read_messages`, `search_messages`, `search_summaries`, `expand_summary`, `recap`, `user_activity`, `member_info`, `channel_info`, `list_channels`, `list_members`, `list_reactions`, `emoji_list`, `recall_memory`, `search_memory`, `user_profile_read`, `character_card_read`, `read_session_record`, `read_session_transcript`, `search_files`, `read_image`, `web_fetch`, `web_search`, `exa_search`, `exa_search_advanced`, `exa_fetch`, `exa_research_list`, `exa_research_result`, `x_fetch`, `x_search`, `youtube_fetch`, `yotsuba`, `danbooru`, `find_source`, `media` (analysis only; it posts nothing), `load_skill`, `tool_search`, `no_reply`); paid reads stay here. Repeatable: `image_generate` (the file lands in the workspace; only a later send posts it) and `exa_research` (starting a paid job). Undoable: `react` (adding or removing a reaction) and `pins` with `action = "pin"`/`"unpin"`. Irreversible: the posting tools, `poll_vote` (no retraction path), `delete_message`, `write_memory`, `user_profile_edit`, `character_card_create`, `character_card_edit`, `set_profile`, `dm_optout`, `bash`, `exa_research_cancel`, `spawn_session`, `delegate_to_session`, the background draft tools (`summary_tool`, `diary_tool`, `session_record_tool`), and every unknown name. **Args-refined** (`ARGS_REFINED_TOOL_NAMES`): `pins` (`list` is redo-safe, `pin`/`unpin` undoable, anything else irreversible); `str_replace_based_edit_tool` (`command = "view"` is redo-safe, every other command irreversible); `browser` (the actions `navigate`, `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `console`, `tabs` and `open`, and the `act` kinds `hover`, `scroll`, `wait` and `back`, are redo-safe; `close`, `pdf` (a workspace write) and every other `act` kind, among them `click`, `type`, `press`, `fill`, `select`, `drag`, `upload`, `evaluate`, `dialog` and `clear_site_data`, are irreversible). A refined call whose args name no known action is irreversible. MCP tools take the class registered for them (`registerToolEffect`, §10 "MCP remote tools"); a registration never overrides a first-party name. **Compensation**: `compensationFor(name, args)` returns the inverse call through the same tool, or `undefined` when the call cannot be compensated (then it counts as irreversible): `react` is undone by the same `message_id`/`emoji` with `remove` flipped (each provider's removal takes away only the agent's own reaction: a Matrix redaction of its own reaction events with that key, a Discord own-reaction delete; providers without reactions do not register `react`), `pins` pin by unpin and unpin by pin. The inverse restores the prior state only when the call changed it (compensating a reaction the agent had already placed removes it). Registered MCP tools have no compensation. The lists are explicit (no prefix wildcards); `test/side-effects.test.ts` scans `src/tools/` and fails when a tool is in no class list or in two, or a listed name no longer exists, and it checks every `browser` action and `act` kind and every `str_replace_based_edit_tool` command against the tool source, so a new tool or action must be classified.

### Chat tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `send_message` | The only path for delivering messages to chat. Mandatory `is_reply` boolean controls reply semantics; `reply_to_id` required when replying. Optional `media` for file attachments. Optional `final` (default true) controls loop termination — when true, returns `terminate: true` to stop the agent loop. Shortcode resolution handled by native layer. Auto-chunks messages exceeding 4000 characters (fence-safe markdown splitting); chunking is skipped when custom HTML is provided (returns recoverable error if combined body+HTML exceeds 60 KB Matrix event budget). Voice messages supported via `as_voice` flag on audio uploads. |
| `delegate_to_session` | Route the current trigger into another running session. On success, current session terminates. On failure (target not running), returns error and session continues. |
| `spawn_session` | The inverse of `delegate_to_session` (duplicate-reply mitigation, §8): spin a coalesced co-reply (surfaced as an `<interjection reason="co-reply">`) off into its own session, identified by its `message_id`. The calling session does NOT terminate. A concurrency miss queues; a full queue / unknown id returns an error so the session handles it inline. |
| `react` | Add or remove an emoji reaction on a message. Accepts unicode emoji or `:shortcode:` — native layer resolves custom emoji from the usage catalog. |
| `emoji_list` | List available custom emoji shortcodes ranked by usage frequency (room-boosted, time-decayed). |
| `edit_message` | Edit a previously sent message. Only own messages can be edited. Native layer handles shortcode rendering in new text. |
| `delete_message` | Redact (delete) a message. Irreversible. Own messages freely; others require moderator power level. |
| `pins` | Pin, unpin, or list pinned messages. Action discriminator: `pin`, `unpin`, `list`. Pinning/unpinning requires room permissions. |
| `list_reactions` | List all reactions on a message with counts and user attribution. |
| `read_messages` | Read room message history (paginated with before/after tokens) or look up a single message by event ID (an edited message returns its stored post-edit body, §6 "Message edits"). For retrieving messages outside the current context window. Extended by cross-channel messaging: `room` param accepts a timeline key or a bare user ID (resolved to a DM via `findDmTimelineKeysForUser`); `anchor: "last_self"` centres the window on the bot's most recent message in that room (via `getLastAssistantEvent`). Visibility gates cross-channel reads: isolated rooms are refused unless the current session is already in them. Bot messages carry their session id in the sender tag (`Name [agent_session_id: s-…]`, §8i "Session ids in sight"). |
| `search_messages` | FTS5 + metadata search over chat history across rooms (§9e): text `query` (scope: body / +captions / all), filters (`from`, `mentions`, `quoted_user`, `is_reply`, `has_attachment`, `attachment_type`, `has_link`), time window (`after`/`before`/`last`/`since_user_absence`), keyset pagination, newest/oldest/relevance order. Each hit is the **full message** (`format`: compact default / snippet / rich) rendered via the shared context renderer + hydration, with an `event_id` reference; plus total + an `elapsedMs` latency trailer. Semantically-empty argument values (`""`, `[]`) are treated as omitted; summary-only filters draw a note naming `search_summaries`. |
| `search_summaries` | Keyword search over the rolling **summaries** (§9b) instead of the raw transcript (§9e) — the entry point to the drill-down ladder. Shares `query`/`rooms`/time-window/pagination/order semantics with `search_messages`, plus the summary-only `level`/`min_level`/`status`. Each hit renders a level/span/count header + snippet and cites a summary `id` for `expand_summary`. Message filters sent here are ignored with a note naming `search_messages`; empty-padded values are treated as omitted. |
| `expand_summary` | Drill a summary one or more tiers DOWN into the finer summaries — and ultimately the raw messages — it was condensed from (§9e/§9b). A level-1 `id` expands to its raw source messages (hydrated like `search_messages`); a higher-level `id` to the level-(N−1) summaries beneath it, each with its own `id` to drill again. `depth` (default 1, capped by config) auto-recurses; `include_messages` drills leaves to raw events; `token_cap` bounds the output and reports how many constituents were omitted. Unknown/superseded id → error. |
| `recap` | "What did I miss" — returns the finest existing **summaries** (§9b) for a window, from absence-gap detection (`since_user_absence`, default the asker) or an explicit `last`/`after`/`before`, coarsening to higher levels under a token budget (§9e). `rooms:"current"` default, `"all"` to span channels. O(1) inference; more detailed than the in-context summary layer. Each summary's `id` is cited in the visible body for follow-up. |
| `user_activity` | Per-room message **counts** + first/last-seen over a window (§9e). One `user`, or a roster ranked by activity. Each count is annotated with its **share of total**, the roster reports the **combined weight of the listed senders**, and the report states the **considered count + actual message span**, with a **coverage footnote** when the data spans less than the requested window. Restrict the counted set by **message type** — `has_attachment` (text-only vs attachments), `attachment_type:["image"…]`, `has_link`, `is_reply`. `order:"least_active"` + `max_messages` is the "who's gone quiet" view; `all_time` drops the 30d window; `include_silent` (or `least_active`) unions current room members so never-posted users show as total 0 (needs a concrete room scope, via the native `roomMembers` API; not combined with a type filter). Multi-room scans append each sender's top-3 channels. Counts, not bodies. |
| `member_info` | Query a room member's display name, avatar, membership state, and flags. |
| `channel_info` | Query room metadata: name, aliases, member count, DM/group type. |
| `set_profile` | Change the bot's display name and/or avatar. Accepts mxc:// URIs, HTTP URLs, or local file paths for avatar. Not room-scoped. |
| `create_poll` | Create a Matrix poll with question and 2-20 answer options. Supports max_selections. |
| `poll_vote` | Vote in an existing poll by selecting answer IDs. |

### Web tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `web_fetch` | Fetch a URL, return markdown text. Routes through the shared egress guard (§ below) with a 30s `AbortController` timeout (same default as the other direct guardedFetch callers), so a stalled or backed-off host can't block the live session indefinitely; non-OK responses cancel the body before erroring so the per-host limiter slot is freed. Max 200K chars. |
| `web_search` | DuckDuckGo HTML search. Returns title/URL/snippet results. |

#### Egress guard & SSRF protection

Every caller-supplied outbound fetch — `web_fetch`, `send_message` media downloads, `set_profile` avatars, `image_generate` references **and its generation POST**, the `danbooru` JSON API **and** asset downloads, the `find_source` SauceNAO search **and** its thumbnail fetches, `character_card` images, and all `FetchClient` asset downloads (media/danbooru/character-card) — routes through a single guard in `src/tools/ssrf.ts`. There is exactly one implementation; no tool open-codes its own URL check or redirect loop. This single chokepoint is also where per-host HTTP rate limiting lives (below).

- **`assertPublicHttpUrl(url)`** — always enforces http/https and rejects embedded credentials (input hygiene). When the guard is enabled it additionally resolves the host and rejects any private/loopback/link-local/metadata address (RFC1918, `127.0.0.0/8`, `169.254.0.0/16` — which subsumes the `169.254.169.254` cloud-metadata endpoint — CGNAT, multicast, IPv6 ULA/link-local/loopback, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 forms).
- **`guardedFetch(url, opts)`** — the one shared fetch primitive (supports `method`/`body`, so POSTs like image-gen's generation call route through it too). Layering on each call: **per-host admission slot** → SSRF address check → `fetch` → **record response status**. Guard ON: `redirect: "manual"` plus a re-run of `assertPublicHttpUrl` on **every** `Location` hop before following it (max 5 hops), so a public URL cannot 302 to a private/metadata host. The manual loop mirrors WHATWG fetch redirect semantics (what undici's native follow does): only the WHATWG redirect statuses {301, 302, 303, 307, 308} are followed — other 3xx (300, 304, 305, 306) are returned to the caller like any final response; on a **cross-origin** hop (scheme+host+port, compared hop-by-hop against the *previous* URL) it strips the credential headers undici strips — `authorization`, `proxy-authorization`, `cookie`, `host` — so a redirect from a credentialed endpoint (Danbooru Basic auth, image-gen's bearer key) cannot deliver the credential to a third-party host; and a 303 (or a 301/302 answering a POST) is followed as a bodyless GET with the body-describing `content-*` headers dropped — only 307/308 preserve method + body. A redirect with a missing `Location` header cancels the response body before erroring (no leaked socket). The per-host slot also follows the chain: when a hop lands on a **different host**, the previous host's slot is released and a slot on the hop host is acquired — gating on *that* host's backoff — before the hop is fetched, so a backed-off host is not reachable via redirects and concurrency is counted against the host actually being hit (exactly one slot held at any time; releases are idempotent, so abort/error mid-chain can't double-count). Guard OFF: a single native `redirect: "follow"` fetch with only the scheme/credential hygiene check (undici applies the same redirect semantics natively); the response status is recorded against the **final** URL (`response.url`), not the original one, so a redirect target's 429 backs off the host that actually throttled. On both paths the **final response's slot release is tied to body settlement**, not header arrival: the returned `Response` wraps the body in a stream that releases the slot on close/error/cancel (immediately when there is no body), so the per-host/global caps bound the whole streaming socket phase of a download, not just time-to-first-byte. Followed redirect responses still release eagerly at the host swap (their bodies are cancelled before the hop). Callers must consume or cancel every returned body — all in-repo callers do (the early-exit paths in web_fetch/send_message/set_profile/danbooru/image-gen cancel explicitly) — and as a backstop the slot is also released when the caller's `signal` aborts, so a body abandoned behind a timeout controller can't pin a slot. A caller's own `User-Agent` is preserved (the default `MikuAgent/1.0` is added only when absent, case-insensitively). The shared `FetchClient` always calls `guardedFetch` (carrying its proxy dispatcher), so neither the guard nor the limiter can be accidentally skipped by a tool. On top of `guardedFetch`, `FetchClient` adds a **bounded transient-retry** around each download: `guardedFetch`'s 429/503 backoff covers throttling *status codes*, but a connection-phase **throw** (`ECONNRESET`/`ECONNREFUSED`/connect-or-socket timeout/transient DNS `EAI_AGAIN`, or a bare undici `TypeError: fetch failed`) would otherwise fail the whole tool call on a single blip. Since each `doFetch` attempt streams to a fresh temp file and unlinks any partial output on failure, the client retries the whole attempt (`maxRetries` default 2, linear `retryBaseDelayMs` backoff default 250 ms) for those transient classes only — deterministic failures (size-cap overflow, SSRF/scheme rejection, the per-attempt timeout `AbortError`, a non-2xx status) are **not** retried — and on final give-up it replaces undici's opaque `fetch failed` with the underlying cause (e.g. `fetch failed (ECONNRESET)`) so the surfaced tool error is diagnosable. Every `FetchClient` consumer (media/danbooru/x_fetch/image-gen references/enrichment downloads) gets this for free.

##### Per-host HTTP limiting (`src/tools/http-limiter.ts`)

`guardedFetch` is also the single home for HTTP rate limiting (spec Design D). Unlike the LLM budget there is no scarce shared pool — each host is independent and most fetches hit arbitrary user-posted hosts — so this is deliberately **not** a scheduler: no priority, no groups, no queue ordering. Two protections, keyed **per host** and shared across all callers:

- **Per-host admission concurrency** (`default_max_in_flight_per_host`, default 8; optional `per_host_max_in_flight` overrides), plus an optional very-high cross-host **global ceiling** (`global_ceiling_max_in_flight`, default 256) as a pure degenerate backstop so a bot in hundreds of channels can't open unbounded sockets at once. This **replaces** the old single cross-domain cap of 6 (`enrichment.fetch_concurrency`, removed) — which neither bounded any one host (the thing that gets 429'd) nor needed to be that low. A slot is held from admission until the final response's **body settles** (see the `guardedFetch` bullet), so the caps bound concurrent sockets, not just request starts.
- **Unconditional 429/503 + `Retry-After` backoff** (always on, independent of config — the §5.3 invariant): one caller's throttle from a host extends a backoff window that **pauses all callers to that host** (honouring `Retry-After` when present — **clamped to `backoff_max_ms`**, mirroring the LLM scheduler, so a hostile `Retry-After: 999999999` can't blackhole a host for the process lifetime — else exponential + jitter between `backoff_base_ms`/`backoff_max_ms`). A non-throttle response resets the host's streak. Both protections hold per **hop** of a redirect chain (the guard-enabled loop swaps the slot when the host changes; the guard-disabled native follow records against the final URL — see the `guardedFetch` bullet above), so a backed-off host can't be reached, nor a throttle mis-attributed, via redirects.

Because hostnames are attacker-controlled (link previews fire on every URL the bot sees; wildcard DNS yields unlimited keys), the per-host state map uses **lossless eviction**: a state that has returned to the zero-information default (no active slots, no backoff in effect, no throttle streak — exactly what would be recreated on next contact) is deleted on release, on a non-throttle response, when an acquire aborts before granting, and by a time-gated full sweep (states can also decay to zero-information passively when a backoff window expires). Eviction never races an in-flight acquire: the acquire loop re-reads the state after every await, the grant is synchronous, and a state with an unreleased slot has `active > 0` so it is never evicted.

Config: `[rate_limits.http]`, applied at startup via `configureHttpLimiter`. `backoff_base_ms`/`backoff_max_ms` have schema `minimum: 1` **and** are floored at 1 ms in code — a 0 would compute a 0 window for every throttle, disabling the unconditional invariant via config (the same `minimum: 1` applies to the `[rate_limits.llm.*]` backoff knobs). The one deliberately rate-limited API we know by name — **Danbooru** — is NOT configured here; it owns an internal limiter in its tool (below), tuned to its documented limits and pacing its JSON-API + asset-CDN hosts as one budget, while still flowing through `guardedFetch` for SSRF safety and the unconditional backoff.

**This is defense-in-depth, not the boundary.** DNS is resolved but not pinned, so a resolve-then-connect race is theoretically bypassable; the authoritative control is the **network-layer egress firewall** (`docker/egress-rules.sh`, §11a/§11c) that drops private destinations at the bridge. The two layers are gated independently:

- **`[network] ssrf_guard`** (default `true`) toggles the app-layer guard. `app.ts` reads it once at startup and calls `setEgressGuardEnabled`. It defaults ON because a bare-metal `tsx` run has no other egress control. The Compose deployment flips it OFF in `docker/95-docker.toml` because the bridge firewall (`docker/agent-egress-rules.sh`) is the boundary there — avoiding the duplicate per-request DNS + redirect-revalidation overhead.

MCP server URLs are exempt (operator-configured infrastructure, not user input — see "No SSRF validation" under the MCP section).

### Browser tool

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `browser` | Drive a real, stealth browser (one persistent identity, shared cookies/logins) for interactive / JS-heavy / login-gated / bot-checked sites — the heavier counterpart to `web_fetch`. Only registered when `[browser].enabled` (§11b). Single tool with an `action` discriminator: `navigate` (http/https only; returns the page's AI snapshot), `snapshot` (accessibility tree with every interactive element tagged `[ref=eN]`, via `locator.ariaSnapshot({ mode: 'ai' })`, capped at `snapshot_max_chars`; descends into up to `snapshot_max_frames` iframes, appending each under a `[frame fN: url]` boundary with refs namespaced `fN:eN`), `act` (`click`/`type`/`press`/`hover`/`select`/`fill`/`scroll`/`wait`/`back`/`evaluate`/`drag`/`upload`/`clear_site_data`, targeting elements by `ref` through the `aria-ref=eN` selector engine — `click` takes `button`/`double`/`modifiers`, `type` takes `submit`, `wait` takes exactly one of `ms`/`wait_text`/`wait_text_gone`/`wait_selector`/`wait_url`/`wait_load_state`, `drag` takes `to_ref`, `upload` takes workspace-relative `paths`, `clear_site_data` wipes the current origin's cookies+storage, `dialog` arms a one-shot accept/dismiss + `prompt_text` for the next JS dialog), `screenshot` (inline image block, like `read_image`; whole page or a single element by `ref`, `png`/`jpeg`; bounded to the `media.image` pixel budget and the same per-model base64 image cap — downscaled via `sharp` to fit rather than rejected), `pdf` (save the current page to `browser-downloads/<session>/page-N.pdf` via CDP `Page.printToPDF` and return the path — write-only: the agent can't read it back, it forwards the path to the message tool), `console` (drain the page's buffered `console`/`pageerror` messages for self-diagnosis — the per-page ring buffer caps both the entry count and each entry's text length **at push time**, so a `console.log(hugeString)` can never park a multi-MB string in memory, and the drain renders at most a bounded total into agent context, appending a truncation marker when either bound is hit), and `open`/`close`/`tabs` (per-session tab management). Refs are snapshot-scoped: after a navigation or DOM change a stale `ref` fails to resolve and the tool returns a structured `ref_expired` error telling the model to re-snapshot. `evaluate` (arbitrary page JS) is gated behind `[browser].evaluate_enabled`. JS dialogs are auto-handled (`dialog_policy`) unless the agent arms a one-shot `act:dialog` override for the next one. Downloads are captured through the shared staging volume (`[browser].downloads_dir`/`downloads_local_dir` — both unset ⇒ downloads disabled; see §11b), finalized into `browser-downloads/<session>/` in the workspace, bounded by `media.download_size_limit` (over-cap transfers are canceled mid-flight), and surfaced as a path; a download that fails (canceled / over the cap / copy error) surfaces as an explicit `[download failed: <name> (<url>)]` marker rather than being silently lost. Errors carry distinct codes (`backend_unavailable`, `auth_failed`, `nav_timeout`, `act_timeout`, `ref_expired`, `bad_url`, `evaluate_disabled`, `evaluate_failed`, `screenshot_failed`, `upload_failed`, `clear_failed`, `pdf_failed`, …). |

### File tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `str_replace_based_edit_tool` | View/create/str_replace/insert on workspace files. Path sandboxed to workspace root (including symlink resolution). Declares `executionMode: "sequential"` so the agent runtime never runs two str_replace calls in parallel against the same file (parallel calls would race on read-modify-write and silently lose edits). Supports batch edits via `edits` array (multiple replacements in one call, applied sequentially with all-or-nothing semantics — a mismatch on any edit aborts the whole batch with no on-disk changes). Edits in a batch chain against the in-progress buffer: an earlier edit's `new_str` is visible to later edits' `old_str` matches, so swap-style transforms (A→B and B→A in the same file) will dup-match-error; the tool description documents this. Passing `edits` (even an empty array) together with `old_str`/`new_str` is rejected; an empty `edits: []` is rejected with a specific message; empty `old_str` is rejected up front (it would otherwise match the start of the file infinitely). On `str_replace` not-found mismatch, the error includes the original on-disk file contents for self-correction; if the on-disk file is CRLF but the supplied `old_str` is LF-only (the common shape after the model reads via `view`, which splits on `/\r?\n/`), the error appends a "(file uses CRLF line endings; include `\r\n` in old_str)" hint so the model can retry without a round trip. On dup-match mismatch, the error includes the in-progress buffer (after prior edits in the batch) and — for batch edits past the first — a hint that an earlier edit may have introduced the duplicate match. For files larger than 800 chars the snippet is replaced with a `[file is N chars; call view to inspect]` hint to avoid burning tokens on irrelevant prefixes. The `create` error for an existing file reports the workspace-relative path, consistent with every other tool message. View uses adaptive paging: when no `view_range` is specified, output is capped to a byte budget derived from the session's **operative context ceiling** (`min(context_window, session_type.max_context_tokens)`, resolved once via `resolveSessionContextCeiling` and passed as `contextWindowTokens`; `contextWindowTokens * 4 * 0.2`, capped at 512KB) — so a read is sized against the budget it will actually consume, not the raw physical window. The 50KB minimum-budget floor is only applied when the share is at least half of it — small-context models keep their narrower share so a single tool result cannot consume the whole window. When the cut lands mid-line, the visible body is sliced back to the last newline so it matches the advertised line range exactly. A continuation hint reports the last fully-visible line so the model can request the next page accurately; if the budget cannot fit a single complete line, a plain `[truncated]` marker is emitted instead. When an explicit `view_range` is truncated by `max_characters`, `details.endLine` reports the last visible line, not the requested end. If `view_range.start` is past the file's last line, view throws a specific error (`view_range.start (N) is past end of file (M lines)`) rather than silently returning an inconsistent empty range. |
| `search_files` | Ripgrep search within workspace. When the sandbox is enabled, `rg` runs inside the container (argv shell-quoted into `sh -lc`); otherwise it runs on the host via `execFile`. Both backends insert a `--` end-of-options separator before the pattern so a `-`-prefixed pattern (e.g. `-l`, `--files`) is searched literally instead of being parsed as a flag. Output parsing and `details` are identical across both backends; `details.truncated` reflects EITHER the `max_results` line cap OR the sandbox byte cap (the backend's `truncated` flag is OR'd in, with an `[output truncated]` marker appended to the text — mirroring the bash tool). |
| `read_image` | Read an image file from workspace and return it as an image content block (base64). Supports png, jpg/jpeg, gif, webp, svg — SVG is rasterized to PNG via `sharp` before being attached (providers reject `image/svg+xml`), and the rasterized PNG is downscaled if needed to fit the size cap. Rasters over the `media.image` pixel budget (`computeTargetDimensions` would shrink them) are resized and re-encoded through `conditionImageBufferForInference` (the same pipeline as trigger attachments) under the same base64 cap; rasters already within it ship byte-for-byte. The byte cap alone is not enough: a well-compressed JPEG can be several megapixels in under 1 MB, and some vision servers fail on inputs that large. Only registered when the **session's reply model** (the session-type model that serves the turn — not `[models.default]`, which may be a different, text-only model) is multimodal. Size cap is `Math.min(<reply model>.image_input_bytes, media.download_size_limit)`, measured as the **base64-encoded payload** (what providers actually meter), not raw file bytes — raw inflates ~4/3 via `4 * ceil(rawBytes / 3)`. Default is 5 MB base64 (≈ 3.75 MB raw), safely under Anthropic's per-image cap. `media.image.max_bytes` is deliberately excluded — that setting is the captioning pipeline's re-encode target (~1 MB) and capping `read_image` to it would reject any 1–3.75 MB workspace image. SVGs that embed a raster via `<image href="data:image/...">` are rejected before rasterization (same `containsEmbeddedRasterDataUri` gate the captioning pipeline uses); other SVGs are rasterized buffer-mode so librsvg cannot follow sibling-file references. Rejects directories and other non-regular files. Description directs the agent to save URLs to the workspace via the `media` tool rather than the (incorrect) `web_fetch`, which returns text/JSON, not bytes. |

### Shell tool

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `bash` | Run a shell command inside the Docker sandbox container (`/bin/sh -lc`). Only registered when `[sandbox].enabled` is true (§11a) — there is no host-side fallback, because running arbitrary shell in the harness process would escape the workspace. Schema: `command`, optional `cwd` (workspace-relative, `..`-escapes rejected), optional `timeout_ms` (1–600000). `executionMode: "sequential"`. `timeout_ms` self-limits the command **inside** the container (coreutils `timeout` wraps it; §11a) and the per-call `AbortSignal` (steer/cancel) kills the in-container process group **out-of-band** — neither relies on SIGTERM of the local `docker exec` client, which does not propagate into the container. Output is byte-capped (`max_output_bytes`), decoded on a complete UTF-8 boundary (no `�` at the cut), and formatted as an `exit: N` header plus stdout/stderr, with `[output truncated]` / `(timed out)` markers. (PTY, background, and host/elevated execution modes from the OpenClaw exec tool are intentionally not ported in v1.) |

### Media tool

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `media` | Analyze media (images, videos, audio) with a multimodal model. Accepts workspace paths or URLs (single via `media`, multiple via `media_items` up to 20). Auto-detects modality from MIME type, file extension, or file magic bytes (falls back to error if unrecognized). Optional `prompt` for targeted analysis, optional `start_time` (seconds) for video/audio to select the starting point of the processed segment. Routes to per-modality inference clients sharing the captioning model config. Each caption is billed as a §8c `tool_invocations` row (one per captioned item, `ref:"caption:<source>"`) and counts against the §8d per-session cost ceiling. When the session's **reply model** has native vision, the description notes that images in the prompt are already visible. **YouTube URL routing (§7e T3)**: when `YoutubeMediaContext` is present in the tool context (i.e. the yt-dlp binary probe passed at startup and `[youtube].enabled`), recognized YouTube video URLs are routed through `loadYouTubeMedia` (`src/tools/media.ts`) instead of `FetchClient` — `probe(videoId)` checks for live/upcoming (refused with a clear error), computes `startSec = start_time ?? urlT ?? 0` and `durationSec = media.video.max_duration_seconds`, downloads the segment via `download(videoId, { startSec, durationSec, maxHeight: media.video.max_resolution, maxBytes: [youtube].max_download_bytes })`, and caches the raw segment in the `MediaCache` at `yt_<videoId>_s<startSec>_d<durationSec>_r<maxRes>.mp4`. The downloaded segment is a pre-cut file starting at 0, so `start_time` is NOT forwarded to `processVideoForInference` (double-seek prevention); instead a `CaptionRequest.youtubeSegment` override carries `{ processedRange, totalDuration, truncated }` so `InferenceClient.caption` overrides the `processVideoForInference`-computed values and `formatTruncationWarning` emits the correct "47:12 … 5:00-7:00" form. When `truncated = false` (whole video fits), no warning is emitted. Subsystem unavailable or `[youtube].enabled = false` → YouTube URLs fall through to `FetchClient` (will fail on HTML, behavior unchanged). |

### Memory tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `search_memory` | Ripgrep over `memory/*.md` files — exact string/regex match (a URL, an exact phrase). Lines inside blocks hidden by memory filters are dropped (§9c). |
| `recall_memory` | Hybrid semantic+BM25 recall over `memory/*.md` (§9d) — natural-language `query`, ranked by relevance with temporal decay, optional `room`/`after`/`before` filters and `user` (only conversations that person took part in). Answers *"what do I remember about X"*; results carry a compact citation `[memory/<file>.md:<lines> · room]` and a match-centred excerpt (~600 characters) so the agent opens the full block with the editor/bash. Memory filters apply (§9c). Registered for chat sessions only; only present when `[retrieval].enabled`. |
| `write_memory` | View/str_replace/insert on today's daily memory file (`memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`). Auto-creates with header if absent. No `create` command — only the daily file pattern. Routed through the single-writer `MemoryFileWriter` (§9c) so chat edits serialize with the diary worker's appends. A successful mutation triggers a §9d reindex of the file. |

### Danbooru tool

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `danbooru` | Search Danbooru posts with structured query parameters, preview a post (returns image block), or download an asset to workspace. Supports `includeTags`/`excludeTags` for structured tag queries, `includeRatings`/`excludeRatings` for rating filters, `order` for 85+ sort modes (with optional `default_order` config fallback when `order` is omitted), `page` for cursor/numeric pagination, `extraTerms` for advanced Danbooru metatags (whitespace-rejected, count against `max_regular_tags`, cannot duplicate structured `rating:`/`order:`/`limit:` fields). The `max_regular_tags` budget mirrors Danbooru's per-account tag limit, which counts the auto-appended `order:*` metatag as a tag (an anonymous account 422s on `2 tags + order:*`) but exempts `rating:*` — so the budget counts `includeTags + excludeTags + extraTerms + (order ? 1 : 0)` and rating filters are free; a search exceeding it is rejected locally with a clear message rather than 422-ing at Danbooru. HTTP errors surface Danbooru's JSON `message`/`error` body (e.g. the tag-limit reason), not a bare status code. `preview` is **vision-aware** (keyed on the **session's reply model** — the serving session-type model, not `[models.default]`). When the reply model has vision, it runs fetched bytes through `conditionImageBufferForInference` so the inline base64 emission always lands under the reply model's `image_input_bytes` cap (measured as base64 bytes; the budget is converted to a raw-output target via `raw = floor(base64 * 3 / 4)` before being passed to the conditioning loop) — independent of the larger `downloadSizeLimit` hard fetch ceiling. When the model has **no** vision, `preview` must not emit an image block the model can't read (nor narrate one as if it could): it routes the fetched asset through the shared **image captioning client** (the same `InferenceClient` backing the `media` tool) and returns the caption text plus asset URLs and a pointer to the `media` tool for specific follow-up questions — the non-vision equivalent of handing the image to a model that can see. That caption is billed as a §8c `tool_invocations` row (`ref:"caption:<postId>"`) and counts against the §8d per-session cost ceiling. The non-vision default variant is `sample` (the 180px `preview` thumbnail captions poorly); the vision default stays `preview`. If captioning is unconfigured, it degrades to URLs only (no fetch). Tool/preview descriptions and the result text adapt to the vision flag. Result text across search/preview/download is terse (final query + per-post lines, or caption + URLs) — the prior step-by-step narration was dropped as wasted tokens; the structured query breakdown remains in the tool-call `details` for the console. `download` writes the raw fetched bytes to disk using `fs.open(path, "wx")` exclusive create (collision suffixes `-1`..`-100`, then a random nonce). Explicit `filename` extensions are allow-listed (jpg/jpeg/png/gif/webp/mp4/webm/zip/swf); anything else falls back to the post's `file_ext`. Auth via config-level `login`/`api_key` (Basic auth) — refused at tool-construction if `base_url` is plaintext `http://`. Both the JSON API fetches (30s `AbortController` timeout + 4 MiB response cap + identifying `User-Agent`) and the binary asset downloads (via `FetchClient`) route through the shared `guardedFetch` (SSRF + unconditional 429/503 backoff) and are paced by a **tool-owned `DanbooruRateLimiter`** spanning the API + CDN hosts as one account-level budget (`min_request_interval_ms`/`max_in_flight`, defaults 500 ms / 2 in flight) — the generic per-host limiter can't model that single-budget-across-two-hosts shape. The limiter is race-free under concurrency: each acquirer **reserves its start instant synchronously** (next free slot in the pacing schedule, so concurrent callers can't read the same stale "last start" and begin 0 ms apart), and slot admission is **FIFO with direct handoff** — `release` transfers the slot to the head waiter without decrementing the in-flight count, so a fresh caller can never double-grant a freed slot past `max_in_flight` or overtake queued waiters. Both paths honor `[network] http_proxy_url` via a shared undici `ProxyAgent` dispatcher when configured. Search results surface `createdAt`/`fileSize`/`source` per post (source is uploader-controlled, exposed as data only) plus the post's **`characters:`/`series:` tags** (the curated identity labels — the signal for picking the right result) ahead of the general descriptive tags; the search line's character list is capped (`+N more`) since it is a multi-post scan view. `preview` (both the vision image-block path and the non-vision caption path) returns the **full** "character first" tag block — character → copyright → artist → a capped slice of general → meta (the identity categories uncapped) — so the model has Danbooru's authoritative "who/what is in this image" labels without a second `media` round-trip; the per-category tags are also emitted under `details.tags`. Tags are uploader/community-controlled text, surfaced verbatim as data only (never fed to a fetcher), the same as `source`. **Tag suggestion ("did you mean")** closes the common failure where the model guesses a tag that doesn't exist (e.g. `mordred_pendragon_(fate)` when the real tag is `mordred_(fate)`): a `resolveTagSuggestions` engine resolves a free-text guess/keyword into real, ranked tag names by hitting Danbooru's `/autocomplete.json` (`search[type]=tag_query`, alias-aware) and, as a backstop, `/tags.json` (`name_matches=*token*&order=count`). It first autocompletes the whole normalized query; if that finds no exact tag it autocompletes each significant **word** (a guess like `mordred_pendragon` autocompletes to nothing as a whole because "pendragon" isn't in the real tag, but each word resolves on its own); if still empty it runs a substring wildcard. Candidates are deduped (deprecated tags dropped), then ranked by how many query words each contains (so `mordred_(fate)` beats a generic high-count `fate_(series)`) then by post count, capped at `max_suggestions` (default 6). The engine is exposed two ways, with the zero-result path as the primary one (it costs no extra tool call — the search the agent already ran surfaces the correction): a **zero-result `search`** (when `suggest_on_empty`, default true, and positive tags were given) auto-resolves each `includeTag` (capped at 4) and appends a "Did you mean?" block; and **`action: "tags"`** with a `query` param is a secondary, explicit lookup that resolves a guess into real tags without searching (for browsing/disambiguating candidates). Tool and skill guidance steer the agent to search-first rather than spend a round-trip looking a tag up speculatively. In the recovery block each tag is "valid" when it appears among its own suggestions (so a real tag is never "corrected"), and when *every* supplied tag is valid the output instead notes the empty result is a *combination*/filter problem, not a typo. The recovery's suggestion requests share the tool-owned `DanbooruRateLimiter` budget like every other call, and a failure in the (best-effort) suggestion path never turns a successful-but-empty search into a tool error. The structured recovery report is also surfaced under `details.suggestions` for the console. Config: `[danbooru]` section (`suggest_on_empty`, `max_suggestions`). |

### Find source tool

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `find_source` | Reverse-image search via **SauceNAO** (`src/tools/find-source.ts`; spec SAUCENAO-SOURCE-LOOKUP) — the **inverse** of `danbooru` (`danbooru` goes tags → images; this goes image → source URL + artist). Takes one `image` param: a workspace-relative path (resolved + traversal-rejected like `read_image`, then read and **conditioned** through `conditionImageBufferForInference` to `max_image_bytes` ≈ 4 MB) **or** an http(s) URL (scheme-validated, passed to SauceNAO as `url=` for server-side fetch — no local read). Calls `GET/POST {base_url}/search.php` via the shared `guardedFetch` (SSRF + per-host 429/503 backoff) with `api_key`, `output_type=2`, `db` (default 999 = all indexes), `numres`=`limit`, `minsim`=`min_similarity`; an upload rides a multipart `file` field (FormData → undici sets the boundary) while the rest stay query params, a URL is a plain GET. Honors `[network] http_proxy_url` via a shared undici dispatcher and bounds the call with a `timeout_ms` `AbortController` composed with the agent abort signal. **Account-quota rate limiting (§4-style):** a process-wide **`SauceNaoRateLimiter`** (`src/saucenao/rate-limiter.ts`, constructed once at app startup, injected into every session — the SauceNAO free quota is per-account/global, so a per-session limiter wouldn't bound it) enforces a sliding short window (`short_window_max`/`short_window_ms`, default ~6/30s); `acquire` waits up to `max_wait_ms` for a slot, else returns a **soft** "try again shortly" result (not an error) so the agent self-throttles instead of blocking the turn. After each response the limiter is **reconciled** from SauceNAO's authoritative `short_remaining` (and the daily `long_remaining` is surfaced, not enforced). Composes with — and is orthogonal to — the per-host HTTP limiter and the SSRF guard. **Status handling:** `header.status < 0` → tool error with SauceNAO's message; `> 0` → results returned with a "partial (some indexes unavailable)" note; HTTP 429 → soft rate-limited result with remaining counts. Results are normalized (tolerant — every field optional), dropped below `min_similarity` (default 55), sorted by perceptual-**similarity %** desc, capped to `limit` (≤ `max_results_limit`). **Output is verification-centric and vision-adaptive:** the text always leads each candidate with its **similarity %** (the identity signal — ≥ ~80% = same image, labelled strong/plausible/weak) plus source type (`index_name`), artist (`member_name`/`author_name`), title, source link(s) (`ext_urls`, http(s)-filtered), notable ids (`pixiv_id`/`danbooru_id`/…/`source`, surfaced verbatim as data only), and the matched thumbnail URL, with a quota header line. By deliberate design SauceNAO thumbnails are **never auto-captioned** (the divergence from danbooru's non-vision caption path): a generic caption of a thumbnail does not establish same-image identity — the similarity score does, far more reliably. On a **vision** model, `view: true` additionally inlines the top matched thumbnails (capped at `view_max_blocks`) as image blocks — fetched via `FetchClient`, conditioned to the same per-model `image_input_bytes` base64 cap as `read_image`, with a graceful fall-back to the URL on fetch/condition failure — so the model can *see* the candidate and confirm it matches the query image it can also see. On a **non-vision** model `view` is ignored with a note ("relying on similarity score"); the skill guides verification via the existing `media` tool on the source URL instead. **Ephemeral** — output lives in the session rollout only; nothing is persisted. Construction throws if `api_key` is missing (matches `image_generate`), but the app never reaches that path without a key: `[saucenao].enabled` is **default ON** for out-of-box capability, yet the tool is registered only when enabled **and** a non-empty `api_key` is present (the operative `sauceNaoConfig`/`sauceNaoEnabled` gate at app wiring). Enabled **without** a key is a **graceful soft-disable** — app wiring logs one `saucenao_disabled_no_api_key` warning and simply does not construct/register `find_source` (no crash, so a key-less public deploy starts cleanly). Config: `[saucenao]` (§4). Persona docs: TOOLS.md/AGENTS.md + the `saucenao` skill. |

### X fetch tool

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `x_fetch` | Fetch a tweet on demand via the FxTwitter API (§7a "X.com enrichment via FxTwitter") — the generic `web_fetch` is blocked by X server-side. The model's manual path for (a) reading tweets whose preview text was `[truncated]`, (b) tweets that never went through enrichment (e.g. URLs found elsewhere), and (c) **individual tweet media** — including the photos behind an enrichment mosaic. Accepts any recognized X/FxTwitter status URL or a bare numeric status id. Builds one canonical text document — header (author, handle, time, stats), **full** tweet text, poll/community-note blocks, a **numbered media listing** (index, kind, dimensions/duration, alt text, direct URL), then the quoted tweet in the same layout (indices continue across the quote) — bounded by `tool.max_total_chars` (default 32768) and returned as the `[offset, offset + max_chars)` window (`max_chars` default `tool.default_max_chars` 4000, hard cap `tool.max_chars_limit` 16000); `details` carries `{ totalChars, nextOffset, truncated }` and the window text ends with `[truncated — continue with offset=N]` when more remains. Media access escalates by listing index: `download_media` (indices or `"all"`) saves the originals (photos at full resolution, video/GIF mp4s) under `downloads/x/{statusId}/` via `FetchClient` (exclusive-create with collision suffixes), returning workspace-relative paths for `read_image`/`send_message`; `view_media` (indices or `"all"`, clamped to `tool.max_view_blocks` per call with a note) returns items inline as image blocks — photos directly, videos/GIFs as their thumbnail frame (a video cannot be an image block) — conditioned through `conditionImageBufferForInference` under the same per-model `image_input_bytes` base64 cap as `read_image`/danbooru `preview`. A fully **ephemeral** tool: output lives in the session rollout only — no enrichment rows, no captioning; downloads are ordinary workspace files. All fetches ride the shared `FxTwitterClient`/`FetchClient` (guardedFetch, proxy, `media.download_size_limit`). API errors (404/private/suspended) surface FxTwitter's message; out-of-range media indices error naming the valid range. Registered only when `[fxtwitter.tool].enabled` (independent of the enrichment enable). Config: `[fxtwitter.tool]` (§4); cross-field `default_max_chars <= max_chars_limit <= max_total_chars` validated fail-fast at app wiring. |

### YouTube fetch tool

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `youtube_fetch` | Fetch a YouTube video's metadata, chapters, and full timestamped transcript on demand (§7e T2), or download the video/audio as a workspace file (§7e T2 §6a). Accepts any recognized YouTube URL form or a bare 11-character video id. **Document mode** (default): `probe(videoId)` + `transcript(videoId, lang?, meta)` → one canonical text document — header (title, channel, upload date, duration, views), bounded description (`≤2000` chars), chapter list with `[M:SS]` / `[H:MM:SS]` timestamps, then the full folded transcript with `[M:SS]` markers — bounded at `[youtube.tool].max_total_chars` (default 32768) and returned as the `[offset, offset + max_chars)` window (`max_chars` default `tool.default_max_chars` 4000, hard cap `tool.max_chars_limit` 16000); `details` carries `{ videoId, url, totalChars, nextOffset, truncated, transcriptKind, transcriptLang }` and the window text ends with `[truncated — continue with offset=N]`. **t= anchor**: when the source URL carried a `t=`/`start=` timestamp and `offset` was not explicitly provided, the window auto-opens at the nearest `[M:SS]` marker in the transcript (`findNearestMarkerOffset`), so the agent lands at the moment the user pointed to. **No transcript**: metadata + chapters still returned, with a `Transcript: none available` line and the media hint. **Errors**: yt-dlp's bounded stderr is surfaced for unavailable/private/age-restricted/geo failures; live/upcoming content is refused with a clear message. Description and transcript are externally-sourced and wrapped in `<untrusted_youtube_fetch source="description|transcript" …>` envelopes (bodies XML-escaped via `escapeXml`; attrs via `escapeAttr`); structural output stays trusted. **Download mode** (`download: "video"|"audio"`): calls `download(videoId, { audioOnly?, maxHeight?, startSec?, durationSec?, maxBytes })` → saves one file under `downloads/youtube/{videoId}/{slug}[-<start>-<end>].{mp4|m4a}` (stat-based exclusive-create with collision suffixes). `max_height` is clamped to `[youtube.tool].download_max_height` (default 720) — never an error. `clip_start`/`clip_duration` map to `--download-sections`. On size-abort the error text suggests lowering `max_height`, using `download: "audio"`, or clipping. Returns metadata header + one workspace-relative path + byte count line. **Ephemeral**: no DB writes; downloads are ordinary workspace files. No LLM cost. Registered only when `[youtube].enabled` (default true) **and** the startup yt-dlp binary probe passed (`youtubeSubsystemAvailable`). Config: `[youtube.tool]` (§4); cross-field `default_max_chars <= max_chars_limit <= max_total_chars` validated fail-fast at app wiring. Persona docs: TOOLS.md. |

### Yotsuba tool

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `yotsuba` | 4chan (yotsuba) browser (`src/tools/yotsuba.ts`). Five actions: **`boards`** — list all boards with SFW flag, optional text filter; **`catalog`** — browse or search a board's catalog (AND-match query, sort orders: `bump`/`replies`/`files`/`created`/`last_reply`, `limit`/`after` pagination, thread excerpts); **`thread`** — read a thread in one of five views (`chronological`, `conversation`, `replies`, `most_replied`, `search`), with `after` paging, `max_tokens` override (capped to `[yotsuba.tool].page_tokens_max`), and `files: "none"` pass; **`view`** — fetch and display a post's file (image: inline conditioned image block via `conditionImageBufferForInference`; video/animated GIF: 2×2 storyboard via `buildStoryboard`; PDF: page-1 thumbnail + text extraction via `extractPdfText`; non-vision: captions through the session caption client billed as `tool_invocations`; unknown: metadata + media URL); **`download`** — save post files to `downloads/yotsuba/{board}/{threadNo}/{postNo}-{name}{ext}` via exclusive-create with collision suffixes (matching `x_fetch`). Naive input tolerance: a bare URL infers action/board/thread/post; `g`/`/g/`/`/g` board forms; `>>N`, `>>>/g/N`, bare integers all accepted for thread/post fields; empty/zero/`[]` treated as absent. All thread output wrapped in `<untrusted_4chan board="…" thread="…" view="…" as_of="…">…</untrusted_4chan>`. Footer carries literal next-call JSON for every omission kind present (next page, unshown posts, unshown files). Freshness: `as_of` timestamp + `cached Ns ago` when from cache. File images carry `block="N"` on the `<file>` element and a `[image N: >>postNo name.ext]` label before each block. All §7.5 errors are actionable (exact re-call with candidates). Registered only when `[features].yotsuba = true` and the `yotsubaSubsystem` is available. Config: `[yotsuba.tool]` (§4). Startup cross-field check: `page_tokens_max <= agent.tools.result_max_tokens`. Skill: `yotsuba`. |

### Image generation tool

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `image_generate` | Generate or edit an image with Google's Gemini "nano banana" models, via the Gemini API base (`GEMINI_BASE_URL`; an operator gateway may proxy it). One `prompt` generates from text; passing `images` (1–6 workspace paths or http(s) URLs) switches to **edit mode** — the same `:generateContent` endpoint, with each reference prepended as an `inlineData` part before the text instruction. `model` selects `pro` (`gemini-3-pro-image`, default — best quality + text rendering) or `flash` (`gemini-3.1-flash-image`, faster; also allows `image_size:"512"`). Optional `aspect_ratio` and `image_size` map to `generationConfig.imageConfig.{aspectRatio,imageSize}` (aspect honored on 3.x models, size loosely). The request **always sets a high `maxOutputTokens` (default 32768)** — Gemini emits the image *as output tokens* (~1290 for 1K), and many gateways default the cap low, so without this every call returns HTTP 200 with no image (`finishReason:"MAX_TOKENS"`). Auth is `Authorization: Bearer ${api_key}` (when an operator gateway fronts Google it injects real Google creds; Google's native `x-goog-api-key` is not used here). The decoded image is saved into `<workspace>/<output_subdir>/` (default `generated-images/`) via `fs.open(path,"wx")` exclusive create (collision suffixes `-1`..`-100`, then a random nonce); the tool returns the workspace-relative path plus an inline preview block conditioned via `conditionImageBufferForInference` to fit the per-image `image_input_bytes` cap. **Delivery is two-step**: the tool never posts to Matrix — the model must call `send_message` with `media` set to the returned path. Reference-image URLs route through `FetchClient`, which applies the shared egress guard (private/metadata block + per-hop redirect revalidation when enabled — see "Egress guard & SSRF protection" above), so a public URL can't 302 to a private/metadata host. Each reference (URL or workspace path) is bounded to a 6 MiB per-image budget: under-budget refs are sent as their original bytes + detected MIME untouched (preserving editing quality), and only over-budget refs are run through `conditionImageBufferForInference` (resize + JPEG) to cap tokens/memory. The generation POST itself also routes through `guardedFetch` (per-host backoff + SSRF), and honors `[network] http_proxy_url`. Output MIME is whatever the response's image part declares (`inlineData.mimeType`, falling back to `image/png`); the on-disk extension is derived from that MIME, constrained to a vetted allow-list (`png`/`jpg`/`webp`/`gif`, default `png`). All outputs carry a SynthID watermark. **Per-agent model overrides (spec PER-AGENT-MODEL-OVERRIDES):** the `pro`/`flash` chains are resolved at session-tool build through the per-agent ladder (`resolveImageGenRef`), so each session uses its agent's override if configured, else the global `image_gen.models.{pro,flash}`. Not registered unless `[image_gen]` is configured. Config: `[image_gen]` section. Persona docs: TOOLS.md + the `image-gen` skill. |
| `x_search` | Search X.com (Twitter) via **Grok as a discovery sub-agent** (`src/tools/x-search.ts`). One **streamed** OpenRouter chat-completions POST (`{base_url}/chat/completions` with `stream: true` + `stream_options.include_usage`, reusing `OPENROUTER_BASE_URL` + `LLM_API_KEY` — no new credential/egress host; the SSE deltas are reassembled into the non-streamed shape, usage read from the final chunk, an in-stream `error` object fails the call, and a plain-JSON answer from a gateway that ignores `stream` is accepted too) sends a fixed system scaffold (force a live cited search; never fabricate) + the agent's `query`, with `plugins:[{id:"web"}]` (Grok's `x_search` **and** auxiliary `web_search` server-side tools) and a top-level `x_search_filter` carrying `allowed_x_handles` **xor** `excluded_x_handles` (max 10 each, validated), `from_date`/`to_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), and the **corpus-vision** flags `enable_image_understanding` / `enable_video_understanding` (both **config-only, default on** — they let Grok analyze images/video it encounters *during* the search; deliberately **not** model-facing knobs). `effort` (`fast`→`model`, `deep`→`deep_model`) picks the Grok tier.
